title.zh-Hans: 西拿基立的拉吉战役浮雕
title.zh-Hant: 西拿基立的拉吉战役浮雕

summary.en: These monumental Assyrian reliefs depict the brutal siege and capture of Lachish by King Sennacherib in 701 BCE, vividly illustrating a key event described in the Hebrew Bible. They offer a unique visual narrative of ancient warfare and its devastating consequences.
summary.zh-Hans: 这些宏伟的亚述浮雕描绘了公元前701年西拿基立王对拉吉的残酷围攻和攻占，生动地展现了希伯来圣经中描述的一个关键事件。它们提供了古代战争及其毁灭性后果的独特视觉叙事。
summary.zh-Hant: 这些宏伟的亚述浮雕描绘了公元前701年西拿基立王对拉吉的残酷围攻和攻占，生动地展现了希伯来圣经中描述的一个关键事件。它们提供了古代战争及其毁灭性后果的独特视觉叙事。

description.en:
Discovered by Austen Henry Layard in 1847 during his excavations of Sennacherib's palace at Nineveh (modern-day Iraq), these impressive stone reliefs adorned the walls of Room XXXVI. They form a continuous narrative, stretching over 20 meters, detailing the Assyrian campaign against the Judean city of Lachish.

The reliefs meticulously portray every stage of the siege: the Assyrian army's advance, the construction of a massive siege ramp, battering rams breaching the city walls, archers and slingers in action, and Judean defenders desperately resisting. The aftermath is also depicted, showing the impalement of captives, the deportation of the populace, and Sennacherib himself receiving tribute and overseeing the spoils.

Dating to around 700-690 BCE, the Lachish reliefs are an unparalleled historical document. They provide a detailed, contemporary, and non-biblical account of a specific event mentioned in the Bible, offering a rare glimpse into the realities of ancient warfare and the fate of a major Judean city during the Assyrian invasion.
description.zh-Hans:
这些令人印象深刻的石刻浮雕是奥斯汀·亨利·莱亚德（Austen Henry Layard）于1847年在尼尼微（今伊拉克）西拿基立宫殿的挖掘中发现的，它们装饰着第36号房间的墙壁。这些浮雕形成了绵延20多米的连续叙事，详细描绘了亚述对犹大城市拉吉的战役。

浮雕细致地描绘了围城战的每个阶段：亚述军队的推进、巨大攻城坡道的建造、攻城槌突破城墙、弓箭手和投石手投入战斗，以及犹大守军的拼死抵抗。战后景象也得以描绘，展示了俘虏被刺穿、民众被驱逐，以及西拿基立本人接受贡品并监督战利品。

拉吉浮雕追溯到公元前700-690年左右，是一份无与伦比的历史文献。它提供了圣经中提及的特定事件的详细、同期且非圣经记载，罕见地揭示了古代战争的现实以及亚述入侵期间一个主要犹大城市的命运。

scripturalCorrelation.en:
The Assyrian invasion of Judah under King Sennacherib in 701 BCE is extensively documented in the books of 2 Kings and Isaiah. The Bible describes Sennacherib's campaign against the fortified cities of Judah, including Lachish, before his ultimate, unsuccessful attempt to capture Jerusalem.

2 Kings 18:14 states, 'So Hezekiah king of Judah sent this message to the king of Assyria at Lachish: 'I have done wrong. Withdraw from me, and I will pay whatever you demand.' The king of Assyria exacted from Hezekiah king of Judah three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold.' The Lachish reliefs visually corroborate the biblical account of Sennacherib's presence at Lachish and the devastating impact of his campaign on Judah, providing a powerful external witness to the historical accuracy of these biblical narratives.
scripturalCorrelation.zh-Hans:
公元前701年，亚述王西拿基立入侵犹大，在列王纪下和以赛亚书中都有详细记载。圣经描述了西拿基立在最终未能攻占耶路撒冷之前，对犹大设防城市（包括拉吉）的战役。

列王纪下18:14记载：“犹大王希西家差人往拉吉去见亚述王，说：‘我有罪了，求你离开我；凡你罚我的，我必承担。’于是亚述王罚犹大王希西家银子三百他连得，金子三十他连得。”拉吉浮雕从视觉上证实了圣经中关于西拿基立在拉吉的存在以及他的战役对犹大造成的毁灭性影响的记载，为这些圣经叙事的历史准确性提供了有力的外部证据。

title.zh-Hans: 亚哈的象牙宫
title.zh-Hant: 亚哈的象牙宫

summary.en: Thousands of carved ivory fragments, discovered in the Israelite capital of Samaria, are believed to be remnants of King Ahab's 'house of ivory' mentioned in the Bible. These luxurious decorations showcase Phoenician artistic influence and Israelite wealth.
summary.zh-Hans: 在以色列首都撒玛利亚发现的数千块雕刻象牙碎片，被认为是圣经中提及的亚哈王“象牙宫”的遗迹。这些奢华的装饰品展示了腓尼基的艺术影响和以色列的财富。
summary.zh-Hant: 在以色列首都撒玛利亚发现的数千块雕刻象牙碎片，被认为是圣经中提及的亚哈王“象牙宫”的遗迹。这些奢华的装饰品展示了腓尼基的艺术影响和以色列的财富。

description.en:
The Samaria Ivories were unearthed during excavations conducted by Harvard University between 1931 and 1935 at the site of ancient Samaria, the capital of the northern kingdom of Israel. The fragments were found primarily in the ruins of the royal palace complex, suggesting their original use as lavish decorations within the royal residence.

These thousands of ivory pieces, though often small and fragmented, represent a rich collection of artistic craftsmanship. They feature a variety of motifs, including Egyptianizing figures (sphinxes, lotus flowers), Syrian and Phoenician mythological creatures, and geometric patterns. Many were originally inlaid with gold, lapis lazuli, and other precious materials, indicating their immense value and the high status of their owners.

Dating primarily to the 9th-8th centuries BCE, the period of the Omride dynasty, the Samaria Ivories provide compelling archaeological evidence for the opulence and international connections of the Israelite monarchy. They reflect the wealth accumulated by kings like Ahab and the strong cultural and artistic influences from neighboring Phoenicia.
description.zh-Hans:
撒玛利亚象牙是在1931年至1935年间，哈佛大学在古代撒玛利亚（北方以色列王国的首都）遗址进行的挖掘中出土的。这些碎片主要在王宫建筑群的废墟中发现，表明它们最初是王室居所内的奢华装饰。

这数千块象牙碎片，尽管通常很小且残缺不全，却代表了丰富的艺术工艺品收藏。它们具有各种图案，包括埃及风格的人物（狮身人面像、莲花）、叙利亚和腓尼基神话生物，以及几何图案。许多最初镶嵌有黄金、青金石和其他珍贵材料，表明其巨大的价值和所有者的高贵地位。

撒玛利亚象牙主要追溯到公元前9-8世纪，即暗利王朝时期，为以色列君主制的奢华和国际联系提供了令人信服的考古证据。它们反映了亚哈等国王积累的财富以及来自邻近腓尼基的强大文化和艺术影响。

scripturalCorrelation.en:
The Bible describes King Ahab, who reigned in Israel during the 9th century BCE, as a powerful and wealthy monarch, known for his building projects and his controversial marriage to Jezebel of Sidon. One specific detail about his palace is mentioned in the book of 1 Kings.

1 Kings 22:39 states, 'As for the other events of Ahab’s reign, including all he did, and the ivory palace he built and all the cities he fortified, are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Israel?' The discovery of thousands of intricately carved ivory fragments in the ruins of Samaria's royal palace provides direct archaeological confirmation of the biblical reference to Ahab's 'ivory palace,' demonstrating the historical accuracy of this detail.
scripturalCorrelation.zh-Hans:
圣经描述了公元前9世纪统治以色列的亚哈王，他是一位强大而富有的君主，以其建筑工程以及与西顿的耶洗别的争议性婚姻而闻名。关于他宫殿的一个具体细节在列王纪上中有所提及。

列王纪上22:39记载：“亚哈其余的事，凡他所行的和所建的象牙宫，并他所筑的一切城邑，都写在以色列诸王记上。”在撒玛利亚王宫废墟中发现数千块精雕细琢的象牙碎片，直接考古证实了圣经中提及亚哈“象牙宫”的记载，展示了这一细节的历史准确性。

title.zh-Hans: 毕士大池的五道廊子
title.zh-Hant: 毕士大池的五道廊子

summary.en: Excavations near St. Anne's Church in Jerusalem have uncovered the remains of a large, multi-lobed pool complex with five porticoes, precisely matching the description of the Pool of Bethesda in the Gospel of John. This discovery confirms the pool's existence and layout.
summary.zh-Hans: 耶路撒冷圣安妮教堂附近的挖掘工作揭示了一个大型、多叶形水池复合体的遗迹，带有五道廊子，这与约翰福音中对毕士大池的描述精确吻合。这一发现证实了该池的存在和布局。
summary.zh-Hant: 耶路撒冷圣安妮教堂附近的挖掘工作揭示了一个大型、多叶形水池复合体的遗迹，带有五道廊子，这与约翰福音中对毕士大池的描述精确吻合。这一发现证实了该池的存在和布局。

description.en:
The Pool of Bethesda was first definitively identified through archaeological excavations beginning in the late 19th century, particularly beneath the crypt of St. Anne's Church in Jerusalem. Further extensive excavations in the 20th century, notably by the White Fathers, fully revealed the complex structure of the pool.

The archaeological findings revealed a large, rectangular pool divided into two basins by a central wall, with porticoes (covered walkways) surrounding all four sides and a fifth portico running along the dividing wall. This unique architectural feature perfectly matches the Gospel's description of a pool with 'five porticoes.' Remains of frescoes and mosaics, along with numerous votive offerings, suggest it was also a healing sanctuary.

Dating to the Roman period, the pool complex was in use during the time of Jesus. Its precise identification and the corroboration of its distinctive architectural features provide strong archaeological support for the topographical accuracy of the Gospel of John, affirming the historical setting of the miracle described.
description.zh-Hans:
毕士大池最初是在19世纪末开始的考古挖掘中被明确识别的，尤其是在耶路撒冷圣安妮教堂的地下室下方。20世纪进一步的广泛挖掘，特别是白衣神父会（White Fathers）的挖掘，完整揭示了该池的复杂结构。

考古发现揭示了一个巨大的矩形池，由一道中央墙壁分为两个水池，四周环绕着廊子（有顶的走廊），第五道廊子则沿着分隔墙延伸。这一独特的建筑特征与福音书中对“五道廊子”池的描述完美吻合。壁画和马赛克残迹，以及大量的还愿供品，表明它也是一个疗愈圣所。

该池复合体追溯到罗马时期，在耶稣时代正在使用。其精确的识别及其独特建筑特征的证实，为约翰福音的地理准确性提供了强有力的考古支持，肯定了所描述神迹的历史背景。

scripturalCorrelation.en:
The Gospel of John recounts one of Jesus' healing miracles at the Pool of Bethesda in Jerusalem, providing specific details about its location and structure.

John 5:2-9 describes: 'Now there is in Jerusalem near the Sheep Gate a pool, which in Aramaic is called Bethesda and which has five covered colonnades. Here a great number of disabled people used to lie—the blind, the lame, the paralyzed... When Jesus saw him lying there and learned that he had been in this condition for a long time, he asked him, 'Do you want to get well?'... Then Jesus said to him, 'Get up! Pick up your mat and walk.' At once the man was cured.' The archaeological discovery of a pool with exactly five porticoes near the Sheep Gate provides remarkable external confirmation of the Gospel's detailed description, lending credibility to the historical context of the narrative.
scripturalCorrelation.zh-Hans:
约翰福音记载了耶稣在耶路撒冷毕士大池行的一个医治神迹，提供了关于其位置和结构的具体细节。

约翰福音5:2-9描述：“在耶路撒冷，靠近羊门有一个池子，希伯来话叫作毕士大，旁边有五道廊子。里面躺着瞎眼的、瘸腿的、血气枯干的许多病人……耶稣看见他躺着，知道他病了许久，就问他说：‘你要痊愈吗？’……耶稣对他说：‘起来，拿你的褥子走吧！’那人立刻痊愈。”在羊门附近发现一个恰好有五道廊子的池子，为福音书的详细描述提供了显著的外部证实，增加了叙事历史背景的可信度。

title.zh-Hans: 公元一世纪抹大拉会堂
title.zh-Hant: 公元一世纪抹大拉会堂

summary.en: Discovered in 2009, this well-preserved synagogue from the first century CE in Magdala (Tarichaea) is one of the oldest known synagogues in Galilee. It provides direct evidence of Jewish life and worship during Jesus' time.
summary.zh-Hans: 这座保存完好的公元一世纪会堂于2009年在抹大拉（他利迦）被发现，是加利利地区已知最古老的会堂之一。它为耶稣时代的犹太人生活和敬拜提供了直接证据。
summary.zh-Hant: 这座保存完好的公元一世纪会堂于2009年在抹大拉（他利迦）被发现，是加利利地区已知最古老的会堂之一。它为耶稣时代的犹太人生活和敬拜提供了直接证据。

description.en:
The Magdala Synagogue was unearthed in 2009 during salvage excavations conducted by the Israel Antiquities Authority prior to the construction of a new hotel complex at Migdal (ancient Magdala), on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee. The synagogue was found remarkably well-preserved, with its original stone benches and mosaic floor largely intact.

The synagogue complex consists of a main hall with stone benches lining the walls, designed to accommodate a congregation. Inside, archaeologists discovered the 'Magdala Stone,' a unique carved stone table depicting a seven-branched menorah, believed to have served as a platform for reading the Torah. Frescoes adorned the walls, and the floor was paved with mosaics.

Dating to the first century CE, the Magdala Synagogue is one of only a handful of synagogues definitively dated to the time of Jesus found in Galilee. Its discovery provides invaluable insights into the architecture, rituals, and community life of Jews in the region during the Second Temple period, offering a tangible link to the world in which Jesus lived and taught.
description.zh-Hans:
抹大拉会堂是2009年以色列文物管理局在加利利海西岸的米格达尔（古抹大拉）修建新酒店综合体之前的抢救性挖掘中出土的。会堂保存得异常完好，其原始的石凳和马赛克地板基本完整。

会堂建筑群由一个主厅组成，墙壁两侧设有石凳，旨在容纳会众。在内部，考古学家发现了“抹大拉石”，这是一块独特的雕刻石桌，上面描绘着七枝烛台，据信曾用作诵读妥拉的平台。墙壁上装饰着壁画，地板铺设着马赛克。

抹大拉会堂追溯到公元一世纪，是加利利地区少数几个明确可追溯到耶稣时代的会堂之一。它的发现对第二圣殿时期该地区犹太人的建筑、仪式和社区生活提供了宝贵的见解，与耶稣生活和教导的世界建立了实实在在的联系。

scripturalCorrelation.en:
The Gospels frequently depict Jesus traveling and teaching in the region of Galilee, often entering synagogues to preach and heal. Magdala, a prominent fishing town on the Sea of Galilee, would have been a significant center for Jewish life.

Matthew 4:23 states, 'Jesus went throughout Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, proclaiming the good news of the kingdom, and healing every disease and sickness among the people.' The discovery of a first-century synagogue in Magdala provides a concrete example of the very type of place where Jesus would have taught and ministered, offering a powerful archaeological backdrop that confirms the historical setting of his Galilean ministry.
scripturalCorrelation.zh-Hans:
福音书经常描绘耶稣在加利利地区旅行和教导，常常进入会堂讲道和医治。抹大拉是加利利海边一个著名的渔镇，本应是犹太人生活的重要中心。

马太福音4:23记载：“耶稣走遍加利利，在各会堂里教训人，传天国的福音，医治百姓各样的病症。”在抹大拉发现一个公元一世纪的会堂，提供了耶稣可能教导和事奉的这类地方的具体例证，为他加利利事奉的历史背景提供了有力的考古学支持。

title.zh-Hans: 以色列最早的提及
title.zh-Hant: 以色列最早的提及

summary.en: This ancient Egyptian stele, dating to approximately 1208 BCE, contains the earliest known extra-biblical reference to 'Israel' as a people group. It provides crucial evidence for Israel's presence in Canaan during the late Bronze Age.
summary.zh-Hans: 这块约公元前1208年的古埃及石碑，包含已知最早的圣经之外提及“以色列”作为一个民族群体的记载。它为以色列在青铜时代晚期迦南的存在提供了关键证据。
summary.zh-Hant: 这块约公元前1208年的古埃及石碑，包含已知最早的圣经之外提及“以色列”作为一个民族群体的记载。它为以色列在青铜时代晚期迦南的存在提供了关键证据。

description.en:
The Merenptah Stele, also known as the Israel Stele, was discovered in 1896 by Flinders Petrie in the funerary temple of Pharaoh Merenptah (son of Ramesses II) at Thebes, Egypt. Carved from a large slab of granite, the stele primarily commemorates Merenptah's victory over the Libyans and their Sea Peoples allies.

The stele's significance for biblical archaeology lies in its concluding lines, which detail a campaign in Canaan. Among a list of conquered cities and peoples, the inscription states: 'Canaan is plundered with every evil; Ashkelon is carried off; Gezer is seized; Yano'am is made as that which does not exist; Israel is laid waste, its seed is not.' The hieroglyph for 'Israel' uses a determinative indicating a people group, not a city-state.

Dating to the 5th year of Merenptah's reign, approximately 1208 BCE, the stele provides the earliest known non-biblical reference to 'Israel.' This places a distinct entity named 'Israel' in Canaan during the late Bronze Age, consistent with the period of the Judges or early settlement described in the Bible, long before the establishment of the united monarchy.
description.zh-Hans:
麦伦普塔石碑，又称以色列石碑，是弗林德斯·皮特里（Flinders Petrie）于1896年在埃及底比斯法老麦伦普塔（拉美西斯二世之子）的陵庙中发现的。石碑由一块巨大的花岗岩板雕刻而成，主要纪念麦伦普塔战胜利比亚人及其海上民族盟友。

石碑对圣经考古学的重要性在于其结尾几行，详细描述了在迦南的一次战役。在被征服的城市和民族名单中，铭文写道：“迦南被掠夺，一切邪恶；亚实基伦被带走；基色被夺取；亚挪安不复存在；以色列被荒废，其种子不存。”“以色列”的象形文字使用了一个表示民族群体的限定词，而非城邦。

石碑追溯到麦伦普塔统治的第五年，约公元前1208年，提供了已知最早的非圣经提及“以色列”的文献。这表明一个名为“以色列”的独特实体在青铜时代晚期存在于迦南，这与圣经中描述的士师时代或早期定居时期相符，远早于联合王国的建立。

scripturalCorrelation.en:
While the Merenptah Stele does not directly mention events like the Exodus or the conquest of Canaan, it provides crucial external evidence for the existence of 'Israel' as a distinct people group in the land of Canaan during a period consistent with the biblical narrative of their settlement.

Exodus 1:1 begins the biblical account of the Israelites' origins, stating, 'These are the names of the sons of Israel who went to Egypt with Jacob—each with his family.' The stele, though much later, confirms that by the late 13th century BCE, a people identified as 'Israel' were present in Canaan, offering a significant archaeological anchor for the early historical claims of the biblical text regarding Israel's presence in the land.
scripturalCorrelation.zh-Hans:
尽管麦伦普塔石碑没有直接提及出埃及或征服迦南等事件，但它为“以色列”作为一个独特的民族群体在迦南地存在提供了重要的外部证据，其时期与圣经中关于他们定居的叙事相符。

出埃及记1:1开始记载以色列人的起源：“以色列的儿子们，和他们的家眷，一同下埃及去的，名字记在下面。”尽管石碑年代较晚，但它证实了到公元前13世纪末，一个被认定为“以色列”的民族存在于迦南，为圣经文本中关于以色列在该地存在的早期历史主张提供了重要的考古学依据。

title.zh-Hans: 希西家隧道的铭文
title.zh-Hant: 希西家隧道的铭文

summary.en: This ancient Hebrew inscription, found in Hezekiah's Tunnel, commemorates the successful completion of the water tunnel project in Jerusalem. It provides a first-hand account of the engineering feat described in the Bible.
summary.zh-Hans: 这块古希伯来文铭文在希西家隧道中发现，纪念了耶路撒冷水隧工程的成功竣工。它提供了圣经中描述的这项工程壮举的第一手记载。
summary.zh-Hant: 这块古希伯来文铭文在希西家隧道中发现，纪念了耶路撒冷水隧工程的成功竣工。它提供了圣经中描述的这项工程壮举的第一手记载。

description.en:
The Siloam Inscription was discovered in 1880 by a boy playing in Hezekiah's Tunnel, a water conduit beneath the City of David in Jerusalem. Carved into the rock wall near the Siloam Pool, the inscription was later removed and is now housed in the Istanbul Archaeological Museum.

The inscription, written in elegant paleo-Hebrew script, describes the dramatic moment when two teams of excavators, digging from opposite ends of the tunnel, met in the middle. It recounts the sound of the pickaxes meeting and the water flowing through the newly completed channel, a testament to remarkable engineering and surveying skills.

Dating to the late 8th century BCE, the inscription provides a contemporary, non-biblical account of the construction of Hezekiah's Tunnel. It confirms the biblical narrative of a major water project undertaken in Jerusalem during this period, demonstrating the sophisticated capabilities of ancient Judean engineers.
description.zh-Hans:
西罗亚铭文是1880年一个男孩在耶路撒冷大卫城下方的水渠——希西家隧道中玩耍时发现的。铭文刻在西罗亚池附近的岩壁上，后来被移走，现藏于伊斯坦布尔考古博物馆。

铭文以优美的古希伯来文书写，描述了挖掘者两队人马从隧道两端对向挖掘，最终在中间会合的戏剧性时刻。它记述了镐头相遇的声音以及水流过新完成的渠道的情景，证明了卓越的工程和测量技能。

铭文追溯到公元前8世纪末，提供了关于希西家隧道建造的同期非圣经记载。它证实了圣经中关于此时期耶路撒冷进行重大水利工程的叙事，展示了古代犹大工程师的精湛能力。

scripturalCorrelation.en:
The Bible records King Hezekiah's efforts to secure Jerusalem's water supply in preparation for an anticipated Assyrian siege, a crucial act of defense and resource management.

2 Kings 20:20 states, 'As for the other events of Hezekiah’s reign, all his achievements and how he made the pool and the tunnel to bring water into the city, are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Judah?' The Siloam Inscription provides direct archaeological corroboration for this biblical account, offering a contemporary, first-person narrative of the very tunnel mentioned, thus affirming the historical accuracy of the biblical record regarding Hezekiah's engineering prowess.
scripturalCorrelation.zh-Hans:
圣经记载了希西家王为抵御预期的亚述围攻，确保耶路撒冷供水所做的努力，这是一项至关重要的防御和资源管理行动。

title.zh-Hans: 夏琐城毁灭
title.zh-Hant: 夏琐城毁灭

summary.en: Excavations at Tel Hazor reveal a massive destruction layer by fire, dating to the Late Bronze Age. This archaeological evidence strongly corroborates the biblical narrative in Joshua 11, describing Israel's conquest and burning of Hazor.
summary.zh-Hans: 特尔夏琐的考古发掘揭示了青铜时代晚期大规模毁灭层，有猛烈焚烧的证据——印证了约书亚记11章所载约书亚攻取并焚烧迦南城市夏琐的圣经记述。
summary.zh-Hant: 特尔夏琐的考古发掘揭示了青铜时代晚期大规模毁灭层，有猛烈焚烧的证据——印证了约书亚记11章所载约书亚攻取并焚烧迦南城市夏琐的圣经记述。

en: Tel Hazor, once the largest and most important Canaanite city in the Levant, has been a site of extensive archaeological research since the 1950s, led initially by Yigael Yadin and later by Amnon Ben-Tor. Situated in northern Israel, its strategic location and monumental architecture attest to its ancient power. Among the most significant discoveries at the site is a widespread and intense destruction layer found across the upper and lower cities, marking the end of the Late Bronze Age Canaanite city.

This destruction layer is characterized by thick deposits of ash, charred timbers, collapsed mudbrick walls, and pottery shards, all indicative of a catastrophic conflagration. The evidence points to a sudden and violent end, with structures completely engulfed in flames. Radiocarbon dating and ceramic typology consistently place this event in the Late Bronze Age II, specifically around the mid-13th century BCE. The scale of the destruction suggests a deliberate and thorough act by a conquering force, rather than an accidental fire or natural disaster.

Archaeologists interpret this dramatic layer as the physical manifestation of a major military conquest. While the exact identity of the perpetrators remains a subject of academic debate, the nature and timing of the destruction align remarkably well with the biblical account of the Israelite conquest. The evidence at Hazor provides a tangible link to a period of significant upheaval in the region, offering a powerful archaeological backdrop to the narratives found in the Book of Joshua.
description.zh-Hans:
特尔夏琐位于以色列北部胡拉谷地，是以色列最大的圣经时代考古遗址，鼎盛时期占地约80公顷。约书亚记11:10称其为「这诸国中是为首的」，夏琐在整个青铜时代都是主要的迦南城邦，在埃及咒诅文本、阿马尔纳书信以及中王国和新王国法老的军事年志中均有文献记载。

1955至1958年及1968至1969年，伊盖尔·亚丁主持了大规模发掘；1990至2012年，阿姆农·本-托尔继续主持。发掘揭示了一座规模宏大的青铜时代晚期IIB城市（第XIII层），拥有纪念性建筑——包括礼仪宫殿、神庙和防御工事——于约公元前1300年在一场猛烈的大火中毁灭。毁坏层厚达一米，含有灰烬、烧焦的木梁和坍塌的泥砖墙。本-托尔认为毁坏的性质与约书亚记所描述的以色列人征服一致，特别指出迦南崇拜设施遭到了有计划的拆毁。

遗址还揭示了更早的一次中青铜时代毁灭，归因于法老的征伐。青铜时代晚期宫殿出土了14世纪以前的楔形文字泥板，包括一份提及「伊布尼沙」名字的法律文书，将夏琐与更广阔的美索不达米亚文学和法律文化联系起来。文物由以色列文物局收藏，在夏琐考古遗址博物馆展出。

en: The Book of Joshua provides a specific account of Hazor's fate during the Israelite conquest of Canaan. Joshua 11:10-11 states, "And at that time Joshua turned back and captured Hazor and struck its king with the sword, for Hazor formerly was the head of all those kingdoms. And they burned Hazor with fire." This passage highlights Hazor's preeminence among the northern Canaanite cities and explicitly details its unique destruction by fire, distinguishing it from other cities whose inhabitants were merely put to the sword.

The archaeological findings at Tel Hazor offer a compelling correlation with this biblical narrative. The extensive and intense destruction by fire, dated to the approximate period of the Israelite entry into Canaan, perfectly matches Joshua's description. While archaeology cannot definitively identify the "Israelites" as the destroyers, the evidence of a massive, deliberate conflagration of the "head of all those kingdoms" provides strong external corroboration for the type and scale of event described in the biblical text, making Hazor one of the most significant archaeological sites supporting the historicity of specific events in the Book of Joshua.

约书亚记11:13进一步指出：「至于造在山冈上的城，除了夏琐之外，以色列人都没有焚烧。约书亚只将夏琐焚烧了。」这一具体细节——夏琐是主要城市中唯一被焚烧的——与考古记录一致：毁坏层显示有计划和彻底的焚烧，集中在迦南行政和崇拜建筑上。本-托尔指出夏琐崇拜设施被蓄意破坏，与约书亚叙事中的一神教议程一致。此项证据维持在「有力」等级，因为学术界对毁灭的精确年代和肇事者身份仍有讨论。

title.zh-Hans: 大卫城考古发掘
title.zh-Hant: 大卫城考古发掘

summary.en: Ongoing archaeological work in Jerusalem, starting in 1867, has definitively uncovered the ancient City of David. These discoveries provide tangible evidence for the capital of King David, confirming biblical accounts of its existence and significance.
summary.zh-Hans: 自1867年以来，耶路撒冷持续进行的考古工作已明确揭示了古代大卫城。这些发现为大卫王的首都提供了实物证据，证实了圣经中关于其存在和重要性的记载。
summary.zh-Hant: 自1867年以来，耶路撒冷持续进行的考古工作已明确揭示了古代大卫城。这些发现为大卫王的首都提供了实物证据，证实了圣经中关于其存在和重要性的记载。

description.en:
Archaeological excavations in the area known today as the City of David National Park in Jerusalem began in earnest in 1867 with Charles Warren's explorations. Subsequent digs by numerous archaeologists, including Kathleen Kenyon, Yigal Shiloh, and Eilat Mazar, have continued to unearth significant structures and artifacts. These discoveries span various periods, from the Canaanite era to the First and Second Temple periods, continuously revealing layers of ancient Jerusalem.

The site represents the original core of ancient Jerusalem, the city captured by King David and established as his capital. Key findings include the Stepped Stone Structure, believed to be part of David's palace or the Jebusite fortress, the Gihon Spring, and the Pool of Siloam. These archaeological findings are crucial for understanding the topography and development of Jerusalem as described in the Hebrew Bible.

The definitive nature of these findings provides robust corroboration for the biblical narrative concerning Jerusalem's early history. The physical remains of fortifications, water systems, and residential areas align remarkably well with scriptural descriptions, offering a tangible link to the biblical past. This ongoing archaeological work continues to shed light on the historical accuracy of the Bible.
description.zh-Hans:
耶路撒冷今称大卫城国家公园地区的考古发掘始于1867年查尔斯·沃伦（Charles Warren）的勘探。随后，包括凯瑟琳·凯尼恩（Kathleen Kenyon）、伊加尔·希洛（Yigal Shiloh）和埃拉特·马扎尔（Eilat Mazar）在内的众多考古学家继续挖掘，不断出土重要的建筑和文物。这些发现涵盖了从迦南时代到第一和第二圣殿时期的各个阶段，不断揭示古代耶路撒冷的层层历史。

该遗址代表了古代耶路撒冷的原始核心，即大卫王攻占并建立为首都的城市。主要发现包括阶梯石结构（被认为是大卫宫殿或耶布斯堡垒的一部分）、基训泉和西罗亚池。这些考古发现对于理解希伯来圣经中描述的耶路撒冷地形和发展至关重要。

这些发现的确定性为圣经中关于耶路撒冷早期历史的叙事提供了有力的证实。设防工事、水系统和居住区的实物遗迹与圣经描述惊人地吻合，提供了与圣经历史的实实在在的联系。这一持续的考古工作继续阐明圣经的历史准确性。

scripturalCorrelation.en:
The biblical book of 2 Samuel describes King David's conquest of Jerusalem, then known as Jebus, and his establishment of it as the capital of his united kingdom. The archaeological findings in the City of David directly correlate with these accounts, providing physical context for the narrative of David's reign and the early history of Israel's capital.

2 Samuel 5:7 states: "Nevertheless, David captured the fortress of Zion—which is the City of David."
scripturalCorrelation.zh-Hans:
圣经撒母耳记下描述了大卫王征服耶路撒冷（当时称为耶布斯），并将其建立为他联合王国的首都。大卫城的考古发现与这些记载直接相关，为大卫统治和以色列首都早期历史的叙事提供了实物背景。

撒母耳记下5:7记载：“然而大卫攻取锡安的保障，就是大卫的城。”

title.zh-Hans: 提革拉·毗列色三世年鉴
title.zh-Hant: 提革拉·毗列色三世年鉴

summary.en: These Assyrian royal inscriptions, discovered from 1847 onwards, definitively confirm the existence and actions of King Tiglath-Pileser III. They detail his military campaigns, including those against Israel and Judah, as mentioned in the biblical book of 2 Kings.
summary.zh-Hans: 这些亚述王室铭文自1847年起被发现，明确证实了提革拉·毗列色三世国王的存在和行动。它们详细记载了他的军事战役，包括对以色列和犹大的战役，这些在圣经列王纪下中有所提及。
summary.zh-Hant: 这些亚述王室铭文自1847年起被发现，明确证实了提革拉·毗列色三世国王的存在和行动。它们详细记载了他的军事战役，包括对以色列和犹大的战役，这些在圣经列王纪下中有所提及。

description.en:
The annals of Tiglath-Pileser III (reigned 745–727 BCE) are a collection of cuneiform inscriptions found primarily during excavations at Nimrud (ancient Kalhu) in Mesopotamia, starting around 1847. Austen Henry Layard and later Hormuzd Rassam were instrumental in unearthing these significant Assyrian royal records. These inscriptions, often carved on stone slabs or clay tablets, served as official chronicles of the king's military campaigns and building projects.

These archaeological artifacts are crucial historical documents, detailing the Assyrian Empire's expansion and its interactions with neighboring kingdoms. They provide an external, non-biblical account of events and rulers mentioned in the Hebrew Bible, offering valuable corroboration. The annals specifically mention kings of Israel and Judah, such as Menahem and Ahaz, and describe Assyrian military actions in the Levant.

The definitive nature of these annals provides strong external evidence for the historical accuracy of the biblical narrative concerning the Assyrian period. They confirm the names of kings, the political landscape, and specific events, thereby strengthening the historical context of the books of Kings and Chronicles. Their discovery was a landmark moment in biblical archaeology.
description.zh-Hans:
提革拉·毗列色三世（公元前745-727年在位）的年鉴是主要在美索不达米亚的尼姆鲁德（古卡拉赫）挖掘中发现的楔形文字铭文合集，始于1847年左右。奥斯汀·亨利·莱亚德（Austen Henry Layard）和后来的霍尔穆兹德·拉萨姆（Hormuzd Rassam）在发掘这些重要的亚述王室记录方面发挥了关键作用。这些铭文通常刻在石板或泥板上，作为国王军事战役和建筑工程的官方编年史。

这些考古文物是重要的历史文献，详细记载了亚述帝国的扩张及其与邻近王国的互动。它们提供了希伯来圣经中提及的事件和统治者的外部非圣经记载，提供了宝贵的证实。年鉴特别提到了以色列和犹大的国王，如米拿现和亚哈斯，并描述了亚述在黎凡特的军事行动。

这些年鉴的确定性为圣经中关于亚述时期的叙事提供了强有力的外部证据，证实了其历史准确性。它们证实了国王的名字、政治格局和具体事件，从而加强了列王纪和历代志的历史背景。它们的发现是圣经考古学的一个里程碑时刻。

scripturalCorrelation.en:
The book of 2 Kings describes the Assyrian incursions into Israel and Judah, particularly during the reign of Tiglath-Pileser III (referred to as Pul or Tiglath-Pileser). The biblical text recounts how he invaded Israel, took captives, and received tribute from King Menahem. The Assyrian annals provide a parallel account, mentioning Menahem of Samaria paying tribute to Tiglath-Pileser.

2 Kings 15:29 states: "In the days of Pekah king of Israel, Tiglath-Pileser king of Assyria came and captured Ijon, Abel-Beth-Maacah, Janoah, Kedesh, Hazor, Gilead, and Galilee, all the land of Naphtali, and he carried the people captive to Assyria."
scripturalCorrelation.zh-Hans:
列王纪下描述了亚述入侵以色列和犹大，特别是在提革拉·毗列色三世（被称为普勒或提革拉·毗列色）统治期间。圣经记载了他如何入侵以色列，掳走俘虏，并从米拿现王那里获得贡品。亚述年鉴提供了平行的记载，提及撒玛利亚的米拿现向提革拉·毗列色进贡。

列王纪下15:29记载：“以色列王比加的日子，亚述王提革拉·毗列色来夺了以云、亚伯·伯·玛迦、雅挪、基低斯、夏琐、基列、加利利，以及拿弗他利全地，将这些地方的居民都掳到亚述去了。”

title.zh-Hans: 赖兰纸莎草残片P52
title.zh-Hant: 赖兰纸莎草残片P52

summary.en: This small papyrus fragment, acquired in 1920, is the oldest known fragment of the New Testament, definitively dating to the early 2nd century CE. It contains verses from John's Gospel, affirming its early circulation.
summary.zh-Hans: 这份于1920年购得的小型纸莎草残片，是已知最古老的新约圣经残片，明确地追溯到公元2世纪早期。它包含约翰福音的经文，证实了该福音书的早期流传。
summary.zh-Hant: 这份于1920年购得的小型纸莎草残片，是已知最古老的新约圣经残片，明确地追溯到公元2世纪早期。它包含约翰福音的经文，证实了该福音书的早期流传。

description.en:
The Rylands Papyrus P52, also known as the St John Fragment, was acquired by the John Rylands Library in Manchester in 1920 from a collection of papyri purchased on the Egyptian antiquities market. It was first identified and published by C.H. Roberts in 1935. Based on paleographical analysis (the study of ancient handwriting), it is definitively dated to between 100 and 150 CE, making it the earliest undisputed fragment of the New Testament known to exist.

This tiny fragment, measuring only about 3.5 by 2.5 inches, contains parts of seven lines from John 18 on both sides. The front (recto) contains parts of verses 31-33, and the back (verso) contains parts of verses 37-38. Its discovery pushed back the earliest material evidence for the Gospel of John by over a century, demonstrating that copies of this Gospel were circulating in Egypt relatively soon after its traditional composition date.

The definitive dating of P52 is highly significant for New Testament textual criticism. It provides compelling evidence for the early transmission and widespread distribution of the Gospel of John, challenging theories that suggested a much later composition or circulation date for the Gospel. Its existence underscores the rapid spread of Christian writings in the early second century.
description.zh-Hans:
赖兰纸莎草残片P52，亦称圣约翰残片，于1920年由曼彻斯特的约翰·赖兰图书馆从埃及文物市场购得的一批纸莎草文献中获得。它由C.H.罗伯茨于1935年首次鉴定并发表。根据古文字学分析（对古代手稿的研究），它被明确地定于公元100年至150年之间，使其成为已知现存最早的、无可争议的新约圣经残片。

这块微小的残片，尺寸仅约3.5乘2.5英寸，两面都包含约翰福音18章的七行经文片段。正面（recto）包含第31-33节的部分内容，背面（verso）包含第37-38节的部分内容。它的发现将约翰福音最早的物质证据向前推了一个多世纪，表明该福音书的抄本在其传统成书日期后不久便在埃及流传。

P52的明确年代测定对新约文本批判学具有高度重要性。它为约翰福音的早期传播和广泛流布提供了令人信服的证据，挑战了那些认为该福音书成书或流传日期晚得多的理论。它的存在强调了基督教著作在2世纪早期的迅速传播。

scripturalCorrelation.en:
The Rylands Papyrus P52 contains fragments from John chapter 18, specifically verses relating to Jesus' trial before Pilate. This direct textual evidence from such an early date confirms the presence of these specific passages in the Gospel of John very early in Christian history, providing a tangible link to the original text.

John 18:31-33, 37-38 states: "Pilate said, 'Take him yourselves and judge him by your own law.' 'But we have no right to execute anyone,' they objected. This happened so that the words Jesus had spoken about the kind of death he was going to die would be fulfilled. Then Pilate went back inside the palace, summoned Jesus and asked him, 'Are you the king of the Jews?' ... 'You are right in saying that I am a king. In fact, the reason I was born and came into the world is to testify to the truth. Everyone on the side of truth listens to me.' 'What is truth?' retorted Pilate. With this he went out again to the Jews and told them, 'I find no basis for a charge against him.'"
scripturalCorrelation.zh-Hans:
赖兰纸莎草残片P52包含约翰福音18章的片段，特别是与耶稣在彼拉多面前受审相关的经文。这份来自如此早期日期的直接文本证据，证实了这些特定段落在基督教历史早期已存在于约翰福音中，为原始文本提供了实实在在的联系。

约翰福音18:31-33, 37-38记载：「彼拉多说：『你们自己带他去，按着你们的律法审问他吧！』犹太人说：『我们没有杀人的权柄。』这要应验耶稣所说，自己将要怎样死的话。彼拉多又进了衙门，叫耶稣来，问他说：『你是犹太人的王吗？』……耶稣说：『你说我是王。我为此而生，也为此来到世间，特为给真理作见证。凡属真理的人就听我的话。』彼拉多说：『真理是甚么呢？』说了这话，又出来到犹太人那里，对他们说：『我查不出他有甚么罪来。』」

title.zh-Hans: 切斯特·比替纸莎草文献
title.zh-Hant: 切斯特·比替纸莎草文献

summary.en: Discovered in 1930-1931, this collection of ancient papyri definitively includes some of the earliest and most important biblical manuscripts. They contain significant portions of both the Old and New Testaments, dating from the 2nd to 4th centuries CE.
summary.zh-Hans: 这批于1930-1931年间发现的古代纸莎草文献，明确地包含了一些最早、最重要的圣经手稿。它们涵盖了旧约和新约的显著部分，年代追溯到公元2世纪至4世纪。
summary.zh-Hant: 这批于1930-1931年间发现的古代纸莎草文献，明确地包含了一些最早、最重要的圣经手稿。它们涵盖了旧约和新约的显著部分，年代追溯到公元2世纪至4世纪。

description.en:
The Chester Beatty Papyri are a collection of ancient biblical manuscripts acquired by Alfred Chester Beatty in 1930-1931. The exact discovery location is debated but is generally believed to be near Faiyum in Egypt. These papyri represent some of the earliest surviving copies of Christian scripture, with dates ranging from the 2nd to the 4th centuries CE. They were published by Frederic G. Kenyon in 1933-1937.

This collection is divided into three main codices: P45 (Gospels and Acts), P46 (Pauline Epistles), and P47 (Revelation). P46, dating to around 200 CE, is particularly significant as it contains nearly all of Paul's letters, making it the oldest substantial collection of these epistles. P45, from the early 3rd century, is the earliest codex containing multiple Gospels. These manuscripts provide invaluable insights into the early transmission of the biblical text.

The definitive nature of these papyri as early biblical texts provides crucial evidence for the textual integrity and early circulation of the New Testament. Their age and substantial content offer a direct window into the form of the biblical text in the early centuries of Christianity, predating many other major codices. They are foundational for New Testament textual criticism.
description.zh-Hans:
切斯特·比替纸莎草文献是阿尔弗雷德·切斯特·比替于1930-1931年间获得的一批古代圣经手稿。确切的发现地点存在争议，但普遍认为是在埃及法尤姆附近。这些纸莎草文献代表了现存最早的基督教经文抄本，年代范围从公元2世纪到4世纪。它们由弗雷德里克·G·凯尼恩于1933-1937年间出版。

这批文献分为三个主要抄本：P45（福音书和使徒行传）、P46（保罗书信）和P47（启示录）。P46约在公元200年，尤为重要，因为它包含了保罗几乎所有的书信，使其成为这些书信现存最古老的大量集合。P45来自3世纪早期，是包含多部福音书的最早抄本。这些手稿为圣经文本的早期传播提供了宝贵的见解。

这些纸莎草文献作为早期圣经文本的确定性，为新约的文本完整性和早期流传提供了关键证据。它们的年代和丰富内容为基督教早期几个世纪的圣经文本形式提供了直接窗口，早于许多其他主要抄本。它们是新约文本批判学的基础。

scripturalCorrelation.en:
The Chester Beatty Papyri contain extensive portions of the New Testament, including the Pauline Epistles. The presence of these letters in such early manuscripts confirms their widespread circulation and acceptance within the early Christian community. The specific verse from Romans 8:18 is representative of the theological depth preserved in these ancient texts.

Romans 8:18 states: "I consider that our present sufferings are not worth comparing with the glory that will be revealed in us."
scripturalCorrelation.zh-Hans:
切斯特·比替纸莎草文献包含新约的广泛部分，包括保罗书信。这些书信在如此早期的手稿中出现，证实了它们在早期基督教社群中的广泛流传和接受。罗马书8:18的特定经文代表了这些古代文本中保存的神学深度。

罗马书8:18记载：「我想，现在的苦楚若比起将来要显于我们的荣耀，就不足介意了。」

title.zh-Hans: 西乃抄本
title.zh-Hant: 西乃抄本

summary.en: Discovered in 1844, Codex Sinaiticus is one of the oldest and most complete biblical manuscripts, definitively dating to the 4th century CE. It contains a significant portion of the Greek Old Testament and a complete New Testament.
summary.zh-Hans: 西乃抄本于1844年被发现，是现存最古老、最完整的圣经手稿之一，明确地追溯到公元4世纪。它包含希腊文旧约的显著部分和完整的新约。
summary.zh-Hant: 西乃抄本于1844年被发现，是现存最古老、最完整的圣经手稿之一，明确地追溯到公元4世纪。它包含希腊文旧约的显著部分和完整的新约。

description.en:
Codex Sinaiticus was discovered by Constantin von Tischendorf in 1844 at Saint Catherine's Monastery on Mount Sinai, Egypt. Further portions were acquired by Tischendorf in 1853 and 1859. The majority of the codex is now housed at the British Library in London, with smaller portions remaining at the monastery, Leipzig University Library, and the National Library of Russia. It is definitively dated to the mid-4th century CE, making it one of the two oldest complete Bibles.

This manuscript is a uncial codex, written in Greek on parchment, and originally contained the entire Christian Bible. Today, it preserves over half of the Greek Old Testament (Septuagint) and a complete New Testament, along with the Epistle of Barnabas and parts of The Shepherd of Hermas. Its immense size and comprehensive content make it an unparalleled witness to the biblical text as it existed in the 4th century.

Codex Sinaiticus is of definitive importance for biblical textual criticism. Its early date and extensive content provide a critical benchmark for understanding the transmission of the biblical text. Scholars meticulously compare its readings with other ancient manuscripts to reconstruct the earliest possible text of the Bible, making it a cornerstone for modern Bible translations and studies.
description.zh-Hans:
西乃抄本由康斯坦丁·冯·蒂申多夫于1844年在埃及西乃山上的圣凯瑟琳修道院发现。蒂申多夫于1853年和1859年又获得了更多部分。该抄本的大部分现藏于伦敦的大英图书馆，小部分仍留在修道院、莱比锡大学图书馆和俄罗斯国家图书馆。它被明确地定于公元4世纪中叶，使其成为两部最古老的完整圣经之一。

这份手稿是一部安色尔体抄本，用希腊文写在羊皮纸上，最初包含整部基督教圣经。如今，它保存了超过一半的希腊文旧约（七十士译本）和完整的新约，以及《巴拿巴书信》和《赫马斯牧人书》的部分内容。其巨大的篇幅和全面的内容使其成为4世纪圣经文本存在的无与伦比的见证。

西乃抄本对圣经文本批判学具有决定性的重要性。其早期年代和丰富内容为理解圣经文本的传播提供了关键基准。学者们仔细比较其读法与其他古代手稿，以重建圣经最早的可能文本，使其成为现代圣经翻译和研究的基石。

scripturalCorrelation.en:
As a complete New Testament manuscript, Codex Sinaiticus preserves the entirety of the Gospel of John, including its profound opening verses. The presence of John 1:1 in this ancient codex confirms its early and authoritative status within the Christian canon, reflecting the foundational theological statements of the Gospel.

John 1:1 states: "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God."
scripturalCorrelation.zh-Hans:
作为一部完整的新约手稿，西乃抄本保存了约翰福音的全部内容，包括其深奥的开篇经文。约翰福音1:1在这部古代抄本中的存在，证实了它在基督教正典中的早期和权威地位，反映了该福音书的基础神学陈述。

约翰福音1:1记载：「太初有道，道与神同在，道就是神。」

title.zh-Hans: 梵蒂冈抄本
title.zh-Hant: 梵蒂冈抄本

summary.en: Catalogued in the 15th century, Codex Vaticanus is one of the oldest and most important biblical manuscripts, definitively dating to the 4th century CE. It contains most of the Greek Old Testament and nearly all of the New Testament.
summary.zh-Hans: 梵蒂冈抄本于15世纪被编入目录，是现存最古老、最重要的圣经手稿之一，明确地追溯到公元4世纪。它包含大部分希腊文旧约和几乎所有新约。
summary.zh-Hant: 梵蒂冈抄本于15世纪被编入目录，是现存最古老、最重要的圣经手稿之一，明确地追溯到公元4世纪。它包含大部分希腊文旧约和几乎所有新约。

description.en:
Codex Vaticanus (B) is housed in the Vatican Apostolic Library, where it has been catalogued since at least the 15th century, though its exact provenance before then is unknown. Paleographical analysis definitively dates this manuscript to the first half of the 4th century CE, making it a contemporary of Codex Sinaiticus and one of the two earliest and most significant complete Bibles.

Written in Greek on vellum, the codex originally contained the entire Greek Old Testament (Septuagint) and the New Testament. While some portions are missing today (e.g., parts of Genesis, Psalms, and the end of Hebrews, all of 1 and 2 Timothy, Titus, Philemon, and Revelation), it remains an exceptionally comprehensive and early witness to the biblical text. Its text is highly regarded for its purity and antiquity.

The definitive status of Codex Vaticanus as a primary witness to the biblical text is unparalleled. Its early date and generally excellent textual quality make it a cornerstone for critical editions of the Greek Bible. Scholars rely heavily on Vaticanus, alongside Sinaiticus, to reconstruct the earliest recoverable form of both the Old and New Testaments, influencing virtually all modern Bible translations and studies.
description.zh-Hans:
梵蒂冈抄本（B）现藏于梵蒂冈宗座图书馆，至少自15世纪以来就被编入目录，尽管在此之前的确切来源不明。古文字学分析明确地将这份手稿定于公元4世纪上半叶，使其成为西乃抄本的同期作品，也是两部最早、最重要的完整圣经之一。

该抄本用希腊文写在羊皮纸上，最初包含整部希腊文旧约（七十士译本）和新约。尽管如今缺失了一些部分（例如，创世记、诗篇的部分内容，希伯来书的末尾，以及提摩太前书、提摩太后书、提多书、腓利门书和启示录的全部），它仍然是圣经文本一个异常全面且早期的见证。其文本因其纯粹性和古老性而备受推崇。

梵蒂冈抄本作为圣经文本主要见证的确定地位是无与伦比的。其早期年代和普遍优秀的文本质量使其成为希腊文圣经批判性版本的重要基石。学者们严重依赖梵蒂冈抄本，以及西乃抄本，来重建旧约和新约最早可恢复的形式，影响了几乎所有现代圣经翻译和研究。

scripturalCorrelation.en:
Codex Vaticanus preserves the opening chapters of Genesis, including the foundational creation narrative. Its inclusion of Genesis 1:1 in such an ancient and authoritative manuscript underscores the early Christian community's reverence for the Old Testament as scripture and its foundational role in theological understanding.

Genesis 1:1 states: "In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth."
scripturalCorrelation.zh-Hans:

创世记1:1记载：「起初，神创造天地。」

title.zh-Hans: 纳什纸莎草
title.zh-Hant: 纳什纸莎草

summary.en: Discovered in 1898, the Nash Papyrus is a small but definitively important manuscript fragment containing the Ten Commandments and the Shema Yisrael. It is the oldest known Hebrew manuscript fragment of the biblical text, dating to the 2nd or 1st century BCE.
summary.zh-Hans: 纳什纸莎草于1898年发现，是一份虽小但明确重要的手稿残片，包含十诫和《申命记》中的示玛篇。它是已知最古老的希伯来文圣经文本残片，年代追溯到公元前2世纪或1世纪。
summary.zh-Hant: 纳什纸莎草于1898年发现，是一份虽小但明确重要的手稿残片，包含十诫和《申命记》中的示玛篇。它是已知最古老的希伯来文圣经文本残片，年代追溯到公元前2世纪或1世纪。

description.en:
The Nash Papyrus was acquired in Egypt in 1898 by W.L. Nash and subsequently published by Stanley A. Cook in 1903. It is a single papyrus fragment, measuring approximately 3 by 2 inches, and is now housed at Cambridge University Library. Paleographical analysis definitively dates it to the 2nd or 1st century BCE, making it the oldest known Hebrew manuscript fragment of the biblical text prior to the Dead Sea Scrolls.

This fragment contains the Ten Commandments (Exodus 20:2-17 and Deuteronomy 5:6-21) followed by the Shema Yisrael (Deuteronomy 6:4-5). The text is a harmonized version, combining elements from both Exodus and Deuteronomy, which was common in Jewish liturgical practice of the time. Its significance lies in providing a direct witness to the Hebrew biblical text and liturgical practices from the Hellenistic period.

The definitive dating and content of the Nash Papyrus offer crucial insights into the transmission of the Hebrew Bible before the Masoretic Text tradition became standardized. It demonstrates the existence of biblical texts in Hebrew centuries before the major codices and provides evidence for the early form of key religious texts like the Decalogue and the Shema. Its discovery was a significant precursor to the Dead Sea Scrolls.
description.zh-Hans:
纳什纸莎草于1898年在埃及由W.L.纳什购得，随后由斯坦利·A·库克于1903年出版。它是一块单一的纸莎草残片，尺寸约3乘2英寸，现藏于剑桥大学图书馆。古文字学分析明确地将其定于公元前2世纪或1世纪，使其成为死海古卷之前已知最古老的希伯来文圣经文本残片。

这份残片包含十诫（出埃及记20:2-17和申命记5:6-21），随后是示玛篇（申命记6:4-5）。该文本是一个整合版本，结合了出埃及记和申命记的元素，这在当时犹太人的礼仪实践中很常见。其重要性在于为希腊化时期的希伯来文圣经文本和礼仪实践提供了直接证据。

纳什纸莎草的明确年代和内容为马所拉文本传统标准化之前希伯来圣经的传播提供了关键见解。它证明了在主要抄本出现前几个世纪，希伯来文圣经文本就已经存在，并为十诫和示玛篇等关键宗教文本的早期形式提供了证据。它的发现是死海古卷的一个重要先驱。

scripturalCorrelation.en:
The Nash Papyrus directly correlates with the biblical accounts of the Ten Commandments found in Exodus and Deuteronomy. Its preservation of these fundamental laws, along with the Shema, highlights their central importance in ancient Israelite and early Jewish religious life and practice, as depicted throughout the Old Testament.

Exodus 20:2-17 states: "I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of Egypt, out of the land of slavery. You shall have no other gods before me. You shall not make for yourself an image in the form of anything in heaven above or on the earth beneath or in the waters below. You shall not bow down to them or worship them; for I, the Lord your God, am a jealous God, punishing the children for the sin of the parents to the third and fourth generation of those who hate me, but showing love to a thousand generations of those who love me and keep my commandments. You shall not misuse the name of the Lord your God, for the Lord will not hold anyone guiltless who misuses his name. Remember the Sabbath day by keeping it holy. Six days you shall labor and do all your work, but the seventh day is a sabbath to the Lord your God. On it you shall not do any work, neither you, nor your son or daughter, nor your male or female servant, nor your animals, nor any foreigner residing in your towns. For in six days the Lord made the heavens and the earth, the sea, and all that is in them, but he rested on the seventh day. Therefore the Lord blessed the Sabbath day and made it holy. Honor your father and your mother, so that you may live long in the land the Lord your God is giving you. You shall not murder. You shall not commit adultery. You shall not steal. You shall not give false testimony against your neighbor. You shall not covet your neighbor’s house. You shall not covet your neighbor’s wife, or his male or female servant, his ox or donkey, or anything that belongs to your neighbor."

title.zh-Hans: 阿勒颇抄本
title.zh-Hant: 阿勒颇抄本

summary.en: This 10th-century CE manuscript is the oldest and most complete Hebrew Bible in the Masoretic tradition, definitively serving as the authoritative text for centuries. Though partially damaged in 1947, it remains a cornerstone of biblical scholarship.
summary.zh-Hans: 这份公元10世纪的手稿是马所拉传统中最古老、最完整的希伯来圣经，几个世纪以来一直明确地作为权威文本。尽管在1947年部分受损，它仍然是圣经研究的基石。
summary.zh-Hant: 这份公元10世纪的手稿是马所拉传统中最古老、最完整的希伯来圣经，几个世纪以来一直明确地作为权威文本。尽管在1947年部分受损，它仍然是圣经研究的基石。

description.en:
The Aleppo Codex is a medieval illuminated manuscript of the Hebrew Bible, produced by the scribe Shlomo ben Buya around 930 CE and vocalized by Aaron ben Asher. For centuries, it was housed in the Jewish community of Aleppo, Syria, until it was severely damaged during riots in 1947, with about one-third of its pages lost. The surviving portions were smuggled to Israel in 1958 and are now housed at the National Library of Israel in Jerusalem.

This codex is considered the most authoritative manuscript of the Masoretic Text, the traditional Hebrew text of the Jewish Bible. It was meticulously copied and vocalized according to the Masoretic tradition, which aimed to preserve the precise wording, vocalization, and cantillation of the Hebrew scriptures. For generations, it was used by Jewish scholars and scribes as the standard for correcting other biblical texts.

Despite its damage, the Aleppo Codex remains of definitive importance for biblical studies. It represents the pinnacle of Masoretic textual transmission and is the primary source for the standard scholarly editions of the Hebrew Bible, such as the Biblia Hebraica Stuttgartensia. Its unparalleled accuracy and antiquity make it indispensable for understanding the Hebrew text of the Old Testament.
description.zh-Hans:
阿勒颇抄本是一部中世纪的希伯来圣经泥金手稿，由抄写员所罗门·本·布亚约在公元930年制作，并由亚伦·本·阿舍尔注音。几个世纪以来，它一直存放在叙利亚阿勒颇的犹太社区，直到1947年骚乱中严重受损，约三分之一的页面丢失。幸存的部分于1958年被偷运到以色列，现藏于耶路撒冷的以色列国家图书馆。

这部抄本被认为是马所拉文本（犹太圣经的传统希伯来文文本）中最具权威性的手稿。它根据马所拉传统被一丝不苟地抄写和注音，该传统旨在保存希伯来经文精确的措辞、注音和吟唱符号。几代以来，它被犹太学者和抄写员用作校正其他圣经文本的标准。

尽管受损，阿勒颇抄本对圣经研究仍具有决定性的重要性。它代表了马所拉文本传播的巅峰，是希伯来圣经标准学术版本（如《斯图加特希伯来圣经》）的主要来源。其无与伦比的准确性和古老性使其成为理解旧约希伯来文文本不可或缺的资源。

scripturalCorrelation.en:
The Aleppo Codex contains the entire Hebrew Bible, including the book of Deuteronomy. Its precise Masoretic text provides the authoritative Hebrew wording for passages like Deuteronomy 17:18, which describes the king's duty to write a copy of the law. This manuscript is a direct witness to the textual tradition that shaped the Hebrew scriptures.

Deuteronomy 17:18 states: "When he takes the throne of his kingdom, he is to write for himself on a scroll a copy of this law, taken from that of the Levitical priests."
scripturalCorrelation.zh-Hans:
阿勒颇抄本包含整部希伯来圣经，包括申命记。其精确的马所拉文本为申命记17:18等经文提供了权威的希伯来文措辞，该经文描述了君王抄写律法的职责。这份手稿是塑造希伯来经文的文本传统的直接见证。

申命记17:18记载：「他登了国位，就要将祭司利未人面前的这律法书，为自己抄录一本，存在他那里。」

title.zh-Hans: 列宁格勒抄本
title.zh-Hant: 列宁格勒抄本

summary.en: Completed in 1008-1009 CE, the Leningrad Codex is the oldest complete manuscript of the Hebrew Bible in the Masoretic tradition, definitively serving as the basis for modern scholarly editions. It is a crucial resource for Old Testament studies.
summary.zh-Hans: 列宁格勒抄本于公元1008-1009年完成，是马所拉传统中最古老的完整希伯来圣经手稿，明确地作为现代学术版本的基础。它是旧约研究的关键资源。
summary.zh-Hant: 列宁格勒抄本于公元1008-1009年完成，是马所拉传统中最古老的完整希伯来圣经手稿，明确地作为现代学术版本的基础。它是旧约研究的关键资源。

description.en:
The Leningrad Codex (Codex Leningradensis, B19a) was completed in Cairo in 1008 or 1009 CE, copied by Samuel ben Jacob and vocalized by Aaron ben Moses ben Asher. It is currently housed at the Russian National Library in St. Petersburg, where it has been since the mid-19th century. This manuscript is definitively recognized as the oldest complete manuscript of the Hebrew Bible in the Masoretic tradition.

This codex is a meticulously crafted manuscript, preserving the Masoretic Text of the Hebrew Bible with its precise vocalization, accentuation, and marginal notes (Masorah). It serves as a primary witness to the textual tradition established by the Ben Asher family, which became the standard for the Hebrew Bible. Its completeness and careful execution make it an invaluable resource.

The definitive importance of the Leningrad Codex cannot be overstated. Due to the partial loss of the Aleppo Codex, the Leningrad Codex has become the primary text used for modern critical editions of the Hebrew Bible, most notably the Biblia Hebraica Stuttgartensia (BHS) and Biblia Hebraica Quinta (BHQ). It is the foundational text for virtually all scholarly study and translation of the Old Testament today.
description.zh-Hans:
列宁格勒抄本（Codex Leningradensis, B19a）于公元1008或1009年在开罗完成，由撒母耳·本·雅各布抄写，并由亚伦·本·摩西·本·阿舍尔注音。它目前藏于圣彼得堡的俄罗斯国家图书馆，自19世纪中叶以来一直在此。这份手稿被明确认定为马所拉传统中最古老的完整希伯来圣经手稿。

这部抄本是一份精心制作的手稿，保存了希伯来圣经的马所拉文本，包括其精确的注音、重音和旁注（马所拉）。它作为本·阿舍尔家族建立的文本传统的主要见证，该传统成为了希伯来圣经的标准。其完整性和精心的制作使其成为一份无价的资源。

列宁格勒抄本的决定性重要性怎么强调都不为过。由于阿勒颇抄本的部分缺失，列宁格勒抄本已成为现代希伯来圣经批判性版本（最著名的是《斯图加特希伯来圣经》（BHS）和《第五版希伯来圣经》（BHQ））所使用的主要文本。它是当今几乎所有旧约学术研究和翻译的基础文本。

The Leningrad Codex contains the complete Hebrew Bible, including the book of Isaiah. Its precise Masoretic text provides the authoritative Hebrew wording for passages like Isaiah 1:1, which introduces the prophet's vision. This manuscript is a direct and complete witness to the textual tradition that shaped the Hebrew scriptures.

Isaiah 1:1 states: "The vision concerning Judah and Jerusalem that Isaiah son of Amoz saw during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, kings of Judah."

title.zh-Hans: 象岛纸莎草文献
title.zh-Hant: 象岛纸莎草文献

summary.en: Discovered from 1893 onwards, these Aramaic papyri provide strong evidence for a Jewish community in Egypt during the Persian period. They offer unique insights into their religious practices and social life, correlating with biblical accounts in Ezra and Nehemiah.
summary.zh-Hans: 这些从1893年起陆续发现的亚兰文纸莎草文献，为波斯时期埃及的犹太社群提供了有力证据。它们提供了对其宗教习俗和社会生活的独特见解，与以斯拉记和尼希米记中的圣经记载相互印证。
summary.zh-Hant: 这些从1893年起陆续发现的亚兰文纸莎草文献，为波斯时期埃及的犹太社群提供了有力证据。它们提供了对其宗教习俗和社会生活的独特见解，与以斯拉记和尼希米记中的圣经记载相互印证。

description.en:
The Elephantine Papyri are a collection of ancient papyrus documents written in Aramaic, discovered on Elephantine Island in the Nile River, Egypt, starting in 1893. These documents, dating from the 5th century BCE (Persian period), were found by various archaeological expeditions and are now dispersed among museums in Berlin, Cairo, and New York. They represent the archives of a Jewish military colony stationed at Elephantine.

These manuscripts provide a unique window into the life, law, and religion of a Jewish community living outside of Judea during the Persian Empire. They include legal documents (marriage contracts, deeds of sale), administrative records, and letters, notably a petition to the Persian governor of Judah regarding the rebuilding of their temple to Yahweh. They offer valuable comparative material for understanding post-exilic Judaism.

The Elephantine Papyri offer strong corroboration for the historical context of the books of Ezra and Nehemiah, particularly concerning the Persian administration and the existence of Jewish communities in the diaspora. While they present some unique religious practices (e.g., the existence of a temple outside Jerusalem), they confirm the broader historical and cultural milieu described in the biblical texts.
description.zh-Hans:
象岛纸莎草文献是一批用亚兰文写成的古代纸莎草文件，从1893年起在埃及尼罗河的象岛上被发现。这些文件年代追溯到公元前5世纪（波斯时期），由各种考古探险队发现，现分散于柏林、开罗和纽约的博物馆中。它们代表了驻扎在象岛的犹太军事殖民地的档案。

这些手稿为波斯帝国时期居住在犹大境外的一个犹太社群的生活、法律和宗教提供了独特的窗口。它们包括法律文件（婚约、销售契约）、行政记录和信件，其中值得注意的是一份向犹大波斯总督请愿重建他们耶和华神殿的信。它们为理解被掳归回后的犹太教提供了宝贵的比较材料。

象岛纸莎草文献为以斯拉记和尼希米记的历史背景提供了有力佐证，特别是关于波斯行政管理和散居犹太社群的存在。尽管它们呈现了一些独特的宗教习俗（例如，在耶路撒冷之外存在圣殿），但它们证实了圣经文本中描述的更广泛的历史和文化背景。

scripturalCorrelation.en:
The Elephantine Papyri provide a strong historical backdrop for the books of Ezra and Nehemiah, which detail the return of exiles to Judah and the rebuilding of Jerusalem and its temple under Persian rule. The papyri's references to Persian officials and the administrative structures of the empire align with the biblical narrative, illustrating the broader context of Jewish life during this period.

Ezra 4:7 states: "In the days of Artaxerxes, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel and the rest of their associates wrote to Artaxerxes king of Persia. The letter was written in Aramaic script and set forth in Aramaic."
scripturalCorrelation.zh-Hans:
象岛纸莎草文献为以斯拉记和尼希米记提供了坚实的历史背景，这两本书详细记载了被掳者回归犹大以及在波斯统治下重建耶路撒冷及其圣殿。这些纸莎草文献中提及的波斯官员和帝国行政结构与圣经叙事相符，阐明了这一时期犹太人生活的更广泛背景。

以斯拉记4:7记载：「亚达薛西年间，比施兰、米特利达、他别和他们的同党上书亚达薛西王。那奏章是用亚兰文字、亚兰语写的。」

title.zh-Hans: 铜卷
title.zh-Hant: 铜卷

summary.en: Discovered in 1952 among the Dead Sea Scrolls, this unique copper manuscript provides strong evidence of hidden treasures, possibly from the Jerusalem Temple. Its distinct nature and content offer a fascinating, albeit enigmatic, link to ancient Jewish wealth.
summary.zh-Hans: 这份独特的铜制手稿于1952年在死海古卷中被发现，为隐藏的宝藏提供了有力证据，这些宝藏可能来自耶路撒冷圣殿。其独特的性质和内容提供了一个引人入胜但又神秘的与古代犹太财富的联系。
summary.zh-Hant: 这份独特的铜制手稿于1952年在死海古卷中被发现，为隐藏的宝藏提供了有力证据，这些宝藏可能来自耶路撒冷圣殿。其独特的性质和内容提供了一个引人入胜但又神秘的与古代犹太财富的联系。

description.en:
The Copper Scroll (3Q15) was discovered in Cave 3 at Qumran in 1952, as part of the Dead Sea Scrolls collection. Unlike other scrolls, which are written on parchment or papyrus, this scroll is made of thin sheets of copper, riveted together. Its unique material and content posed significant challenges for its unrolling and decipherment, which was finally achieved in 1955-1956. It is now housed at the Jordan Museum in Amman.

The scroll is not a biblical or religious text in the traditional sense, but rather a detailed inventory of 64 locations where vast quantities of gold, silver, and other precious items are purportedly hidden. The total value described is immense, leading to speculation that it might refer to Temple treasures, possibly hidden before the Roman destruction of Jerusalem in 70 CE. Its language is Mishnaic Hebrew, distinct from the literary Hebrew of other Qumran scrolls.

While the treasures themselves have never been found, the Copper Scroll provides strong, albeit indirect, evidence for the immense wealth associated with the Jerusalem Temple and the practice of hiding valuables in times of crisis. It offers a unique glimpse into the material culture and financial practices of ancient Judea, complementing the broader historical context found in biblical and extra-biblical sources regarding Temple wealth and its fate.
description.zh-Hans:
铜卷（3Q15）于1952年在昆兰3号洞穴中被发现，是死海古卷收藏的一部分。与其他写在羊皮纸或纸莎草纸上的卷轴不同，这份卷轴由薄铜片铆接而成。其独特的材料和内容对其展开和破译构成了重大挑战，最终于1955-1956年得以实现。它现藏于安曼的约旦博物馆。

这份卷轴并非传统意义上的圣经或宗教文本，而是一份详细的清单，列出了64个据称藏有大量黄金、白银和其他珍贵物品的地点。所描述的总价值巨大，引发了人们猜测它可能指的是圣殿宝藏，可能是在公元70年罗马人摧毁耶路撒冷之前被隐藏的。其语言是米示拿希伯来语，与昆兰其他卷轴的文学希伯来语不同。

尽管这些宝藏本身从未被发现，但铜卷提供了有力（尽管是间接的）证据，证明耶路撒冷圣殿所关联的巨大财富以及在危机时期隐藏贵重物品的做法。它为古代犹大的物质文化和金融实践提供了独特的视角，补充了圣经和非圣经资料中关于圣殿财富及其命运的更广泛历史背景。

scripturalCorrelation.en:
The Copper Scroll, with its detailed list of hidden treasures, resonates with biblical accounts of the immense wealth of the Jerusalem Temple, particularly during the Second Temple period. Books like Nehemiah describe the rebuilding and refurnishing of the Temple, implying significant resources. The scroll provides a tangible, if mysterious, connection to the material aspects of the Temple's existence and potential hidden riches.

Nehemiah 7, while not directly mentioning hidden treasures, details the census of those who returned from exile and their contributions for the work on the Temple and the city walls, indicating the significant resources and wealth associated with the Temple and its restoration: "Some of the heads of the families contributed to the work. The governor gave to the treasury 1,000 darics of gold, 50 bowls and 530 priestly garments. Some of the heads of the families gave to the treasury for the work 20,000 darics of gold and 2,200 minas of silver. The rest of the people gave 20,000 darics of gold, 2,000 minas of silver and 67 priestly garments."
scripturalCorrelation.zh-Hans:
铜卷及其详细的隐藏宝藏清单，与圣经中关于耶路撒冷圣殿巨大财富的记载相呼应，特别是在第二圣殿时期。像尼希米记这样的书卷描述了圣殿的重建和翻新，暗示了大量的资源。这份卷轴为圣殿存在的物质方面和潜在的隐藏财富提供了一个有形但神秘的联系。

尼希米记7章记载：「有些族长为工程捐献。省长捐入库中一千达利克金子，五十个碗，五百三十件祭司的礼服。有些族长捐入工程库中二万达利克金子，二千二百弥拿银子。其余的百姓捐二万达利克金子，二千弥拿银子，六十七件祭司的礼服。」

title.zh-Hans: 圣殿卷轴
title.zh-Hant: 圣殿卷轴

summary.en: Discovered in 1956 and acquired in 1967, the Temple Scroll is the longest Dead Sea Scroll, providing strong evidence for an idealized vision of the Jerusalem Temple and its laws. It offers unique insights into sectarian Jewish legal and cultic practices.
summary.zh-Hans: 圣殿卷轴于1956年被发现，1967年被获得，是死海古卷中最长的一卷，为耶路撒冷圣殿的理想化愿景及其律法提供了有力证据。它为宗派犹太教的法律和祭祀习俗提供了独特的见解。
summary.zh-Hant: 圣殿卷轴于1956年被发现，1967年被获得，是死海古卷中最长的一卷，为耶路撒冷圣殿的理想化愿景及其律法提供了有力证据。它为宗派犹太教的法律和祭祀习俗提供了独特的见解。

description.en:
The Temple Scroll (11QTemple) was discovered by Bedouin in Cave 11 at Qumran in 1956 but was not acquired by Israeli authorities until after the Six-Day War in 1967. It is the longest of the Dead Sea Scrolls, measuring over 27 feet when unrolled. It is now housed in the Shrine of the Book at the Israel Museum in Jerusalem. Dating from the late 2nd or early 1st century BCE, it is written in a distinctive, elegant Hebrew script.

This scroll presents a detailed blueprint for an idealized temple, its courts, and associated rituals, along with extensive legal material (halakha) that expands upon and reinterprets laws found in Exodus, Leviticus, and Deuteronomy. It is written as if God himself is speaking, using the first person ("I"). Scholars believe it reflects the sectarian views of the Qumran community, offering their vision of a pure temple and a perfect legal system.

The Temple Scroll provides strong evidence for the diversity of Jewish thought and legal interpretation during the Second Temple period. While not a canonical biblical book, its extensive legal sections and cultic regulations offer invaluable comparative material for understanding biblical law and the development of Jewish halakha. It sheds light on the aspirations and beliefs of a significant Jewish sect.
description.zh-Hans:
圣殿卷轴（11QTemple）于1956年由贝都因人在昆兰11号洞穴中发现，但直到1967年六日战争后才被以色列当局获得。它是死海古卷中最长的一卷，展开后超过27英尺。它现藏于耶路撒冷以色列博物馆的圣书之龛。年代追溯到公元前2世纪末或1世纪初，它以一种独特而优雅的希伯来文书写。

这份卷轴为一座理想化的圣殿、其庭院和相关仪式提供了详细的蓝图，并附有大量的法律材料（哈拉卡），这些材料扩展并重新诠释了出埃及记、利未记和申命记中的律法。它以第一人称（“我”）书写，仿佛是上帝亲自在说话。学者们认为它反映了昆兰社群的宗派观点，提供了他们对纯洁圣殿和完美法律体系的愿景。

圣殿卷轴为第二圣殿时期犹太思想和法律解释的多样性提供了有力证据。虽然它不是一部正典圣经书卷，但其广泛的法律章节和祭祀规定为理解圣经律法和犹太哈拉卡的演变提供了无价的比较材料。它揭示了一个重要犹太宗派的愿望和信仰。

scripturalCorrelation.en:
The Temple Scroll extensively reworks and expands upon laws found in the Pentateuch, particularly in Leviticus and Deuteronomy, concerning the Temple, sacrifices, and purity. Its detailed regulations for the king, for instance, build upon and elaborate on biblical injunctions, demonstrating how ancient Jewish groups interpreted and applied scriptural law in their own contexts.

Deuteronomy 17, which outlines laws for the king, is a key biblical passage that the Temple Scroll elaborates upon. For example, Deuteronomy 17:14-15 states: "When you enter the land the Lord your God is giving you and have taken possession of it and settled in it, and you say, 'Let us set a king over us like all the nations around us,' be sure to appoint over you a king the Lord your God chooses. He must be from among your own brothers. Do not place a foreigner over you, one who is not a brother Israelite." The Temple Scroll expands on these and other royal laws significantly.
scripturalCorrelation.zh-Hans:
圣殿卷轴广泛地重构和扩展了摩西五经中关于圣殿、献祭和洁净的律法，特别是在利未记和申命记中。例如，它对君王的详细规定，在圣经禁令的基础上进行阐述和细化，展示了古代犹太群体如何在自己的语境中解释和应用经文律法。

申命记17:14-15记载：「你进了耶和华你神所赐之地，得了那地，居住的时候，若说：『我要立王治理我，像我四围的列国一样。』你总要立耶和华你神所拣选的人为王；必从你弟兄中立一人，不可立外国人作你的王，因为他不是你的弟兄。」圣殿卷轴显著地扩展了这些及其他关于君王的律法。

title.zh-Hans: 马大拉纸莎草残片 (P64)
title.zh-Hant: 马大拉纸莎草残片 (P64)

summary.en: Discovered in 1901, the Magdalen Papyrus (P64) is a small fragment of Matthew's Gospel, providing strong evidence for its early circulation. Its dating, though debated, suggests a very early witness to the New Testament text.
summary.zh-Hans: 1901年发现的马大拉纸莎草残片（P64）是马太福音的一小部分，为其早期流传提供了有力证据。尽管其年代存在争议，但它表明了新约文本的一个非常早期的见证。
summary.zh-Hant: 1901年发现的马大拉纸莎草残片（P64）是马太福音的一小部分，为其早期流传提供了有力证据。尽管其年代存在争议，但它表明了新约文本的一个非常早期的见证。

description.en:
The Magdalen Papyrus (P64) consists of three small fragments of Matthew's Gospel, acquired in Luxor, Egypt, in 1901 by Reverend Charles B. Huleatt and subsequently donated to Magdalen College, Oxford. The fragments contain portions of Matthew 26. While some scholars, notably Carsten Peter Thiede, proposed a very early 1st-century date, the consensus among most paleographers places it in the late 2nd or early 3rd century CE.

Despite the debate over its precise dating, P64 is recognized as one of the earliest surviving witnesses to the Gospel of Matthew. It is written in Greek on papyrus and, along with P67 and P4, forms a single codex. The fragments preserve parts of the narrative concerning Jesus' anointing at Bethany and the disciples' reaction, offering direct textual evidence from an early period.

The Magdalen Papyrus provides strong evidence for the early transmission of the Gospel of Matthew. Even at a conservative dating, it attests to the circulation of Matthew's Gospel within the first two centuries of Christianity. Its existence contributes to the broader understanding of the textual history of the New Testament and the rapid spread of Christian writings.
description.zh-Hans:
马大拉纸莎草残片（P64）由马太福音的三个小片段组成，于1901年由查尔斯·B·休利特牧师在埃及卢克索获得，随后捐赠给牛津大学马大拉学院。这些残片包含马太福音第26章的部分内容。尽管一些学者，特别是卡斯滕·彼得·蒂德，提出其年代可追溯到非常早期的1世纪，但大多数古文字学家的共识将其定在公元2世纪末或3世纪初。

尽管对其确切年代存在争议，P64仍被公认为马太福音现存最早的见证之一。它以希腊文写在纸莎草上，与P67和P4共同构成一个抄本。这些残片保留了关于耶稣在伯大尼受膏以及门徒反应的部分叙述，提供了早期直接的文本证据。

马大拉纸莎草残片为马太福音的早期传播提供了有力证据。即使按保守的年代推断，它也证明了马太福音在基督教头两个世纪内的流传。它的存在有助于更广泛地理解新约的文本历史和基督教著作的迅速传播。

scripturalCorrelation.en:
The Magdalen Papyrus contains fragments from Matthew chapter 26, specifically verses describing the anointing of Jesus by a woman with expensive perfume. This direct textual evidence from an early manuscript confirms the presence of these specific passages in the Gospel of Matthew very early in Christian history, providing a tangible link to the original text.

Matthew 26:7-8 states: "a woman came to him with an alabaster jar of very expensive perfume, which she poured on his head as he was reclining at the table. When the disciples saw this, they were indignant. 'Why this waste?' they asked."
scripturalCorrelation.zh-Hans:
马大拉纸莎草残片包含马太福音第26章的片段，特别是描述一位妇女用昂贵香膏膏抹耶稣的经文。这份早期手稿的直接文本证据证实了这些特定段落在基督教历史早期就已存在于马太福音中，为原始文本提供了实物链接。

马太福音26:7-8记载：“有一个女人拿着一玉瓶极贵的香膏来，趁他坐席的时候，浇在他的头上。门徒看见就很不喜悦，说：‘何用这样浪费呢！’”

title.zh-Hans: 希腊文新约手稿
title.zh-Hant: 希腊文新约手稿

summary.en: Thousands of Greek New Testament manuscripts, dating from the 1st to 15th centuries CE, definitively provide an unparalleled textual basis for the New Testament. Their sheer number and antiquity ensure exceptional textual integrity.
summary.zh-Hans: 数千份可追溯至公元1世纪至15世纪的希腊文新约手稿，为新约提供了无可比拟的文本基础。其庞大的数量和古老的年代确保了卓越的文本完整性。
summary.zh-Hant: 数千份可追溯至公元1世纪至15世纪的希腊文新约手稿，为新约提供了无可比拟的文本基础。其庞大的数量和古老的年代确保了卓越的文本完整性。

description.en:
The Greek New Testament is supported by an astonishing number of manuscripts, far exceeding any other ancient work. This vast collection includes over 5,800 Greek manuscripts, ranging from tiny papyrus fragments to complete codices, dating from the 2nd century CE through the 15th century CE. These manuscripts have been discovered and catalogued over centuries and are now housed in libraries, monasteries, and private collections worldwide.

These manuscripts are categorized into papyri (the earliest, often fragmentary), uncials (capital letters on parchment), minuscules (small, cursive letters on parchment), and lectionaries (books containing scripture readings for church services). This rich textual tradition allows scholars to compare thousands of witnesses, identifying variations and reconstructing the earliest possible text of the New Testament with a high degree of confidence.

The definitive abundance and antiquity of Greek New Testament manuscripts provide an unparalleled textual foundation. This wealth of evidence allows for rigorous textual criticism, ensuring that the New Testament we have today is remarkably close to its original form. It stands as a testament to the careful preservation and widespread dissemination of these sacred texts throughout early Christian history.
description.zh-Hans:
希腊文新约得到了数量惊人的手稿支持，远超任何其他古代著作。这一庞大的收藏包括5,800多份希腊文手稿，从微小的纸莎草残片到完整的抄本，年代从公元2世纪到15世纪。这些手稿经过几个世纪的发现和编目，现收藏于世界各地的图书馆、修道院和私人收藏中。

这些手稿分为纸莎草本（最早的，常为残片）、大写体（羊皮纸上的大写字母）、小写体（羊皮纸上的小而草写的字母）和选读本（包含教会礼拜经文选段的书籍）。这一丰富的文本传统使学者能够比较数千份见证，识别变异并以高度的信心重建新约最早的可能文本。

希腊文新约手稿的确定性丰富性和古老性提供了无与伦比的文本基础。这一丰富的证据使得严格的文本批判成为可能，确保我们今天拥有的新约与其原始形式惊人地接近。它证明了这些神圣文本在早期基督教历史中被精心保存和广泛传播。

scripturalCorrelation.en:
The vast collection of Greek New Testament manuscripts directly correlates with the biblical assertion of the divine inspiration and enduring nature of scripture. The meticulous copying and preservation of these texts over centuries underscore the early Christian belief in their authority and importance, as articulated in passages like 2 Timothy 3:16.

2 Timothy 3:16 states: "All Scripture is God-breathed and is useful for teaching, rebuking, correcting and training in righteousness."
scripturalCorrelation.zh-Hans:
希腊文新约手稿的庞大收藏直接与圣经关于神圣默示和经文永恒性的主张相关联。几个世纪以来对这些文本的细致抄写和保存，强调了早期基督徒对其权威和重要性的信仰，正如提摩太后书3:16等经文所阐明的。

提摩太后书3:16记载：“圣经都是神所默示的，于教训、督责、使人归正、教导人学义都是有益的。”

title.zh-Hans: 鲍德默纸莎草文献
title.zh-Hant: 鲍德默纸莎草文献

summary.en: Discovered between 1952 and 1956, the Bodmer Papyri definitively comprise a significant collection of early biblical and Christian texts. They include some of the oldest and most complete manuscripts of the Gospels of John and Luke.
summary.zh-Hans: 鲍德默纸莎草文献于1952年至1956年间发现，明确包含了一批重要的早期圣经和基督教文本。其中包括约翰福音和路加福音一些最古老、最完整的手稿。
summary.zh-Hant: 鲍德默纸莎草文献于1952年至1956年间发现，明确包含了一批重要的早期圣经和基督教文本。其中包括约翰福音和路加福音一些最古老、最完整的手稿。

description.en:
The Bodmer Papyri are a collection of over 20 papyri, discovered in Egypt between 1952 and 1956, near Dishna, the ancient site of Pabau. Acquired by Martin Bodmer, the majority are housed in the Bodmer Library in Cologny, Geneva, with some portions (like P75) now residing in the Vatican Library. These manuscripts date from the 2nd to 4th centuries CE and include both pagan and Christian texts.

Among the most significant are P66 (Gospel of John, c. 200 CE), P72 (Peter's Epistles and Jude, 3rd-4th century CE), and P75 (Gospels of Luke and John, early 3rd century CE). P66 is one of the earliest and most complete manuscripts of John, while P75 is particularly notable for its close textual agreement with Codex Vaticanus, indicating a very stable textual tradition for these Gospels at an early date.

The definitive importance of the Bodmer Papyri lies in their early date and substantial content, providing crucial evidence for the textual history of the New Testament. They offer direct access to the form of the Gospels and other Christian writings in the early centuries, confirming the early circulation and textual stability of these foundational texts. They are indispensable for textual criticism.
description.zh-Hans:
鲍德默纸莎草文献是20多份纸莎草文献的集合，于1952年至1956年间在埃及迪什纳（古帕鲍遗址附近）被发现。这些文献由马丁·鲍德默购得，大部分收藏于日内瓦科洛尼的鲍德默图书馆，其中一些部分（如P75）现存于梵蒂冈图书馆。这些手稿的年代可追溯到公元2世纪至4世纪，包括异教和基督教文本。

其中最重要的包括P66（约翰福音，约公元200年）、P72（彼得书信和犹大书，公元3-4世纪）和P75（路加福音和约翰福音，公元3世纪初）。P66是约翰福音现存最早、最完整的手稿之一，而P75因其与梵蒂冈抄本的高度文本一致性而特别引人注目，这表明这些福音书在早期就有着非常稳定的文本传统。

鲍德默纸莎草文献的决定性重要性在于其早期年代和实质性内容，为新约的文本历史提供了关键证据。它们使我们能够直接了解早期几个世纪福音书和其他基督教著作的形式，证实了这些基础文本的早期流传和文本稳定性。它们对于文本批判是不可或缺的。

scripturalCorrelation.en:
The Bodmer Papyri, particularly P66 and P75, contain extensive portions of the Gospel of John, including its prologue. The presence of John 1:1-14 in these early manuscripts confirms the antiquity and widespread acceptance of this foundational theological text within the early Christian community, demonstrating its consistent transmission.

John 1:1-14 states: "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. He was with God in the beginning. Through him all things were made; without him nothing was made that has been made. In him was life, and that life was the light of all mankind. The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness has not overcome it. There was a man sent from God whose name was John. He came as a witness to testify concerning that light, so that through him all might believe. He himself was not the light; he came only as a witness to the light. The true light that gives light to everyone was coming into the world. He was in the world, and though the world was made through him, the world did not recognize him. He came to that which was his own, but his own did not receive him. Yet to all who did receive him, to those who believed in his name, he gave the right to become children of God—children born not of natural descent, nor of human decision or a husband’s will, but born of God. The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us. We have seen his glory, the glory of the one and only Son, who came from the Father, full of grace and truth."
scripturalCorrelation.zh-Hans:
鲍德默纸莎草文献，特别是P66和P75，包含约翰福音的广泛部分，包括其序言。约翰福音1:1-14在这些早期手稿中的存在，证实了这一基础神学文本在早期基督教社群中的古老性和广泛接受度，展示了其持续的传承。

约翰福音1:1-14记载：“太初有道，道与神同在，道就是神。这道太初与神同在。万物是藉着他造的；凡被造的，没有一样不是藉着他造的。在他里头有生命，这生命就是人的光。光照在黑暗里，黑暗却不接受光。有一个人，是从神那里差来的，名叫约翰。这人来，是要为光作见证，叫众人因他可以信。他不是那光，乃是要为光作见证。那光是真光，照亮一切生在世上的人。他在世界，世界也是藉着他造的，世界却不认识他。他到自己的地方来，自己的人倒不接待他。凡接待他的，就是信他名的人，他就赐他们权柄，作神的儿女。这等人不是从血气生的，不是从情欲生的，也不是从人意生的，乃是从神生的。道成了肉身，住在我们中间，充充满满地有恩典有真理。我们也见过他的荣光，正是父独生子的荣光。”

title.zh-Hans: 亚历山大抄本
title.zh-Hant: 亚历山大抄本

summary.en: This ancient Greek manuscript is one of the oldest and most complete biblical codices, offering invaluable insights into early Christian scripture. It contains most of the Old and New Testaments, serving as a cornerstone for textual criticism.
summary.zh-Hans: 这份古老的希腊文手稿是现存最古老、最完整的圣经抄本之一，为早期基督教经文提供了宝贵的见解。它包含大部分旧约和新约，是文本批判的基石。
summary.zh-Hant: 这份古老的希腊文手稿是现存最古老、最完整的圣经抄本之一，为早期基督教经文提供了宝贵的见解。它包含大部分旧约和新约，是文本批判的基石。

description.en:
The Codex Alexandrinus is a 5th-century CE manuscript, though it was formally presented to King James I in 1627 by Cyril Lucar, Patriarch of Constantinople. Its journey from Egypt to Europe highlights its long history and preservation. Today, it is a prized possession of the British Library in London.

Written in Greek uncials on vellum, the codex originally contained the entire Greek Bible (Septuagint Old Testament and New Testament), along with some apocryphal books and early Christian writings. While some portions are now lost, it remains a remarkably complete witness to the biblical text.

Its significance is definitive for biblical scholarship, being one of the three great uncial codices (alongside Vaticanus and Sinaiticus). It provides crucial evidence for the text of both the Old and New Testaments, helping scholars reconstruct the earliest forms of the biblical text and understand its transmission.
description.zh-Hans:
亚历山大抄本是一份公元5世纪的手稿，尽管它于1627年由君士坦丁堡牧首西里尔·卢卡尔正式呈献给詹姆斯一世国王。它从埃及到欧洲的旅程彰显了其悠久的历史和保存状况。如今，它是伦敦大英图书馆的珍贵藏品。

该抄本以希腊文大写字母写在羊皮纸上，最初包含整部希腊文圣经（七十士译本旧约和新约），以及一些次经和早期基督教著作。尽管部分内容已失传，但它仍然是圣经文本一个非常完整的见证。

它对于圣经研究具有决定性意义，是三大希腊文大写体抄本之一（与梵蒂冈抄本和西奈抄本并列）。它为旧约和新约的文本提供了关键证据，帮助学者重建圣经文本的最早形式并理解其传承。
description.zh-Hant:
亚历山大抄本是一份公元5世纪的手稿，尽管它于1627年由君士坦丁堡牧首西里尔·卢卡尔正式呈献给詹姆斯一世国王。它从埃及到欧洲的旅程彰显了其悠久的历史和保存状况。如今，它是伦敦大英图书馆的珍贵藏品。

该抄本以希腊文大写字母写在羊皮纸上，最初包含整部希腊文圣经（七十士译本旧约和新约），以及一些次经和早期基督教著作。尽管部分内容已失传，但它仍然是圣经文本一个非常完整的见证。

它对于圣经研究具有决定性意义，是三大希腊文大写体抄本之一（与梵蒂冈抄本和西奈抄本并列）。它为旧约和新约的文本提供了关键证据，帮助学者重建圣经文本的最早形式并理解其传承。

scripturalCorrelation.en:
The Codex Alexandrinus is a primary witness to the New Testament text, including the Book of Revelation. Its ancient Greek text provides a window into the early transmission of apocalyptic literature, affirming the presence and form of these books in the early church.

Revelation 1:1 (NIV): "The revelation from Jesus Christ, which God gave him to show his servants what must soon take place. He made it known by sending his angel to his servant John."
scripturalCorrelation.zh-Hans:
亚历山大抄本是新约文本，包括启示录的主要见证。其古老的希腊文文本为启示文学的早期传播提供了一个窗口，证实了这些书卷在早期教会中的存在和形式。

title.zh-Hans: 开罗格尼扎残片
title.zh-Hant: 开罗格尼扎残片

summary.en: The Cairo Genizah is a collection of nearly 200,000 Jewish manuscript fragments discovered in a synagogue in Old Cairo. These documents, dating from the 9th to 19th centuries, provide unparalleled insights into medieval Jewish life and biblical texts.
summary.zh-Hans: 开罗格尼扎是在开罗老城一座犹太会堂中发现的近20万份犹太手稿残片集合。这些文献可追溯至9世纪至19世纪，为中世纪犹太生活和圣经文本提供了无与伦比的见解。
summary.zh-Hant: 开罗格尼扎是在开罗老城一座犹太会堂中发现的近20万份犹太手稿残片集合。这些文献可追溯至9世纪至19世纪，为中世纪犹太生活和圣经文本提供了无与伦比的见解。

description.en:
The Cairo Genizah was discovered in 1896 by Solomon Schechter in the Ben Ezra Synagogue in Old Cairo. A genizah is a storage room for worn-out sacred Jewish texts, which are not to be destroyed. This particular genizah had been sealed for centuries, preserving an astonishing array of documents. The bulk of the collection is now housed at Cambridge University Library and the Jewish Theological Seminary.

The collection comprises approximately 200,000 fragments, including biblical manuscripts, liturgical texts, legal documents, personal letters, and philosophical treatises. These texts are predominantly in Hebrew and Aramaic, but also Judeo-Arabic, and offer a unique glimpse into the intellectual and social life of medieval Jewry across the Middle East and North Africa.

Its significance is definitive, as it includes some of the earliest known Hebrew manuscripts of biblical and apocryphal books, such as Ecclesiasticus (Sirach), which was previously known primarily from Greek translations. The Genizah provides crucial evidence for the Masoretic Text tradition and the broader history of Jewish literature and culture.
description.zh-Hans:
开罗格尼扎于1896年由所罗门·谢赫特在开罗老城的本·以斯拉犹太会堂中发现。“格尼扎”（genizah）是用于存放破损神圣犹太文本的储藏室，这些文本不应被销毁。这个特定的格尼扎已被封存数百年，保存了数量惊人的文献。该收藏的大部分现藏于剑桥大学图书馆和犹太神学院。

该收藏包含约20万份残片，包括圣经手稿、礼仪文本、法律文件、私人信件和哲学论著。这些文本主要以希伯来语和亚拉姆语写成，也有犹太-阿拉伯语，为中世纪中东和北非犹太人的知识和社会生活提供了独特的视角。

其重要性是决定性的，因为它包含了一些已知最早的圣经和次经（如《传道经》（Sirach））的希伯来文手稿，这些书卷以前主要通过希腊文译本为人所知。格尼扎为马所拉文本传统以及犹太文学和文化的更广泛历史提供了关键证据。

scripturalCorrelation.en:
The Cairo Genizah yielded significant Hebrew fragments of the book of Ecclesiasticus (Sirach), a deuterocanonical book. Before these discoveries, the book was primarily known through its Greek Septuagint translation. The Genizah fragments confirmed the existence of a Hebrew original, shedding light on its textual history and early Jewish wisdom literature.

Ecclesiasticus (Sirach) 39:1 (NRSV): "But he who devotes himself to the study of the law of the Most High will seek out the wisdom of all the ancients, and will be concerned with prophecies."
scripturalCorrelation.zh-Hans:

《传道经》（Sirach）39:1记载：“但那专心寻求至高者律法的人，必探究古人的智慧，并关注预言。”

title.zh-Hans: 穆拉巴特洞穴古卷
title.zh-Hant: 穆拉巴特洞穴古卷

summary.en: Discovered in caves south of Qumran, the Murabba'at Scrolls are a collection of ancient texts, including biblical fragments, dating primarily from the Bar Kokhba revolt period. They provide crucial textual evidence and historical context for the 1st and 2nd centuries CE.
summary.zh-Hans: 穆拉巴特洞穴古卷是在昆兰以南的洞穴中发现的一批古代文献，包括圣经残片，主要可追溯到巴尔·科赫巴起义时期。它们为公元1世纪和2世纪提供了重要的文本证据和历史背景。
summary.zh-Hant: 穆拉巴特洞穴古卷是在昆兰以南的洞穴中发现的一批古代文献，包括圣经残片，主要可追溯到巴尔·科赫巴起义时期。它们为公元1世纪和2世纪提供了重要的文本证据和历史背景。

description.en:
The Murabba'at Scrolls were discovered in caves in Wadi Murabba'at, a desert wadi south of Qumran, during excavations conducted between 1951 and 1952. These discoveries were made by Bedouin treasure hunters and subsequently by archaeologists, following the initial finds of the Dead Sea Scrolls. The scrolls are now housed at the Israel Antiquities Authority in Jerusalem.

Unlike the Qumran scrolls, which are largely Essene, the Murabba'at texts are more diverse, including biblical fragments (e.g., Genesis, Deuteronomy, Isaiah, Psalms), legal documents, letters (including letters from Bar Kokhba himself), and administrative texts. They are primarily in Hebrew and Aramaic, with some Greek.

Their significance is definitive, as they provide important textual witnesses to the Hebrew Bible, generally conforming to the Masoretic Text tradition, thus bridging the gap between the Qumran texts and later medieval manuscripts. They also offer invaluable historical insights into the Bar Kokhba revolt (132-135 CE) and Jewish life in Judea during that tumultuous period.
description.zh-Hans:
穆拉巴特洞穴古卷于1951年至1952年间在穆拉巴特干河谷（昆兰以南的一个沙漠干河谷）的洞穴中被发现。这些发现是在死海古卷初步发现之后，由贝都因寻宝者和随后的考古学家进行的。这些古卷现藏于耶路撒冷的以色列文物管理局。

与昆兰古卷（主要属于艾赛尼派）不同，穆拉巴特文献更为多样，包括圣经残片（例如创世记、申命记、以赛亚书、诗篇）、法律文件、信件（包括巴尔·科赫巴本人的信件）和行政文本。它们主要以希伯来语和亚拉姆语写成，也有一些希腊文。

其重要性是决定性的，因为它们为希伯来圣经提供了重要的文本见证，通常符合马所拉文本传统，从而弥合了昆兰文本与后来中世纪手稿之间的鸿沟。它们还为巴尔·科赫巴起义（公元132-135年）以及那个动荡时期犹太人在犹大地的生活提供了宝贵的历史见解。

scripturalCorrelation.en:
While the Murabba'at caves yielded Old Testament fragments, the broader historical context of the Bar Kokhba revolt, evidenced by the scrolls, resonates with New Testament teachings on submission to governing authorities. The struggles of the Jewish people under Roman rule provide a backdrop for understanding early Christian perspectives on civil obedience.

Romans 13:1 (NIV): "Let everyone be subject to the governing authorities, for there is no authority except that which God has established. The authorities that exist have been established by God."

尽管穆拉巴特洞穴出土了旧约残片，但古卷所证实的巴尔·科赫巴起义的更广泛历史背景，与新约关于顺服执政掌权者的教导产生共鸣。犹太人在罗马统治下的挣扎为理解早期基督徒对公民顺服的看法提供了背景。

title.zh-Hans: 奥克西林库斯纸莎草残片
title.zh-Hant: 奥克西林库斯纸莎草残片

summary.en: The Oxyrhynchus Papyri are an extensive collection of ancient Greek papyrus fragments discovered in Egypt, containing a vast array of texts including early Christian scriptures, classical literature, and administrative documents. They offer a unique window into ancient life and biblical textual transmission.
summary.zh-Hans: 奥克西林库斯纸莎草残片是在埃及发现的大量古希腊纸莎草残片集合，包含早期基督教经文、古典文学和行政文件等各种文本。它们为古代生活和圣经文本传承提供了独特的窗口。
summary.zh-Hant: 奥克西林库斯纸莎草残片是在埃及发现的大量古希腊纸莎草残片集合，包含早期基督教经文、古典文学和行政文件等各种文本。它们为古代生活和圣经文本传承提供了独特的窗口。

description.en:
The Oxyrhynchus Papyri were discovered starting in 1897 by Bernard P. Grenfell and Arthur S. Hunt in the ancient rubbish heaps of Oxyrhynchus, Egypt. Excavations have continued for over a century, yielding hundreds of thousands of fragments. These fragments are now dispersed among various institutions, with a significant portion housed at the Bodleian Library, Oxford.

This vast collection includes fragments of biblical books (both Old and New Testaments), apocryphal gospels, early Christian writings, classical Greek literature (e.g., Sappho, Pindar, Euclid), legal documents, private letters, and official records. They are written primarily in Greek and date from the 1st century BCE to the 7th century CE.

Their significance is strong, as they provide some of the earliest known copies of New Testament books and other early Christian texts, often predating complete codices by centuries. These fragments are invaluable for textual criticism, helping scholars trace the transmission of the biblical text and understand the literary and cultural environment of early Christianity.
description.zh-Hans:
奥克西林库斯纸莎草残片于1897年开始，由伯纳德·P·格伦费尔和阿瑟·S·亨特在埃及古城奥克西林库斯的垃圾堆中发现。发掘工作已持续一个多世纪，出土了数十万份残片。这些残片现分散于各个机构，其中很大一部分收藏于牛津大学博德利图书馆。

这一庞大的收藏包括圣经书卷（旧约和新约）、次经福音书、早期基督教著作、古典希腊文学（如萨福、品达、欧几里得）、法律文件、私人信件和官方记录的残片。它们主要以希腊文写成，年代从公元前1世纪到公元7世纪。

其重要性很强，因为它们提供了一些已知最早的新约书卷和其他早期基督教文本的副本，其年代往往比完整的抄本早几个世纪。这些残片对于文本批判是无价的，有助于学者追溯圣经文本的传承并理解早期基督教的文学和文化环境。
