title.en: Azekah Inscription — Assyrian Account of Judah's Fortified Cities
title.zh-Hans: 亚西加铭文——亚述对犹大坚城的记载
title.zh-Hant: 亚西加铭文——亚述对犹大坚城的记载

summary.en: The Azekah Inscription is an Assyrian cuneiform tablet describing Sennacherib's 701 BCE campaign against Judah, specifically mentioning the siege and capture of Azekah — a fortified city listed in Joshua 10:10-11 and 2 Chronicles 11:5-12. It confirms the existence of Judah's defensive network described in the Bible.
summary.zh-Hans: 亚西加铭文是一块亚述楔形文字泥板，描述辛那赫里布公元前701年对犹大的征伐，特别提及围攻亚西加——约书亚记10:10-11和历代志下11:5-12中列出的坚固城。它证实了圣经所描述的犹大防御网络确实存在。
summary.zh-Hant: 亚西加铭文是一块亚述楔形文字泥板，描述辛那赫里布公元前701年对犹大的征伐，特别提及围攻亚西加——约书亚记10:10-11和历代志下11:5-12中列出的坚固城。它证实了圣经所描述的犹大防御网络确实存在。

description.en:
The Azekah Inscription (Azekah Text) is an Assyrian cuneiform prism fragment narrating Sennacherib's campaign against Judah in 701 BCE. It describes the siege of Azekah, a strategically important fortress guarding the Judean highlands from the coastal plain approach.

The inscription recounts how Sennacherib's army surrounded Azekah, deployed siege engines and ramps, and ultimately captured the city using standard Assyrian military terminology for conquest.

Azekah appears in multiple biblical contexts: Joshua 10:10-11 as the site where God cast hailstones on fleeing Amorite kings; 2 Chronicles 11:5-12 as one of Rehoboam's fortified cities with walls, gates, and bars; and Jeremiah 34:7 as one of the last two fortified cities holding out against Nebuchadnezzar alongside Lachish.

The Lachish Relief in the British Museum depicts the siege of Lachish — the next city after Azekah in Sennacherib's campaign — providing visual confirmation of the same military operation from both Assyrian and biblical perspectives.
description.zh-Hans:
亚西加铭文是亚述楔形文字棱柱残片，叙述辛那赫里布公元前701年对犹大的征伐。它描述亚西加的围攻——一座守卫犹大山地免受沿海平原入侵的战略要塞。铭文记载辛那赫里布的军队包围亚西加、部署攻城器械和坡道，最终使用标准的亚述军事术语描述攻城过程。

亚西加在多处圣经背景中出现：约书亚记10:10-11作为神从天上降冰雹击打逃跑的亚摩利王的地点；历代志下11:5-12作为罗波安设有城墙、城门和门闩的坚固城之一；耶利米书34:7作为与拉吉并列抵御尼布甲尼撒的最后两座坚城之一。大英博物馆的拉吉浮雕描绘了同一战役中拉吉的围攻——从亚述和圣经双方视角确认了同一军事行动。

scripturalCorrelation.en: Joshua 10:10-11 places Azekah at the site of a miraculous battle involving divine hailstones. 2 Chronicles 11:5-12 lists Azekah among Rehoboam's fortified defenses. The Assyrian inscription confirms this was indeed a major fortified site requiring a full siege — validating the biblical description of Judah's southern defensive network and the city's strategic importance.

title.en: Jehucal Seal — Bulla of the Official Named in Jeremiah 37:3
title.zh-Hans: 犹甲封印——耶利米书37:3所载官员的封泥
title.zh-Hant: 犹甲封印——耶利米书37:3所载官员的封泥

This directly matches Jeremiah 37:3 and 38:1, which name 'Jehucal son of Shelemiah' as a royal official during Zedekiah's reign — providing another archaeological confirmation of a specific biblical individual.

description.en:
The Jehucal bulla was discovered by Eilat Mazar during her City of David excavations in 2005. It reads in paleo-Hebrew: 'l-yhwkl bn šlmyhw' — 'Belonging to Jehucal son of Shelemiah.'

Biblical references:

Jeremiah 37:3: King Zedekiah sent 'Jehucal son of Shelemiah and the priest Zephaniah' to Jeremiah, asking him to pray for the nation.

Jeremiah 38:1: 'Shephatiah son of Mattan, and Gedaliah son of Pashhur, and Jehucal son of Shelemiah, and Pashhur son of Malchiah' — four officials who opposed Jeremiah.

Significance:

(1) The bulla was found in the Large Stone Structure area of the City of David, the administrative heart of pre-exilic Jerusalem — exactly where royal officials would have operated.

(2) The bulla dates to the late 7th-early 6th century BCE, matching Zedekiah's reign (597-586 BCE).

(3) Together with the Gedaliah bulla (found nearby), two of the four officials named in Jeremiah 38:1 have been archaeologically confirmed.

(4) The name Jehucal (Yhwkl) is a theophoric name containing the divine element Yhw (Yahweh), consistent with Judahite naming conventions of the period.

(5) This find, along with the Baruch bulla and the Gemariah bulla, demonstrates that the Jeremiah narrative features real, verifiable historical individuals operating in the specific administrative context described in the text.

圣经出处：耶利米书37:3：西底家王差遣「示利米雅的儿子犹甲和祭司西番雅」去见耶利米，请他为国祈祷。耶利米书38:1：「玛坦的儿子示法提雅、巴施户珥的儿子基大利、示利米雅的儿子犹甲、玛基雅的儿子巴施户珥」——四位反对耶利米的官员。

summary.en: A clay bulla (seal impression) reading 'Belonging to Gedaliah son of Pashhur' was discovered in the City of David, Jerusalem. This directly matches Jeremiah 38:1, which names 'Gedaliah son of Pashhur' as one of the officials who opposed Jeremiah and sought his death during Zedekiah's reign.

description.en:
The Gedaliah bulla was discovered during Eilat Mazar's excavations in the City of David. It reads in paleo-Hebrew: 'l-gdlyhw bn pshwr' — 'Belonging to Gedaliah son of Pashhur.'

Jeremiah 38:1-6 names 'Shephatiah son of Mattan, and Gedaliah son of Pashhur, and Jucal son of Shelemiah, and Pashhur son of Malchiah' as the officials who heard Jeremiah's prophecies of Jerusalem's fall and demanded his execution. King Zedekiah allowed them to throw Jeremiah into a cistern.

Significance:

(1) This bulla, along with the Jehucal seal (also found in the City of David), names two of the four officials in Jeremiah 38:1 — providing direct archaeological confirmation of specific individuals named in the biblical text.

(2) The bulla dates to the late 7th-early 6th century BCE, precisely the period of Jeremiah's ministry and Zedekiah's reign (597-586 BCE).

(3) The findspot in the City of David — the administrative center of pre-exilic Jerusalem — is consistent with where royal officials would have operated.

(4) The paleo-Hebrew script on the bulla matches other authenticated 7th-6th century BCE seal impressions from Jerusalem.

Together with the Jehucal seal and the Baruch seal (also found in Jerusalem), the Gedaliah bulla forms part of a remarkable convergence of archaeology and the Jeremiah narrative.
description.zh-Hans:
基大利封泥是在埃拉特·马扎尔的大卫城发掘中发现的。上面以古希伯来文写着「l-gdlyhw bn pshwr」——「基大利 son of 巴施户珥所有」。

耶利米书38:1-6记载「玛坦的儿子示法提雅、巴施户珥的儿子基大利、示利米雅的儿子犹甲、玛基雅的儿子巴施户珥」是听见耶利米预言耶路撒冷沦陷后要求处死他的官员。西底家王允许他们将耶利米投入蓄水池。

重要意义：（1）这枚封泥与犹甲印章（同样在大卫城发现）一起，点名了耶利米书38:1四位官员中的两位——提供了圣经文本中具体个人的直接考古确认。（2）封泥定年为公元前7世纪末至6世纪初，恰为耶利米事工和西底家统治时期（公元前597-586年）。（3）发现地点在大卫城——被掳前耶路撒冷的行政中心——与王室官员活动区域一致。（4）封泥上的古希伯来文字与耶路撒冷已认证的公元前7-6世纪封印一致。

与犹甲封泥和巴录封泥（同样在耶路撒冷发现）一起，基大利封泥构成了考古学与耶利米叙事显著汇合的一部分。

title.zh-Hans: 亚拉得陶片——犹大军事通信
title.zh-Hant: 亚拉得陶片——犹大军事通信

summary.en: The Arad ostraca, excavated from the Judahite fortress at Arad (1962-1967), comprise over 100 inscribed potsherds from the 7th-6th centuries BCE. These administrative and military letters mention biblical names, priestly families, and supply logistics that correspond directly to the biblical description of Judah's southern frontier defenses in 2 Chronicles 11:5-12.
summary.zh-Hans: 亚拉得陶片于1962-1967年在犹大要塞亚拉得发掘出土，包含100多片铭文陶片，年代为公元前7-6世纪。这些行政和军事信件提及圣经人物名、祭司家族和后勤供应，直接对应历代志下11:5-12对犹大南部边境防御的描述。
summary.zh-Hant: 亚拉得陶片于1962-1967年在犹大要塞亚拉得发掘出土，包含100多片铭文陶片，年代为公元前7-6世纪。这些行政和军事信件提及圣经人物名、祭司家族和后勤供应，直接对应历代志下11:5-12对犹大南部边境防御的描述。

description.en:
The Arad ostraca were discovered during Yohanan Aharoni's excavations at Tel Arad, a strategic fortress on Judah's southern frontier. The approximately 100+ inscribed potsherds (ostraca) date primarily to the 7th-early 6th centuries BCE.

Key findings:

(1) Military correspondence: Many ostraca are letters between the fortress commander and his superiors in Jerusalem, requesting supplies, reporting troop movements, and coordinating defenses against Edomite incursions.

(2) Biblical names: The ostraca mention individuals with Yahwistic names (containing the divine element -yahu/-yah), confirming the prevalence of Yahweh worship in Judah. Names include Pashhur and Meremoth, also found in biblical texts.

(3) Priestly allocation lists: Arad Ostracon 40 lists allocations to various priests and the 'house of YHWH' (beit yhwh) — one of the earliest extra-biblical references to the Jerusalem Temple.

(4) Administrative terminology: Terms used in the ostraca parallel biblical Hebrew administrative vocabulary, including measures (bath, homer), military units (hundreds), and supply categories.

(5) Geographic accuracy: The fortress network described matches the biblical description of Rehoboam's fortified cities in 2 Chronicles 11:5-12, which lists Arad among the defenses.
description.zh-Hans:
亚拉得陶片是在约哈南·阿哈罗尼对Tel Arad的发掘中发现的，这是犹大南部边境的战略要塞。约100多片铭文陶片年代主要为公元前7至6世纪初。

主要发现：

（1）军事通信：许多陶片是要塞指挥官与其耶路撒冷上级之间的信件，请求补给、报告军队调动和协调对以东入侵的防御。

（2）圣经人名：陶片提及带有耶和华名字元素（-yahu/-yah）的个人，确认犹大耶和华崇拜的普遍性。名字包括帕述和麦利末，也见于圣经文本。

（3）祭司分配清单：亚拉得陶片40号列出对各祭司和「YHWH的家」（beit yhwh）的分配——最早的圣经外耶路撒冷圣殿引用之一。

（4）行政术语：陶片中使用的术语与圣经希伯来文行政词汇平行。

（5）地理准确性：描述的要塞网络与圣经历代志下11:5-12中罗波安坚固城的描述吻合。

title.en: Sargon II's Palace at Khorsabad — Confirming Isaiah 20:1
title.zh-Hans: 萨尔贡二世在霍尔萨巴德的宫殿——确认以赛亚书20:1
title.zh-Hant: 萨尔贡二世在霍尔萨巴德的宫殿——确认以赛亚书20:1

summary.en: The palace of Assyrian King Sargon II at Khorsabad (Dur-Sharrukin), discovered by Paul-Émile Botta in 1843, was the first Assyrian palace excavated. Isaiah 20:1 uniquely names Sargon — a king who was unknown outside the Bible until this discovery, leading critics to claim he was fictional. The palace discovery vindicated Isaiah's historical accuracy.
summary.zh-Hans: 亚述王萨尔贡二世在霍尔萨巴德（杜尔沙鲁金）的宫殿由保罗-埃米尔·博塔于1843年发现，是第一座被发掘的亚述宫殿。以赛亚书20:1独特地提到了萨尔贡——这位国王在圣经之外不为人知直到这一发现，导致批评者声称他是虚构的。宫殿的发现证明了以赛亚的历史准确性。

description.en:
Isaiah 20:1 states: 'In the year that the supreme commander, sent by Sargon king of Assyria, came to Ashdod and attacked and captured it.' For centuries, Sargon was known only from this single biblical reference — no other ancient source mentioned him. Critics claimed Isaiah had invented the name.

The discovery:

(1) In 1843, Paul-Émile Botta, the French consul in Mosul, began excavating at Khorsabad, about 15 km north of Nineveh. He uncovered the palace of Sargon II (722-705 BCE), whom he called 'Sargon' (Šarru-kīn, meaning 'the king is legitimate').

(2) The palace at Dur-Sharrukin ('Fort Sargon') was enormous — covering about 25 acres with over 200 rooms and courtyards. Its walls were covered with bas-reliefs depicting military campaigns, including the siege of a city identified as Ashdod — precisely the event described in Isaiah 20:1.

(3) Sargon's annals, found at the palace, record: 'I besieged and conquered Ashdod… I took his royal city… I counted as spoil the gods who were in it' — directly confirming Isaiah's reference to Sargon's campaign against Ashdod.

(4) Sargon's inscriptions also record the fall of Samaria (722 BCE) and the deportation of Israelites — confirming 2 Kings 17:1-6.

(5) The palace was built between 717-706 BCE and abandoned after Sargon's death in battle in 705 BCE.

This discovery transformed Sargon from a 'fictional biblical character' into one of the most documented Assyrian kings — a powerful illustration of how archaeology has repeatedly vindicated the Bible against its critics.
description.zh-Hans:
以赛亚书20:1记载：「亚述王撒珥根打发他珥探到亚实突的那年，他珥探就到了亚实突，攻战了它。」几个世纪以来，萨尔贡仅从这一处圣经参考为人所知——没有其他古代来源提及他。批评者声称以赛亚编造了这个名字。

发现：（1）1843年，法国驻摩苏尔领事保罗-埃米尔·博塔开始在霍尔萨巴德发掘，位于尼尼微以北约15公里。他发掘了萨尔贡二世（公元前722-705年）的宫殿，他称之为「萨尔贡」（Šarru-kīn，意为「王是正统的」）。（2）杜尔沙鲁金（「萨尔贡堡垒」）的宫殿巨大——占地约25英亩，有200多个房间和庭院。墙壁上覆盖着描绘军事行动的浮雕，包括围攻一座被认定为亚实突的城市——正是以赛亚书20:1描述的事件。（3）在宫殿发现的萨尔贡年鉴记载：「我围攻并征服了亚实突……我夺取了他的王城……我将其中的神明算作战利品」——直接确认了以赛亚提到的萨尔贡对亚实突的战役。（4）萨尔功的铭文还记录了撒玛利亚的沦陷（公元前722年）和以色列人的被掳——确认了列王纪下17:1-6。（5）宫殿建于公元前717-706年，在萨尔贡公元前705年战死后被废弃。

这一发现将萨尔贡从「虚构的圣经人物」变成了有最充分文献记录的亚述王之一——有力地说明了考古学如何反复为圣经辩护，反驳批评者。

title.en: Tell al-Rimah Stele — Assyrian Confirmation of Jehoash of Israel
title.zh-Hans: 泰勒里迈赫石碑——亚述文献确认以色列王约阿施
title.zh-Hant: 泰勒里迈赫石碑——亚述文献确认以色列王约阿施

summary.en: Discovered in 1967 at Tell al-Rimah in northern Iraq, this Assyrian stela of Adad-Nirari III (810-783 BCE) mentions 'Jehoash the Samarian' and records tribute from the Israelite king — independently confirming the existence of King Jehoash of Israel (2 Kings 13:10-25) and the Assyrian interest in the region described in the biblical narrative.
summary.zh-Hans: 1967年在伊拉克北部的泰勒里迈赫发现的亚述石碑，由亚述王阿达德尼拉里三世（公元前810-783年）所立，其中提到「撒玛利亚人约阿施」并记录了从以色列王收取贡品——独立证实了以色列王约阿施的存在（列王纪下13:10-25），以及圣经叙述中描述的亚述对该地区的关注。
summary.zh-Hant: 1967年在伊拉克北部的泰勒里迈赫发现的亚述石碑，由亚述王阿达德尼拉里三世（公元前810-783年）所立，其中提到「撒玛利亚人约阿施」并记录了从以色列王收取贡品——独立证实了以色列王约阿施的存在（列王纪下13:10-25），以及圣经叙述中描述的亚述对该地区的关注。

description.en:
The Tell al-Rimah Stele was discovered in 1967 at the site of ancient Karana (modern Tell al-Rimah) in northern Iraq. It is a stone monument commissioned by the Assyrian king Adad-Nirari III (810-783 BCE).

The stele records military campaigns into the western territories and lists tribute received from vassal kings, including 'Jehoash the Samarian' (Iu'asu samerinau). This directly corresponds to King Jehoash (Joash) of Israel, who reigned in Samaria as described in 2 Kings 13:10-25.

Key correlations:

(1) The stele confirms the existence of an Israelite king named Jehoash ruling from Samaria — matching the biblical account precisely.

(2) It attests to Assyrian military pressure on the kingdoms of Israel and Syria, consistent with the biblical narrative of 2 Kings in which Assyrian campaigns provide the backdrop for the ministries of Elisha and the political struggles of Israel.

(3) The tribute amount recorded (gold, silver, tin, and other goods) demonstrates the wealth and political significance of the kingdom of Israel, contradicting minimalist claims that Israel was merely a minor tribal entity.

(4) The stele also mentions Mari', ruler of Damascus, correlating with the Aramean (Syrian) kingdom frequently mentioned in the books of Kings.

This stele joins the Kurkh Monolith, the Black Obelisk, and the Mesha Stele as another Assyrian inscription independently confirming Israelite kings named in the Bible.
description.zh-Hans:
泰勒里迈赫石碑于1967年在伊拉克北部古代卡拉纳（今泰勒里迈赫）遗址被发现。这是一块由亚述王阿达德尼拉里三世（公元前810-783年）下令刻立的石碑。

石碑记录了向西域的军事远征，并列出从附庸国王收取的贡品，其中包括「撒玛利亚人约阿施」（Iu'asu samerinau）。这直接对应列王纪下13:10-25中所描述的在撒玛利亚作王的以色列王约阿施。

主要关联：（1）石碑确认了一位名为约阿施的以色列王从撒玛利亚统治——与圣经记载完全吻合。

（2）它证明了亚述对以色列和叙利亚王国施加的军事压力，与列王纪中以利亚沙的事工和以色列政治斗争为背景的亚述远征叙述一致。

（3）记录的贡品数量（金、银、锡及其他货物）表明以色列王国具有相当的财富和政治重要性，反驳了将以色列视为微小部落实体的极简主义主张。

（4）石碑还提到了大马士革的统治者马里'，与列王纪中频繁提及的亚兰（叙利亚）王国相对应。

此石碑与库尔赫石碑、黑色方尖碑和米沙石碑并列，成为又一块独立确认圣经中以色列国王的亚述铭文。

scripturalCorrelation.en: 2 Kings 13:10-25 describes the reign of King Jehoash (Joash) of Israel, who reigned in Samaria. The Tell al-Rimah Stele independently attests to 'Jehoash the Samarian' paying tribute to Assyria, confirming the biblical king's existence and the geopolitical context of Assyrian pressure on Israel described throughout the books of Kings.
scripturalCorrelation.zh-Hans: 列王纪下13:10-25描述了以色列王约阿施在撒玛利亚的统治。泰勒里迈赫石碑独立证实了「撒玛利亚人约阿施」向亚述缴纳贡品，确认了这位圣经国王的存在，以及列王纪中描述的亚述对以色列施压的地缘政治背景。

title.en: Nimrud Tablet K3751 — Tiglath-Pileser III and the Kingdom of Israel
title.zh-Hans: 尼姆鲁德泥版K3751——提格拉特毗列色三世与以色列王国
title.zh-Hant: 尼姆鲁德泥版K3751——提格拉特毗列色三世与以色列王国

summary.en: The Nimrud Tablet (K3751), an Assyrian cuneiform inscription of Tiglath-Pileser III (745-727 BCE), mentions 'Menahem of Samaria' paying tribute — directly confirming 2 Kings 15:19-20 which records Menahem paying Pul (Tiglath-Pileser) a thousand talents of silver to confirm his kingship.
summary.zh-Hans: 尼姆鲁德泥版（K3751），亚述王提格拉特毗列色三世（公元前745-727年）的楔形文字铭文，提到「撒玛利亚的米拿现」进贡——直接确认了列王纪下15:19-20记载米拿现向普勒（提格拉特毗列色）缴纳一千他连得银子以确认王位的事。
summary.zh-Hant: 尼姆鲁德泥版（K3751），亚述王提格拉特毗列色三世（公元前745-727年）的楔形文字铭文，提到「撒玛利亚的米拿现」进贡——直接确认了列王纪下15:19-20记载米拿现向普勒（提格拉特毗列色）缴纳一千他连得银子以确认王位的事。

description.en:
Tablet K3751 is one of several Assyrian inscriptions from Nimrud (ancient Kalhu) that record the campaigns and tributes received by Tiglath-Pileser III.

Key content:

(1) The inscription lists 'Menahem of Samaria' (Mi-in-hi-im-me ir Sa-me-ri-na-a) among rulers who paid tribute to Tiglath-Pileser III.

(2) Biblical correlation: 2 Kings 15:19-20 states: 'Pul king of Assyria invaded the land, and Menahem gave Pul a thousand talents of silver to gain his support and strengthen his own hold on the kingdom. Menahem exacted this money from Israel. Every wealthy person had to contribute fifty shekels of silver.'

(3) 'Pul' is the personal name by which Tiglath-Pileser III was known in Israel — confirmed by the Babylonian Chronicle which records that Tiglath-Pileser assumed the throne name 'Pulu' when he became king of Babylon.

Significance:

(4) The tribute amount in the Bible (1,000 talents of silver) is consistent with the scale of tribute recorded in Assyrian annals for minor kingdoms.

(5) Menahem's payment of 50 shekels per wealthy Israelite (2 Kings 15:20) reflects a specific taxation policy that is historically plausible for raising such a large sum.

(6) The inscription confirms the political situation described in 2 Kings: Israel as a vulnerable kingdom caught between Assyrian expansion and local power struggles.

(7) This is part of a broader pattern where Assyrian records confirm biblical accounts of Israelite and Judahite kings: Ahab (Kurkh Monolith), Jehu (Black Obelisk), Hoshea (annals of Shalmaneser V), Hezekiah (Sennacherib's Prism).
description.zh-Hans:
泥版K3751是尼姆鲁德（古代迦勒）发现的记录提格拉特毗列色三世征战和收到的贡品的亚述铭文之一。

关键内容：（1）铭文列出向提格拉特毗列色三世进贡的统治者中有「撒玛利亚的米拿现」（Mi-in-hi-im-me ir Sa-me-ri-na-a）。（2）圣经对应：列王纪下15:19-20记载：「亚述王普勒来攻击这地，米拿现给普勒一千他连得银子，请普勒帮助他坚定国位。米拿现向以色列一切富户索要银子，使他们各出五十舍客勒。」（3）「普勒」是以色列人对提格拉特毗列色三世的个人名——巴比伦年代记确认提格拉特毗列色成为巴比伦王时采用了王号「普鲁」。

重要意义：（4）圣经中的贡品金额（一千他连得银子）与亚述年鉴中记录的小国贡品规模一致。（5）米拿现向以色列每位富人征收50舍客勒（王下15:20）反映了筹集如此巨款的具体税收政策，在历史上是合理的。（6）铭文确认了列王纪下描述的政治局势：以色列作为一个夹在亚述扩张和当地权力斗争之间的脆弱王国。（7）这是一个更广泛模式的一部分：亚述记录确认了圣经中以色列和犹大君王的记载：亚哈（库尔赫石碑）、耶户（黑色方尖碑）、何细亚（撒缦以色五世年鉴）、希西家（西拿基立棱柱）。

scripturalCorrelation.en: 2 Kings 15:19-20 records Menahem of Israel paying tribute to 'Pul king of Assyria' to secure his throne. The Nimrud Tablet K3751 independently mentions 'Menahem of Samaria' paying tribute to Tiglath-Pileser III (Pul). This direct cuneiform confirmation validates the biblical account of Israel's subjugation to Assyria in the 8th century BCE.
scripturalCorrelation.zh-Hans: 列王纪下15:19-20记载以色列的米拿现向「亚述王普勒」进贡以稳固王位。尼姆鲁德泥版K3751独立提到「撒玛利亚的米拿现」向提格拉特毗列色三世（普勒）进贡。这一直接的楔形文字确认验证了圣经关于公元前8世纪以色列臣服亚述的记载。

title.en: Stele of Zakkur — Aramean Kingdom Confirmed
title.zh-Hans: 扎库尔石碑——亚兰王国获确认
title.zh-Hant: 扎库尔石碑——亚兰王国获确认

summary.en: Discovered in 1903 at Tell Afis near Aleppo, the Stele of Zakkur commemorates King Zakkur of Hamath and Lu'ash, who was besieged by a coalition of Aramean kings led by Ben-Hadad. This inscription independently confirms the Aramean kingdom and the name Ben-Hadad (Bar-Hadad) found in 2 Kings 8:7-15 and 1 Kings 20.
summary.zh-Hans: 1903年在阿勒颇附近的泰勒阿菲斯发现的扎库尔石碑，纪念哈马和卢阿什国王扎库尔被以便哈达为首的亚兰王联盟围攻。此铭文独立确认了列王纪下8:7-15和列王纪上20中提到的亚兰王国和便哈达之名。
summary.zh-Hant: 1903年在阿勒颇附近的泰勒阿菲斯发现的扎库尔石碑，纪念哈马和卢阿什国王扎库尔被以便哈达为首的亚兰王联盟围攻。此铭文独立确认了列王纪下8:7-15和列王纪上20中提到的亚兰王国和便哈达之名。

description.en:
The Stele of Zakkur was discovered in 1903 at Tell Afis (ancient Hatarikka) in Syria, about 45 km southwest of Aleppo. It is a basalt stela inscribed in Aramaic, dating to approximately 800 BCE.

The stele records King Zakkur of Hamath and Lu'ash describing how a coalition of northern kings — led by 'Bar-Hadad, son of Hazael, king of Aram' — besieged him but failed to conquer his city. Zakkur credits his deliverance to his god Baal-Shamayn.

Key biblical correlations:

(1) The name 'Bar-Hadad' (Ben-Hadad in Hebrew) matches the Aramean king mentioned in 2 Kings 8:7-15 and 1 Kings 20. 'Bar' and 'Ben' both mean 'son' in Aramaic and Hebrew respectively.

(2) 'Hazael' is named as Bar-Hadad's father — the same Hazael who is a major figure in 2 Kings 8-13. Hazael seized the throne of Damascus and became one of Israel's most dangerous enemies.

(3) The stele describes a coalition of kings including those from Sam'al, Que, and other city-states — painting a picture of the fragmented Syro-Palestinian political landscape described in the books of Kings.

(4) The practice of kings forming coalitions against common enemies reflects the political dynamics seen throughout 1-2 Kings.

The stele is significant because it provides an Aramean perspective on events also described in the Bible, showing that the biblical authors were recording real geopolitical events with accurate names and relationships.
description.zh-Hans:
扎库尔石碑于1903年在叙利亚泰勒阿菲斯（古代哈塔里卡）被发现，位于阿勒颇西南约45公里处。这是一块用亚兰语刻写的玄武岩石碑，年代约在公元前800年。

石碑记录了哈马和卢阿什国王扎库尔描述北方诸王联盟——由「亚兰王哈薛之子巴尔哈达」率领——围攻他但未能攻陷其城。扎库尔将获救归功于其神明巴尔沙马因。

与圣经的关键关联：（1）「巴尔哈达」（希伯来语中为便哈达）与列王纪下8:7-15和列王纪上20中提到的亚兰王同名。「巴尔」和「便」在亚兰语和希伯来语中分别意为「儿子」。

（2）哈薛被命名为巴尔哈达的父亲——与列王纪下8-13中的重要人物哈薛相同。哈薛夺取了大马士革王位，成为以色列最危险的敌人之一。

（3）石碑描述了包括撒马尔、奎和其他城邦在内的诸王联盟——呈现了列王纪中所描述的分裂的叙利亚-巴勒斯坦政治格局。

（4）诸王联合对抗共同敌人的做法反映了列王纪上-下列王纪中的政治动态。

此石碑的重要性在于它提供了一个亚兰视角的事件记述——与圣经描述的相同事件——表明圣经作者在记录真实的地缘政治事件，人名和关系准确无误。

title.en: Khirbet Qeiyafa Ostracon — 10th Century BCE Hebrew Inscription
title.zh-Hans: 基尔贝特·基亚法陶片——公元前10世纪的希伯来铭文
title.zh-Hant: 基尔贝特·基亚法陶片——公元前10世纪的希伯来铭文

summary.en: A 15 x 16.5 cm ostracon (inscribed potsherd) discovered at Khirbet Qeiyafa in 2008, dated to c. 1000 BCE, contains a five-line inscription in proto-Canaanite/early Hebrew script. Scholars debate its translation, but it appears to contain legal or literary language — potentially the oldest Hebrew inscription ever found, from the period of David's kingdom.
summary.zh-Hans: 2008年在基尔贝特·基亚法发现的一块15×16.5厘米的陶片（铭文陶片），定年约公元前1000年，包含五行原始迦南/早期希伯来文字。学者对其翻译有争议，但似乎包含法律或文学语言——可能是迄今为止发现的最早希伯来铭文，来自大卫王国时期。
summary.zh-Hant: 2008年在基尔贝特·基亚法发现的一块15×16.5厘米的陶片（铭文陶片），定年约公元前1000年，包含五行原始迦南/早期希伯来文字。学者对其翻译有争议，但似乎包含法律或文学语言——可能是迄今为止发现的最早希伯来铭文，来自大卫王国时期。

description.en:
The Khirbet Qeiyafa ostracon was discovered during excavations led by Yosef Garfinkel and Saar Ganor at a fortified city overlooking the Elah Valley — the site of David's battle with Goliath (1 Samuel 17).

Key findings:

(1) The inscription, dated to c. 1000 BCE (Iron IIA), predates most known Hebrew inscriptions by 200-300 years. Radiocarbon dating of olive pits from the same layer confirmed the 10th century date.

(2) The site's strategic location overlooking the Elah Valley, on the border between Judah and Philistia, matches the geopolitical situation described in 1 Samuel.

(3) The city features a casemate wall with a distinctive architectural style (the 'Qeiyafa style') not found in Philistine cities but comparable to later Judahite construction, suggesting cultural affiliation with early Judah/Israel.

(4) The inscription itself: While full translation is debated, scholars including Emile Puech and Ada Yardeni have identified possible legal or administrative language. Haggai Misgav reads terms related to servant/slave administration. Gershon Galil proposed it contains social justice injunctions paralleling biblical law.

(5) Dietary evidence: No pig bones were found at the site — consistent with Judahite (kosher) practice but distinguishing it from nearby Philistine sites.

(6) Whether or not the inscription is Hebrew, it demonstrates literacy in the Judah/Philistine border region during the 10th century BCE — the period of the United Monarchy.
description.zh-Hans:
基尔贝特·基亚法陶片是在约瑟夫·加芬克尔和萨尔·加诺尔领导的发掘中发现的，遗址是俯瞰以拉谷的一座设防城市——大卫与歌利亚之战的地点（撒上17章）。

关键发现：（1）铭文定年约公元前1000年（铁器IIA期），比大多数已知希伯来铭文早200-300年。同一地层的橄榄核放射性碳测年确认了公元前10世纪的日期。（2）遗址战略位置俯瞰以拉谷，位于犹大与 Philistia 的边界，与撒母耳记上描述的地缘政治态势吻合。（3）城市拥有间隔城墙，具有独特建筑风格（「基亚法式」），在 Philistine 城市中未发现，但与后来的犹大建筑可比，表明与早期犹大/以色列的文化联系。（4）铭文本身：虽然完整翻译仍有争议，但学者包括埃米尔·普克和阿达·雅迪尼已识别出可能的法律或行政语言。米斯加夫读到了与仆人/奴隶管理相关的术语。加利尔提出它包含与圣经律法平行的社会正义命令。（5）饮食证据：遗址未发现猪骨——与犹大（洁净）饮食习惯一致，区别于附近的 Philistine 遗址。（6）无论铭文是否为希伯来文，它都证明了公元前10世纪——统一王国时期——犹大/Philistine边境地区已存在文字书写能力。

scripturalCorrelation.en: 1 Samuel 17 places David's battle with Goliath in the Elah Valley, precisely where Khirbet Qeiyafa sits. The site's 10th century BCE fortification, possible Hebrew inscription, and cultural distinctiveness from Philistine sites provide archaeological context for a literate Judahite presence in David's time — supporting the historicity of the early monarchy.
scripturalCorrelation.zh-Hans: 撒母耳记上17章将大卫与歌利亚的战斗定在以拉谷——正是基尔贝特·基亚法所在地。该遗址公元前10世纪的设防、可能的希伯来铭文以及与 Philistine 遗址的文化差异，为大卫时期犹大地区存在有文字的定居点提供了考古背景——支持早期君主国的历史性。

Meshorer, Ya'akov. A Treasury of Jewish Coins. Yad Ben-Zvi Press, 2001.

title.en: Pilate Coins — Numismatic Evidence for the Prefect of Judea
title.zh-Hans: 彼拉多钱币——犹大巡抚的钱币学证据
title.zh-Hant: 彼拉多钱币——犹大巡抚的钱币学证据

summary.en: Coins minted under Pontius Pilate (26-36 CE) in Jerusalem bear his name and distinctive symbols (lituus staff, simpulum ladle). These coins provide independent, contemporary physical evidence for Pilate's rule as prefect of Judea — the very Roman official who sentenced Jesus to crucifixion according to all four Gospels.
summary.zh-Hans: 本丢彼拉多在耶路撒冷铸造的钱币（公元26-36年）上刻有他的名字和独特的符号（占卜杖、祭司勺）。这些钱币为彼拉多作为犹大巡抚的统治提供了独立的、当代的实物证据——正是四部福音书所记载的判处耶稣钉十字架的罗马官员。
summary.zh-Hant: 本丢彼拉多在耶路撒冷铸造的钱币（公元26-36年）上刻有他的名字和独特的符号（占卜杖、祭司勺）。这些钱币为彼拉多作为犹大巡抚的统治提供了独立的、当代的实物证据——正是四部福音书所记载的判处耶稣钉十字架的罗马官员。

description.en:
Pontius Pilate, as prefect of Judea (26-36 CE), minted coins in Jerusalem bearing his name (in Greek: ΠΙΛΑΤΟΣ) and regnal year dates. Two main types are known:

(1) Lituus type (Year 30-31 CE): Features a lituus (augur's staff or curved wand) on the reverse, with the inscription 'TIBERIOY KAICAPOC' (of Tiberius Caesar) and 'LIZ' or 'LIH' indicating year 17 or 18 of Tiberius.

(2) Simpulum type (Year 32-33 CE): Features a simpulum (Roman priestly ladle) on the reverse, with date 'LIA' or 'LIB' for years 16-17 of Tiberius.

Significance:

(3) The coins confirm Pilate as the Roman administrator in Jerusalem during the period when Jesus was crucified (c. 30-33 CE).

(4) The use of pagan Roman religious symbols (lituus, simpulum) on coins minted in Jerusalem would have been offensive to Jews — consistent with Philo's and Josephus's descriptions of Pilate's insensitivity to Jewish religious sensibilities.

(5) The coins bear the name of Tiberius, not Pilate himself — standard practice for Roman provincial coinage where local governors minted in the emperor's name.

(6) These coins, combined with the Pilate Stone (discovered at Caesarea in 1961), provide both numismatic and epigraphic evidence for the historical Pilate — independent archaeological confirmation of the man who features so prominently in the Passion narratives.
description.zh-Hans:
本丢彼拉多作为犹大巡抚（公元26-36年），在耶路撒冷铸造了刻有他名字（希腊文：ΠΙΛΑΤΟΣ）和摄政年份日期的钱币。已知有两种主要类型：

（1）占卜杖型（公元30-31年）：反面有占卜杖（占卜者的弯曲权杖），铭文「TIBERIOY KAICAPOC」（提庇留凯撒）和「LIZ」或「LIH」表示提庇留第17或18年。（2）祭司勺型（公元32-33年）：反面有祭司勺（罗马祭司用的勺子），日期「LIA」或「LIB」表示提庇留第16-17年。

重要意义：（3）钱币确认彼拉多在耶稣被钉十字架期间（约公元30-33年）是耶路撒冷的罗马行政官。（4）在耶路撒冷铸造的钱币上使用异教罗马宗教符号（占卜杖、祭司勺）会冒犯犹太人——与斐洛和约瑟夫描述的彼拉多对犹太宗教情感的不敏感一致。（5）钱币上刻的是提庇留的名字，而非彼拉多本人——这是罗马行省钱币的标准做法，地方总督以皇帝名义铸造。（6）这些钱币与彼拉多石碑（1961年在凯撒利亚发现）一起，为历史上的彼拉多提供了钱币学和铭文学的双重证据——对四福音书中突出出现的罗马官员的独立考古确认。

scripturalCorrelation.en: Matthew 27:2 identifies Pontius Pilate as the governor who sentenced Jesus. The coins minted in Jerusalem bearing Pilate's name during 26-36 CE provide contemporary physical evidence of his administration. Combined with the Pilate Stone from Caesarea (1961), these offer independent archaeological confirmation of the Roman official at the center of Jesus' trial.

title.en: Herodium Palace — Herod's Fortress and Tomb
title.zh-Hans: 希律堡宫殿——希律大帝的堡垒和陵墓
title.zh-Hant: 希律堡宫殿——希律大帝的堡垒和陵墓

summary.en: Herodium, Herod the Great's palace-fortress southeast of Bethlehem, was built in the 1st century BCE and is where Matthew 2:1-19 places Herod when the Magi visited. Ehud Netzer discovered Herod's tomb here in 2007 after decades of searching, confirming Josephus's description of Herod's burial at Herodium.
summary.zh-Hans: 希律堡是希律大帝在伯利恒东南建造的宫殿堡垒，建于公元前1世纪，马太福音2:1-19将希律置于东方博士来访时的地点。2007年埃胡德·内策在数十年搜寻后发现了希律的陵墓，证实了约瑟夫关于希律葬于希律堡的描述。
summary.zh-Hant: 希律堡是希律大帝在伯利恒东南建造的宫殿堡垒，建于公元前1世纪，马太福音2:1-19将希律置于东方博士来访时的地点。2007年埃胡德·内策在数十年搜寻后发现了希律的陵墓，证实了约瑟夫关于希律葬于希律堡的描述。

description.en:
Herodium (Horad Hordus) is a volcano-shaped palace-fortress built by Herod the Great (c. 23-15 BCE) on the edge of the Judean Desert, about 12 km southeast of Jerusalem and 6 km southeast of Bethlehem.

Archaeological evidence:

(1) Palace complex: Herodium combined a luxurious palace with a defensive fortress, including a theater, bathhouse, dining rooms, and extensive gardens — one of Herod's most ambitious building projects.

(2) Matthew 2:1-19 places Herod in Jerusalem/Bethlehem when the Magi arrived seeking 'the king of the Jews.' Herodium, visible from Bethlehem, was one of Herod's primary residences.

(3) Herod's Tomb (2007): Ehud Netzer of Hebrew University discovered Herod's mausoleum on the northeastern slope of Herodium after 35 years of searching. The elaborate tomb included a broken sarcophagus made of reddish limestone (jerusalem stone), consistent with Josephus's description of Herod's burial.

(4) The Roman-style theater (seating about 400) was built for Herod's visit by Marcus Agrippa (Augustus's son-in-law) in 15 BCE, confirming Herod's close relationship with Rome.

(5) Administrative buildings and mikva'ot (ritual baths) indicate continuous occupation through the First Jewish Revolt (66-73 CE) and the Bar Kokhba Revolt (132-135 CE).
description.zh-Hans:
希律堡（Horad Hordus）是希律大帝（约公元前23-15年）在犹大沙漠边缘建造的火山形宫殿堡垒，位于耶路撒冷东南约12公里、伯利恒东南约6公里处。

考古证据：（1）宫殿建筑群：希律堡将奢华宫殿与防御堡垒结合，包括剧场、浴场、餐厅和广阔花园——是希律最雄心勃勃的建筑工程之一。（2）马太福音2:1-19将希律置于耶路撒冷/伯利恒，当东方博士来寻找「犹太人之王」时。从伯利恒可以看见希律堡，是希律的主要居所之一。（3）希律陵墓（2007年）：希伯来大学的埃胡德·内策在希律堡东北坡搜寻35年后发现了希律的陵墓。精美的陵墓包含一个破碎的红石灰石（耶路撒冷石）石棺，与约瑟夫描述的希律葬礼一致。（4）罗马式剧场（约400座）为希律接待马可·阿格里帕（奥古斯都女婿）于公元前15年的访问而建，证实了希律与罗马的密切关系。（5）行政建筑和洁净池表明从第一次犹太起义（公元66-73年）到巴柯巴起义（公元132-135年）的持续居住。

scripturalCorrelation.en: Matthew 2:1-19 describes Herod the Great's reaction to the Magi's news of a newborn 'king of the Jews' — the title Herod himself bore. Herodium, visible from Bethlehem, was one of Herod's closest palaces to the birthplace of Jesus. The discovery of Herod's actual tomb in 2007 confirms Josephus's account of Herod's burial, adding archaeological weight to the historical Herod described in Matthew's infancy narrative.

title.en: Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsaᵃ) — Complete Isaiah Text from 2nd Century BCE
title.zh-Hans: 以赛亚书大卷（1QIsaᵃ）——公元前2世纪的完整以赛亚书
title.zh-Hant: 以赛亚书大卷（1QIsaᵃ）——公元前2世纪的完整以赛亚书

summary.en: The Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsaᵃ), the best-preserved and most complete Dead Sea Scroll, contains the entire Book of Isaiah dated to c. 125 BCE. It demonstrates remarkable textual stability — the text is virtually identical to the Masoretic Text established a millennium later, confirming faithful transmission of biblical prophecy including the famous messianic passages of Isaiah 53.
summary.zh-Hans: 以赛亚书大卷（1QIsaᵃ）是保存最完好、最完整的死海古卷，包含整卷以赛亚书，定年约公元前125年。它展示了非凡的文本稳定性——文本与千年后确立的马所拉文本几乎完全一致，证实了包括著名的以赛亚书53章弥赛亚预言在内的圣经预言的忠实传承。
summary.zh-Hant: 以赛亚书大卷（1QIsaᵃ）是保存最完好、最完整的死海古卷，包含整卷以赛亚书，定年约公元前125年。它展示了非凡的文本稳定性——文本与千年后确立的马所拉文本几乎完全一致，证实了包括著名的以赛亚书53章弥赛亚预言在内的圣经预言的忠实传承。

description.en:
The Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsaᵃ) was found in Qumran Cave 1 in 1947 and is the most complete manuscript among the Dead Sea Scrolls. Dated paleographically to approximately 125 BCE, it contains all 66 chapters of Isaiah on a single scroll measuring 7.34 meters in length.

Key significance:

(1) Textual fidelity: 1QIsaᵃ is overwhelmingly identical to the Masoretic Text (MT) of Isaiah, which was standardized approximately 1,000 years later. While minor spelling and grammatical variations exist, no theological or substantive differences appear — confirming extraordinary textual stability over a millennium.

(2) Isaiah 53: This famous 'Suffering Servant' passage — prophesying a figure despised and rejected, pierced for transgressions, and assigned a grave with the wicked but buried with the rich — is preserved in its entirety in 1QIsaᵃ. This predates Jesus by over a century, eliminating claims that the passage was written after the fact.

(3) Isaiah 7:14 ('Behold, a virgin shall conceive') and Isaiah 9:6 ('For unto us a child is born') — key messianic prophecies — are both preserved in the scroll.

(4) The scroll confirms that the Book of Isaiah was already a unified whole by the 2nd century BCE, countering theories that chapters 1-39 and 40-66 were separate works only later combined.

(5) The Septuagint translation of Isaiah (3rd century BCE) further confirms that the complete book was already circulating before 1QIsaᵃ was copied.
description.zh-Hans:
以赛亚书大卷（1QIsaᵃ）于1947年在昆兰1号洞发现，是死海古卷中最完整的手稿。古文字学定年约公元前125年，在一卷长7.34米的羊皮卷上包含以赛亚书全部66章。

重要意义：（1）文本忠实性：1QIsaᵃ与约1000年后标准化的马所拉文本（MT）极为一致。虽然存在轻微的拼写和语法差异，但没有神学或实质性的不同——证实了一千年来非凡的文本稳定性。（2）以赛亚书53章：这段著名的「受苦仆人」预言——预告一位被人藐视厌弃、为过犯被刺透、与恶人同死却葬在财主坟墓中的人物——在1QIsaᵃ中完整保存。这比耶稣早一个多世纪，消除了此段是事后编写的说法。（3）以赛亚书7:14（「必有童女怀孕生子」）和以赛亚书9:6（「因有一婴孩为我们而生」）——关键弥赛亚预言——都在卷轴中完整保存。（4）卷轴证实以赛亚书在公元前2世纪已是一部统一的作品，反驳了1-39章和40-66章是独立作品后来才合并的理论。（5）以赛亚书的七十士译本翻译（公元前3世纪）进一步证实了完整的以赛亚书在1QIsaᵃ抄写之前就已经流传。

scripturalCorrelation.en: Isaiah 53's 'Suffering Servant' prophecy — written centuries before Jesus — describes his rejection, suffering, death with the wicked, burial with the rich, and ultimate vindication. The Great Isaiah Scroll proves this passage existed verbatim before Christ's birth. Isaiah 7:14 and 9:6, equally preserved, point to a virgin-born divine ruler — fulfilled in Matthew 1:22-23 and Luke 2:11.
scripturalCorrelation.zh-Hans: 以赛亚书53章的「受苦仆人」预言——写于耶稣之前数世纪——描述了他的被弃、受苦、与恶人同死、葬在财主墓中以及最终的平反。以赛亚书大卷证明这段经文在基督降生前就逐字存在。以赛亚书7:14和9:6同样被保存，指向一位童女所生的神圣君王——应验于马太福音1:22-23和路加福音2:11。

title.en: Habakkuk Commentary (1QpHab) — Dead Sea Pesher on the Prophet
title.zh-Hans: 哈巴谷书注释（1QpHab）——死海古卷先知注解
title.zh-Hant: 哈巴谷书注释（1QpHab）——死海古卷先知注解

summary.en: The Habakkuk Commentary (1QpHab), found in Qumran Cave 1, is a verse-by-verse interpretation of Habakkuk 1-2 applying the prophet's words to the Qumran community's own time. It mentions the 'Teacher of Righteousness' and the 'Wicked Priest,' providing independent attestation of Second Temple period interpretive traditions.
summary.zh-Hans: 哈巴谷书注释（1QpHab）在昆兰1号洞发现，是对哈巴谷书1-2章逐句诠释的注释，将先知的话语应用于昆兰社群自身时代。它提到「正义之师」和「邪恶祭司」，提供了第二圣殿时期释经传统的独立证据。
summary.zh-Hant: 哈巴谷书注释（1QpHab）在昆兰1号洞发现，是对哈巴谷书1-2章逐句诠释的注释，将先知的话语应用于昆兰社群自身时代。它提到「正义之师」和「邪恶祭司」，提供了第二圣殿时期释经传统的独立证据。

description.en:
The Pesher Habakkuk (1QpHab) is one of the most important Dead Sea Scrolls. Found in Cave 1 and dating to the 1st century BCE, it quotes verses from Habakkuk 1-2 and provides a running commentary (pesher) applying each verse to the community's contemporary situation.

Key elements:

(1) The 'Teacher of Righteousness' (Moreh ha-Zedek): The scroll's central figure, a priestly leader to whom 'God made known all the mysteries of the words of his servants the prophets.'

(2) The 'Wicked Priest' (Kohein ha-Resha): The Teacher's opponent, identified by some scholars as a High Priest of the Hasmonean dynasty (Jonathan Apphus or Simon Maccabeus).

(3) The 'Kittim': A foreign power described in military terms. Column 3 mentions the Kittim sacrificing to their standards and treating their weapons as objects of worship — a striking parallel to Roman military practices described by Josephus.

(4) Theological significance: The pesher demonstrates that Second Temple Jews understood biblical prophecy as having continuing fulfillment — an interpretive approach shared by early Christianity.

(5) Text preservation: The Habakkuk text quoted in 1QpHab closely matches the Masoretic Text, confirming the accurate transmission of Habakkuk over two millennia.
description.zh-Hans:
哈巴谷佩舍尔（1QpHab）是最重要的死海古卷之一。在1号洞发现，定年为公元前1世纪，逐节引用哈巴谷书1-2章并提供连续注释（佩舍尔），将每节经文应用于社群的当代处境。

关键要素：（1）「正义之师」（Moreh ha-Zedek）：古卷的核心人物，神「使他知道他仆人众先知话语的一切奥秘」的祭司领袖。（2）「邪恶祭司」（Kohein ha-Resha）：正义之师的对手，有学者认为可对应哈斯摩尼王朝的大祭司（约拿单·阿普斯或西门·马加比）。（3）「基提人」：以军事术语描述的外国势力。第3栏描述基提人向军旗献祭、将武器当作崇拜对象——与约瑟夫描述的罗马军事实践的惊人平行。（4）神学意义：佩舍尔展示了第二圣殿犹太教将圣经预言理解为持续应验——一种与早期基督教共享的释经方法。（5）文本保存：1QpHab引用的哈巴谷文本与马所拉文本密切吻合，证实了两千多年来哈巴谷书的准确传承。

scripturalCorrelation.en: Habakkuk 1-2 is the base text of this commentary. The pesher's interpretive method — applying prophetic words to contemporary events — parallels the New Testament's use of Old Testament prophecy (e.g., Matthew's formula quotations, Paul's typological readings). The accurate transmission of the Habakkuk text in 1QpHab confirms the reliability of the Masoretic Text tradition.
scripturalCorrelation.zh-Hans: 哈巴谷书1-2章是该注释的基础文本。佩舍尔的释经方法——将先知话语应用于当代事件——与新约使用旧约预言的方式平行（如马太的公式引文、保罗的预表解读）。1QpHab中哈巴谷文本的准确传承证实了马所拉文本传统的可靠性。

title.en: Kuntillet Ajrud Inscriptions — Evidence for Yahweh Worship in the 9th-8th Century BCE
title.zh-Hans: 昆提莱特·阿吉鲁德铭文——公元前9-8世纪耶和华崇拜的证据
title.zh-Hant: 昆提莱特·阿吉鲁德铭文——公元前9-8世纪耶和华崇拜的证据

summary.en: Inscriptions discovered at Kuntillet Ajrud (a caravanserai in the northeastern Sinai, dated c. 800 BCE) contain blessings 'by Yahweh of Samaria' and 'by Yahweh of Teman' — the oldest extrabiblical references to Israel's God by name. They confirm widespread Yahweh worship in the kingdoms of Israel and Judah during the First Temple period.
summary.zh-Hans: 在昆提莱特·阿吉鲁德（东北西奈的一处商旅驿站，约公元前800年）发现的铭文包含「撒玛利亚的耶和华」和「提幔的耶和华」的祝福——最古老的圣经以外提及以色列之神名字的文献。它们证实了第一圣殿时期以色列和犹大王国中耶和华崇拜的广泛存在。
summary.zh-Hant: 在昆提莱特·阿吉鲁德（东北西奈的一处商旅驿站，约公元前800年）发现的铭文包含「撒玛利亚的耶和华」和「提幔的耶和华」的祝福——最古老的圣经以外提及以色列之神名字的文献。它们证实了第一圣殿时期以色列和犹大王国中耶和华崇拜的广泛存在。

description.en:
Kuntillet Ajrud was excavated by Zeev Meshel in 1975-1976. The site, a way-station/caravanserai in the northeastern Sinai, yielded numerous inscriptions and drawings on pithoi (large storage jars) and plaster walls, dated to c. 800 BCE.

Key inscriptions:

(1) 'I bless you by Yahweh of Samaria and by his Asherah' — This formula appears multiple times, using the personal name YHWH attached to the capital of the Northern Kingdom (Samaria).

(2) 'I bless you by Yahweh of Teman and by his Asherah' — 'Teman' is associated with the southern region (Edom/Negev), possibly referencing a southern shrine.

(3) The name 'Yahweh' (YHWH) in these inscriptions is among the oldest extrabiblical occurrences of Israel's God, predating the Mesha Stele (c. 840 BCE) context.

Significance:

(4) The inscriptions confirm that Yahweh was actively worshipped by name in both the Northern and Southern Kingdoms during the 9th-8th centuries BCE.

(5) The mention of 'Asherah' alongside Yahweh has generated extensive scholarly debate — whether it refers to the goddess Asherah, a cultic symbol (a carved wooden pole), or something else entirely. The biblical prophets repeatedly condemned Asherah worship (1 Kings 18:19, 2 Kings 23:4-7).

(6) The site also contains drawings interpreted as various figures, including possible depictions of the Egyptian god Bes, lions, and other symbols — reflecting the diverse cultural influences at this desert way-station.
description.zh-Hans:
昆提莱特·阿吉鲁德由齐夫·梅谢尔于1975-1976年发掘。该遗址位于东北西奈的一处旅站/商旅驿站，出土了众多铭文和绘制在大型储物罐和灰泥墙上的图画，定年约公元前800年。

关键铭文：（1）「我奉撒玛利亚的耶和华和他的亚舍拉祝福你」——此公式多次出现，使用与北国首都（撒玛利亚）相连的YHWH个人名。（2）「我奉提幔的耶和华和他的亚舍拉祝福你」——「提幔」与南部地区（以东/内盖夫）相关，可能指南部圣所。（3）这些铭文中的「耶和华」（YHWH）是以色列神名最古老的圣经以外出现之一。

重要意义：（4）铭文证实公元前9-8世纪以色列和犹大王国中耶和华名号被积极敬拜。（5）耶和华旁边提到的「亚舍拉」引发了广泛的学术争论——是指女神亚舍拉、崇拜象征物（雕刻的木杆）还是其他。圣经先知反复谴责亚舍拉崇拜（王上18:19，王下23:4-7）。（6）遗址还包含被解读为各种人物的图画，包括可能的埃及神贝斯、狮子和其他符号——反映了这一沙漠旅站多样的文化影响。

The Kuntillet Ajrud inscriptions confirm that Yahweh worship coexisted with Asherah veneration in some Israelite circles — precisely the syncretism that the biblical prophets condemned. The inscriptions provide extrabiblical proof that Yahweh was worshipped by name in the 9th-8th centuries BCE.

title.en: Book of Enoch Manuscripts — Qumran Fragments Confirmed
title.zh-Hans: 以诺书手稿——昆兰残卷确认古老来源
title.zh-Hant: 以诺书手稿——昆兰残卷确认古老来源

summary.en: The Book of Enoch (1 Enoch), quoted in Jude 14-15, was discovered in multiple Aramaic fragments among the Dead Sea Scrolls — confirming this text existed well before the New Testament period and was regarded as authoritative by Second Temple Jewish communities.
summary.zh-Hans: 以诺书（1 Enoch）被犹大书14-15引用。在昆兰死海古卷中发现了其多份亚兰文残片——确认该文本远在新约之前就已存在，并被第二圣殿犹太社群视为权威。
summary.zh-Hant: 以诺书（1 Enoch）被犹大书14-15引用。在昆兰死海古卷中发现了其多份亚兰文残片——确认该文本远在新约之前就已存在，并被第二圣殿犹太社群视为权威。

description.en:
The Book of Enoch (1 Enoch) is an ancient Jewish apocalyptic text attributed to the patriarch Enoch. Jude 14-15 directly quotes it: 'Enoch, the seventh from Adam, prophesied: See, the Lord is coming with thousands upon thousands of his holy ones.'

Qumran discoveries:

(1) Multiple Aramaic fragments of 1 Enoch were found in Caves 1, 2, 4, and 11 (4QEnocha through 4QEnochg, plus 1QEn, 2QEn, 11QEn).

(2) These fragments date from the 3rd to 1st centuries BCE, confirming the text's pre-Christian origin.

(3) The Astronomical Book (1 Enoch 72-82) is the oldest section, with fragments dating to the 3rd-2nd century BCE.

(4) The complete Ge'ez (Ethiopic) translation preserved by the Ethiopian Orthodox Church was authenticated by the Qumran discoveries.

The Qumran fragments demonstrate that 1 Enoch was widely read in Second Temple Judaism, making Jude's quotation natural for his original audience.
description.zh-Hans:
以诺书是归于先祖以诺的古代犹太启示文本。犹大书14-15直接引用：「亚当的七世孙以诺曾预言这些人说：看哪，主带着他的千万圣者降临。」

昆兰发现：（1）在1、2、4、11号洞发现1 Enoch多份亚兰文残片（4QEnocha至4QEnochg）。（2）残片年代为公元前3至1世纪，确认文本的前基督教起源。（3）天文之书是最古老部分，残片测年公元前3-2世纪。（4）守望者之书拥有最多残片，是昆兰最受欢迎的文本之一。（5）完整的吉兹语（埃塞俄比亚语）译本由埃塞俄比亚正教会保存，其真实性直到昆兰发现才被确认。这些残片表明1 Enoch在第二圣殿犹太教中被广泛阅读。

scripturalCorrelation.en: Jude 14-15 directly quotes 1 Enoch 1:9, attributing prophecy to Enoch. 2 Peter 2:4 alludes to Enochic traditions about fallen angels. The Qumran Aramaic fragments confirm 1 Enoch existed centuries before Jude wrote, validating the antiquity of the text he quoted.

title.en: Fouad Papyrus 266 — Greek Deuteronomy with Tetragrammaton
title.zh-Hans: 法乌德纸草266——带四字神名的希腊文申命记
title.zh-Hant: 法乌德纸草266——带四字神名的希腊文申命记

summary.en: Papyrus Fouad 266 (Rahlfs 848), dated to the 1st century BCE, is a Greek translation of Deuteronomy that preserves the divine name YHWH (Tetragrammaton) written in Hebrew square characters within the Greek text — providing crucial evidence for how God's name was treated in pre-Christian Septuagint manuscripts.
summary.zh-Hans: 法乌德纸草266（Rahlfs 848），定年为公元前1世纪，是一份希腊文申命记抄本，在希腊文本中保留了希伯来方块字书写的神名YHWH（四字神名）——为基督教之前的七十士译本抄本中如何处理神名提供了关键证据。
summary.zh-Hant: 法乌德纸草266（Rahlfs 848），定年为公元前1世纪，是一份希腊文申命记抄本，在希腊文本中保留了希伯来方块字书写的神名YHWH（四字神名）——为基督教之前的七十士译本抄本中如何处理神名提供了关键证据。

description.en:
Papyrus Fouad 266 was acquired in 1941 from the Fouad I Papyrus Collection in Cairo. Dated paleographically to the 1st century BCE, it contains portions of Deuteronomy in Greek translation.

Key significance:

(1) The Tetragrammaton: Unlike later Septuagint manuscripts that replaced YHWH with 'Kyrios' (Lord), Fouad 266 preserves the divine name written in Hebrew square characters (the Aramaic/Assyrian script) within the Greek text — exactly where 'Kyrios' appears in later manuscripts.

(2) This confirms that the earliest Greek translations of the Hebrew Bible preserved the divine name rather than substituting it, supporting the view that the practice of replacing YHWH with Kyrios developed later.

(3) The papyrus predates the New Testament, meaning that Greek-speaking Jews (and later Christians) in the 1st century would have been familiar with both the spoken substitution and the written Tetragrammaton.

(4) Deuteronomy 6:4 — the Shema ('Hear, O Israel: the LORD our God, the LORD is one') — is among the passages preserved in this papyrus, making it a directly relevant witness to one of Judaism's most fundamental texts.

The papyrus is now in the Cairo Museum and has been extensively studied by Septuagint scholars including Alfred Rahlfs and Emanuel Tov.
description.zh-Hans:
法乌德纸草266于1941年从开罗的福阿德一世纸草收藏中获得。古文字学定年为公元前1世纪，包含希腊文申命记的部分内容。

重要意义：（1）四字神名：与后来用「Kyrios」（主）替代YHWH的七十士译本抄本不同，法乌德266在希腊文本中以希伯来方块字（亚兰/亚述文字）保留了神名——恰好位于后来抄本中「Kyrios」出现的位置。（2）这证实了最早的希伯来圣经希腊文译本保留了神名而非替换它，支持了以Kyrios替代YHWH的做法是后来发展的观点。（3）该纸草早于新约，意味着1世纪讲希腊语的犹太人（以及后来的基督徒）会同时熟悉口语替代和书面四字神名。（4）申命记6:4——示玛（「以色列啊，你要听：耶和华我们神是独一的耶和华」）——是该纸草保存的经文之一，使其成为犹太教最根本经文的直接见证。

该纸草现藏开罗博物馆，已被拉尔夫斯、托夫等七十士译本学者广泛研究。

scripturalCorrelation.en: Deuteronomy 6:4, the Shema — the foundational declaration of Jewish monotheism — is among the texts preserved in this papyrus. The use of the Hebrew Tetragrammaton within Greek text confirms that God's personal name was reverently preserved even in translation, supporting the authenticity of the divine name as it appears throughout the Hebrew Bible.

title.en: Nag Hammadi Codices — Gnostic Library and New Testament Context
title.zh-Hans: 拿戈哈马迪抄本——诺斯替图书馆与新约背景
title.zh-Hant: 拿戈哈马迪抄本——诺斯替图书馆与新约背景

summary.en: Thirteen leather-bound codices discovered at Nag Hammadi, Egypt in 1945 contain over 50 texts including Gnostic gospels (Thomas, Philip, Mary) and numerous other writings. While not canonical, they illuminate the diverse religious landscape of early Christianity and confirm the antiquity and reliability of the canonical New Testament texts by contrast.
summary.zh-Hans: 1945年在埃及拿戈哈马迪发现的13部皮革装订抄本包含50多份文本，包括诺斯替福音书（多马福音、腓力福音、马利亚福音）等。虽不属于正典，但它们照亮了早期基督教的多元宗教环境，并通过对比确认了正典新约文本的古老性和可靠性。
summary.zh-Hant: 1945年在埃及拿戈哈马迪发现的13部皮革装订抄本包含50多份文本，包括诺斯替福音书（多马福音、腓力福音、马利亚福音）等。虽不属于正典，但它们照亮了早期基督教的多元宗教环境，并通过对比确认了正典新约文本的古老性和可靠性。

description.en:
The Nag Hammadi library was discovered in December 1945 by Egyptian farmers near the town of Nag Hammadi in Upper Egypt. The collection comprises 13 codices containing over 50 texts in Coptic translation, originally written in Greek during the 2nd-3rd centuries CE.

Key contents and significance:

(1) The Gospel of Thomas: 114 sayings attributed to Jesus, some paralleling canonical Gospels. This text demonstrates that sayings of Jesus circulated independently and were valued by different communities.

(2) Contrasting theology: The Gnostic texts present a radically different worldview — emphasizing secret knowledge (gnosis) for salvation, denigrating the material world, and often portraying the Old Testament God as a lesser deity (the Demiurge). By contrast, the New Testament affirms the goodness of creation, bodily resurrection, and salvation through faith in Christ.

(3) Manuscript dating: The Nag Hammadi codices date to the 4th century CE, but the original compositions are typically dated to the 2nd century — significantly later than the canonical Gospels (Mark c. 65-70 CE, Matthew/Luke c. 80-85 CE, John c. 90-95 CE).

(4) Luke 1:1-4 acknowledges 'many' had undertaken to compile accounts of Jesus. The Nag Hammadi texts represent some of these later, non-apostolic traditions.

(5) The codices confirm that the early Church's selection of canonical texts was not arbitrary but reflected genuine criteria of apostolic authorship, widespread use, and theological consistency with Hebrew Scripture.
description.zh-Hans:
拿戈哈马迪图书馆于1945年12月由埃及农民在上埃及拿戈哈马迪镇附近发现。该收藏包含13部抄本，其中50多份文本为科普特语翻译，原文为希腊文，写于公元2-3世纪。

主要内容和意义：（1）多马福音：114条归于耶稣的语录，部分与正典福音书平行。这表明耶稣的语录独立流传并被不同社群所重视。（2）对比神学：诺斯替文本呈现了截然不同的世界观——强调通过秘密知识（gnosis）获得救恩、贬低物质世界、常将旧约神描绘为较低的神（造物主）。相比之下，新约确认受造之物的美好、身体复活以及通过对基督的信心获得救恩。（3）手稿定年：拿戈哈马迪抄本定年为公元4世纪，但原作通常定年为公元2世纪——明显晚于正典福音书（马可福音约公元65-70年，马太/路加约80-85年，约翰约90-95年）。（4）路加福音1:1-4承认「许多人」已着手编写耶稣的事迹。拿戈哈马迪文本代表了这些较晚的、非使徒传统中的一部分。（5）抄本确认早期教会选择正典文本并非随意，而是反映了使徒作者身份、广泛使用和与希伯来圣经神学一致性的真正标准。

scripturalCorrelation.en: Luke 1:1-4 acknowledges that 'many have undertaken to draw up an account' of Jesus. The Nag Hammadi codices represent some of these later accounts. Their distinctly different theology — denying bodily resurrection and the goodness of creation — confirms by contrast the unique and historically grounded nature of the canonical New Testament. 1 John 4:1-3's warning to 'test the spirits' addresses the very tendencies visible in Gnostic writings.

title.en: Nabonidus Harran Inscription — Confirming Daniel's Belshazzar
title.zh-Hans: 拿波尼度哈兰铭文——确认但以理中的伯沙撒
title.zh-Hant: 拿波尼度哈兰铭文——确认但以理中的伯沙撒

summary.en: The Harran Inscriptions of Nabonidus (c. 540 BCE) confirm that Belshazzar — named in Daniel 5 as the last king of Babylon — was indeed Nabonidus's son and co-regent, exercising royal authority in Babylon while his father was away. This validates a detail in Daniel that was long dismissed as a historical error.
summary.zh-Hans: 拿波尼度哈兰铭文（约公元前540年）证实伯沙撒——但以理书5章中称为巴比伦末代王的——确实是拿波尼度的儿子和摄政王，在其父亲离开时在巴比伦行使王权。这验证了但以理书中的一个长期被视为历史错误的细节。
summary.zh-Hant: 拿波尼度哈兰铭文（约公元前540年）证实伯沙撒——但以理书5章中称为巴比伦末代王的——确实是拿波尼度的儿子和摄政王，在其父亲离开时在巴比伦行使王权。这验证了但以理书中的一个长期被视为历史错误的细节。

description.en:
The Harran Inscriptions were discovered on stelae at Harran (ancient Carrhae) in southeastern Turkey. They record the religious building activities of Nabonidus, the last king of Babylon (556-539 BCE).

Key significance for Daniel:

(1) Daniel 5 names 'Belshazzar' as the king of Babylon who saw the writing on the wall the night Babylon fell. For centuries, critics argued this was a historical error because ancient sources listed Nabonidus as the last king.

(2) The Harran Inscriptions, along with the Nabonidus Chronicle and the Verse Account of Nabonidus, revealed that Belshazzar was Nabonidus's eldest son and was left as co-regent in Babylon while his father spent years at the Arabian oasis of Tayma.

(3) This explains why Daniel 5:7, 16, 29 records Belshazzar offering Daniel the position of 'third ruler in the kingdom' — Belshazzar himself was the second ruler (after his father), so he could only offer third place.

(4) The Nabonidus Chronicle confirms that Belshazzar was in charge of Babylon's defenses when Cyrus the Persian conquered the city in 539 BCE.

(5) Josephus (Antiquities 10.11.2-3) also preserved the tradition that Nabonidus entrusted the kingdom to Belshazzar, confirming the biblical account.

The discovery vindicated the author of Daniel against charges of historical ignorance regarding Babylonian succession — a remarkable confirmation that emerged only after 2,400 years.
description.zh-Hans:
哈兰铭文是在土耳其东南部哈兰（古代迦勒）发现的石碑上。它们记录了巴比伦末代王拿波尼度（公元前556-539年）的宗教建筑活动。

对但以理书的重要意义：（1）但以理书5章将「伯沙撒」称为巴比伦沦陷之夜看见墙上写字的的王。几个世纪以来，批评者认为这是历史错误，因为古代史料将拿波尼度列为末代王。（2）哈兰铭文连同拿波尼度年代记和拿波尼度诗歌叙述揭示了伯沙撒是拿波尼度的长子，在其父亲在阿拉伯绿洲泰马逗留多年期间被留在巴比伦担任摄政。（3）这解释了为什么但以理书5:7、16、29记载伯沙撒只能提供「国中位列第三」的位置——伯沙撒本人是第二位统治者（在其父之后），所以他只能提供第三位。（4）拿波尼度年代记证实波斯王居鲁士于公元前539年征服巴比伦时伯沙撒负责巴比伦的防御。（5）约瑟夫（《犹太古史》10.11.2-3）也保存了拿波尼度将王国委托给伯沙撒的传统，确认了圣经记载。

这一发现为但以理作者洗清了关于巴比伦王位继承历史无知的指控——经过2400年才出现的非凡确认。

scripturalCorrelation.en: Daniel 5 describes Belshazzar as king of Babylon during the city's fall. The Harran Inscriptions and Nabonidus Chronicle confirm that Belshazzar was Nabonidus's son and co-regent, left in charge of Babylon — exactly matching Daniel's account. Belshazzar's offer of 'third ruler' (Daniel 5:7, 16, 29) is historically explained by his position as second ruler under his father.

title.en: Philo on Pontius Pilate — Contemporary Jewish Witness to the Prefect
title.zh-Hans: 斐洛论本丢彼拉多——该巡抚的当代犹太见证
title.zh-Hant: 斐洛论本丢彼拉多——该巡抚的当代犹太见证

summary.en: Philo of Alexandria (c. 20 BCE – 50 CE), a Jewish philosopher contemporary with Jesus, wrote about Pontius Pilate in his Embassy to Gaius (c. 40 CE). He described Pilate's 'corruptibility, violence, robberies, assaults, abusive behavior, frequent executions without trial, and endless savage ferocity' — confirming the harsh character of the prefect who sentenced Jesus to crucifixion.
summary.zh-Hans: 亚历山大里亚的斐洛（约公元前20年–公元50年），与耶稣同时代的犹太哲学家，在《致盖乌斯的使团》（约公元40年）中写到本丢彼拉多。他描述彼拉多「贪婪、暴力、掠夺、袭击、辱骂行为、频繁未经审判的处决和无尽的残暴」——确认了这位判处耶稣钉十字架的巡抚的严厉性格。
summary.zh-Hant: 亚历山大里亚的斐洛（约公元前20年–公元50年），与耶稣同时代的犹太哲学家，在《致盖乌斯的使团》（约公元40年）中写到本丢彼拉多。他描述彼拉多「贪婪、暴力、掠夺、袭击、辱骂行为、频繁未经审判的处决和无尽的残暴」——确认了这位判处耶稣钉十字架的巡抚的严厉性格。

description.en:
Philo of Alexandria, one of the most important Jewish thinkers of the 1st century, provides an independent contemporary account of Pontius Pilate in his work 'Embassy to Gaius' (Legatio ad Gaium).

Key content:

(1) Philo describes Pilate's administration as characterized by 'corruptibility, violence, robberies, assaults, abusive behavior, frequent executions without trial, and endless savage ferocity' (Legatio 301-302).

(2) Philo records a specific incident where Pilate set up golden shields (or shields with inscriptions) in Herod's palace in Jerusalem, offending Jewish sensibilities. When Jews protested, Pilate refused to remove them until they appealed to Emperor Tiberius.

(3) This incident reveals: (a) Pilate's insensitivity to Jewish religious concerns, (b) his willingness to use force, and (c) his ultimate accountability to Rome — all consistent with the biblical portrait.

Biblical correlation:

(4) Matthew 27:11-26 shows Pilate as a ruler who recognizes Jesus' innocence but yields to crowd pressure — consistent with a pragmatic politician navigating complex power dynamics.

(5) Luke 13:1 mentions 'the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices' — another reference to Pilate's violent rule.

(6) Philo's account, combined with Josephus's independent description of Pilate, provides two contemporary Jewish witnesses confirming the character and actions of the man who sentenced Jesus — a remarkable convergence for a provincial Roman official.
description.zh-Hans:
亚历山大里亚的斐洛，1世纪最重要的犹太思想家之一，在其著作《致盖乌斯的使团》中提供了本丢彼拉多的独立当代记载。

关键内容：（1）斐洛描述彼拉多的施政以「贪婪、暴力、掠夺、袭击、辱骂行为、频繁未经审判的处决和无尽的残暴」为特征（《使团》301-302）。（2）斐洛记录了一个具体事件：彼拉多在耶路撒冷希律宫中设置了金盾（或刻有铭文的盾牌），冒犯了犹太人的宗教情感。当犹太人抗议时，彼拉多拒绝移除，直到他们向提庇留皇帝上诉。（3）这一事件揭示了：(a)彼拉多对犹太宗教关切的不敏感，(b)他使用武力的意愿，(c)他最终对罗马负责——都与圣经中的画像一致。

圣经对应：（4）马太福音27:11-26展示彼拉多为一个承认耶稣无罪但向群众压力屈服的统治者——与在复杂权力动态中周旋的务实政治家一致。（5）路加福音13:1提到「彼拉多使加利利人的血搀杂在他们的祭物中」——另一处彼拉多暴虐统治的参考。（6）斐洛的记载结合约瑟夫对彼拉多的独立描述，提供了两位当代犹太证人确认了这位判处耶稣之人的品格和行为——对于一个罗马地方官员来说是非凡的汇合。

scripturalCorrelation.en: Matthew 27:11-26 portrays Pilate as a pragmatic but morally weak ruler who yields to pressure despite recognizing Jesus' innocence. Philo's independent description of Pilate's 'savage ferocity' and 'frequent executions without trial' confirms the character of the prefect. Luke 13:1's reference to Pilate killing Galilean worshippers aligns with Philo's portrait of a violent administrator.

title.en: Roman Crucifixion Evidence — Archaeological Confirmation of the Practice
title.zh-Hans: 罗马钉十字架证据——该做法的考古确认
title.zh-Hant: 罗马钉十字架证据——该做法的考古确认

summary.en: Archaeological evidence for Roman crucifixion includes the 1968 discovery of a 1st-century CE Jewish man's remains with a 7-inch iron nail still embedded in his heel bone — the first physical evidence confirming the Roman practice of crucifixion described in all four Gospels. Literary sources (Josephus, Seneca, Pliny) independently confirm crucifixion as Rome's standard execution method.
summary.zh-Hans: 罗马钉十字架的考古证据包括1968年发现的一具公元1世纪犹太人遗骸，其跟骨中仍嵌有一根7英寸长的铁钉——这是首件物理证据确认四部福音书描述的罗马钉十字架做法。文献来源（约瑟夫、塞内加、普林尼）独立确认钉十字架是罗马的标准处决方式。
summary.zh-Hant: 罗马钉十字架的考古证据包括1968年发现的一具公元1世纪犹太人遗骸，其跟骨中仍嵌有一根7英寸长的铁钉——这是首件物理证据确认四部福音书描述的罗马钉十字架做法。文献来源（约瑟夫、塞内加、普林尼）独立确认钉十字架是罗马的标准处决方式。

description.en:
While the Gospels describe Jesus' crucifixion in detail, physical evidence was lacking until 1968, when Vassilios Tzaferis discovered a burial cave at Giv'at ha-Mivtar in Jerusalem containing the remains of a man named Yehohanan.

The crucified man:

(1) A 7-inch iron nail was found embedded in his right heel bone (calcaneum), with fragments of olive wood attached — confirming that nails were driven through the feet/ankles.

(2) Scratches on the radius and ulna of both forearms suggest the arms were nailed or tied to the crossbeam (patibulum).

(3) The legs had been broken — consistent with the Roman practice of crurifragium (leg-breaking) to hasten death (John 19:31-33).

(4) The nail bent after hitting a knot in the olive wood cross, which is why it remained in the bone — the relatives could not remove it for burial.

Literary evidence:

(5) Josephus describes the mass crucifixion of Jews during the siege of Jerusalem (Wars 5.449-451).

(6) Seneca (Viva 6.20) describes various crucifixion positions.

(7) The Alexamenos Graffito (2nd century CE, Rome) depicts a Roman soldier worshiping a crucified figure with a donkey's head — the earliest known depiction of crucifixion, mocking Christian worship.

This evidence confirms that the Gospel accounts of crucifixion accurately reflect Roman execution practices of the 1st century.
description.zh-Hans:
虽然福音书详细描述了耶稣的钉十字架，但直到1968年瓦西里奥斯·扎费里斯在耶路撒冷吉瓦特哈米弗塔发现一个墓穴之前，缺乏物理证据。墓中有一个名叫耶荷哈南的人的遗骸。

被钉十字架的人：（1）他的右跟骨（跟骨）中发现了一根7英寸长的铁钉，附有橄榄木碎片——证实钉子穿过脚/脚踝钉入。（2）两前臂的桡骨和尺骨上有划痕，表明手臂被钉或绑在横梁（patibulum）上。（3）腿已被打断——与罗马人为加速死亡而打断腿的做法（crurifragium）一致（约19:31-33）。（4）钉子在碰到橄榄木十字架的结后弯曲，这就是为什么它留在骨头中——亲属无法在安葬前将其取出。

文献证据：（5）约瑟夫描述了耶路撒冷围攻期间大规模钉十字架的犹太人（《战争》5.449-451）。（6）塞内加（Viva 6.20）描述了各种钉十字架的姿势。（7）亚历山大诺涂鸦（公元2世纪，罗马）描绘了一名罗马士兵崇拜一个长着驴头的钉十字架人物——已知最早的钉十字架描绘，嘲笑基督徒的敬拜。

这些证据确认福音书中的钉十字架记载准确反映了公元1世纪罗马的处决做法。

这些证据确认福音书中的钉十字架记载准确反映了公元1世纪罗马的处决做法。

scripturalCorrelation.en: John 19:31-33 describes the Roman soldiers breaking the legs of the crucified to hasten death, but finding Jesus already dead. The Giv'at ha-Mivtar remains show the same practice — legs broken during crucifixion. The nail through the heel bone confirms the nailing practice described in all four Gospels (Matthew 27:35, Mark 15:24, Luke 24:39-40, John 20:25).
scripturalCorrelation.zh-Hans: 约翰福音19:31-33描述罗马兵丁打断被钉十字架者的腿以加速死亡，但发现耶稣已经死了。吉瓦特哈米弗塔的遗骸显示了同样的做法——钉十字架时腿被打断。跟骨中的铁钉证实了四部福音书描述的钉钉做法（马太福音27:35、马可福音15:24、路加福音24:39-40、约翰福音20:25）。

title.en: Strabo's Geographica — Roman-Era Geographic Confirmation of Biblical Sites
title.zh-Hans: 斯特拉波《地理志》——罗马时代对圣经地点的地理确认
title.zh-Hant: 斯特拉波《地理志》——罗马时代对圣经地点的地理确认

summary.en: Strabo's Geographica (c. 7 BCE - 23 CE), a 17-volume survey of the known world, provides extensive independent descriptions of Judea, Jerusalem, the Dead Sea, the Jordan River, and other biblical locations. Written by a non-Jewish, non-Christian geographer, Strabo's account confirms the geographic and cultural details found throughout the New Testament and Hebrew Bible.
summary.zh-Hans: 斯特拉波的《地理志》（约公元前7年-公元23年），一部17卷的已知世界地理调查，对犹太地、耶路撒冷、死海、约旦河等圣经地点提供了广泛的独立描述。由一位非犹太、非基督徒的地理学家撰写，斯特拉波的叙述确认了新约和希伯来圣经中的地理和文化细节。
summary.zh-Hant: 斯特拉波的《地理志》（约公元前7年-公元23年），一部17卷的已知世界地理调查，对犹太地、耶路撒冷、死海、约旦河等圣经地点提供了广泛的独立描述。由一位非犹太、非基督徒的地理学家撰写，斯特拉波的叙述确认了新约和希伯来圣经中的地理和文化细节。

description.en:
Strabo (c. 64 BCE - 24 CE) was a Greek geographer, historian, and philosopher from Amaseia in Pontus (modern Turkey). His Geographica is a 17-volume work describing the known world of his time, based on both earlier sources and his own extensive travels.

Strabo devotes considerable attention to the region of Judea and surrounding areas in Book 16 of the Geographica. His account provides independent confirmation of numerous biblical details:

(1) Jerusalem: Strabo describes Jerusalem as a notable city of Judea, confirming its status as the regional capital as portrayed throughout the New Testament.

(2) The Dead Sea: He describes the unusual properties of the Dead Sea — its extreme salinity, the absence of marine life, and the floating of objects — consistent with biblical descriptions of the region.

(3) The Jordan River: Strabo describes the Jordan River valley and the river's flow into the Dead Sea, confirming the geography described in Joshua and the Gospels.

(4) Jewish customs: He describes Jewish religious practices, including Sabbath observance, dietary customs, and monotheistic worship — all consistent with biblical descriptions.

(5) The temple in Jerusalem: Strabo references the Jewish temple and its priesthood.

(6) Regional cities: He mentions cities across the Levant that correspond to New Testament locations, including Damascus, Tyre, Sidon, and Caesarea.

Strabo is particularly valuable because he wrote as a pagan observer with no religious stake in the accuracy of biblical claims. His geographic and cultural descriptions align with the biblical text, confirming that the biblical authors were describing real places and real customs.
description.zh-Hans:
斯特拉波（约公元前64年-公元24年）是来自本都阿马塞亚（今土耳其）的希腊地理学家、历史学家和哲学家。他的《地理志》共17卷，描述了当时已知的世界，基于早期文献和他自己广泛的旅行经历。

斯特拉波在《地理志》第16卷中对犹太地及周边地区给予了相当的关注。他的记述为圣经中的许多细节提供了独立确认：

（1）耶路撒冷：斯特拉波将耶路撒冷描述为犹太地的著名城市，确认其作为地区首府的地位，与新约全书的描述一致。

（2）死海：他描述了死海的不寻常特性——极端的盐度、没有海洋生物、物体漂浮——与圣经对该地区的描述一致。

（3）约旦河：斯特拉波描述了约旦河谷和约旦河流入死海的地理，确认了约书亚记和福音书中描述的地理环境。

（4）犹太习俗：他描述了犹太宗教实践，包括安息日遵守、饮食习俗和一神论崇拜——均与圣经描述一致。

（5）耶路撒冷圣殿：斯特拉波提到了犹太圣殿及其祭司制度。

（6）地区城市：他提及了黎凡特地区的城市，与新约地点相对应，包括大马士革、推罗、西顿和凯撒利亚。

斯特拉波特别有价值，因为他是以异教观察者的身份撰写的，对圣经记载的准确性没有宗教利益考量。他的地理和文化描述与圣经文本一致，证实了圣经作者在描述真实的地方和真实的习俗。

His independent, non-biblical descriptions match the geographic and cultural details found throughout the Gospels and Acts.
scripturalCorrelation.zh-Hans: 斯特拉波的《地理志》确认了新约世界的地理框架——耶路撒冷地位、死海特性、约旦河谷、犹太宗教习俗以及黎凡特诸城。他独立的、非圣经的描述与福音书和使徒行传中的地理和文化细节相吻合。

title.en: Herodotus on Egypt — Independent Confirmation of Biblical Details
title.zh-Hans: 希罗多德论埃及——圣经细节的独立印证
title.zh-Hant: 希罗多德论埃及——圣经细节的独立印证

summary.en: Herodotus of Halicarnassus (c. 484-425 BCE), the 'Father of History,' visited Egypt and recorded details that independently confirm aspects of the biblical Exodus narrative, including the use of forced labor for building projects, the geography of the Nile Delta, and Egyptian customs described in Genesis and Exodus.
summary.zh-Hans: 哈利卡纳索斯的希罗多德（约公元前484-425年），「历史之父」，访问埃及并记录的细节独立印证了圣经出埃及记叙事的多个方面，包括使用强迫劳动建造工程、尼罗河三角洲地理以及创世记和出埃及记中描述的埃及习俗。
summary.zh-Hant: 哈利卡纳索斯的希罗多德（约公元前484-425年），「历史之父」，访问埃及并记录的细节独立印证了圣经出埃及记叙事的多个方面，包括使用强迫劳动建造工程、尼罗河三角洲地理以及创世记和出埃及记中描述的埃及习俗。

description.en:
Herodotus traveled to Egypt around 450 BCE and devoted Book II of his Histories entirely to Egyptian civilization. Several of his observations correspond to details in the biblical Exodus/Genesis narratives:

(1) Forced labor and store cities: Herodotus describes Pharaohs using conscripted labor for massive building projects, confirming the biblical picture of Israelite slavery (Exodus 1:11: 'They built Pithom and Rameses as store cities for Pharaoh').

(2) Geography of the Nile Delta: Herodotus accurately describes the Nile's delta region, the land of Goshen, and the canal systems — matching the geographical setting of the Exodus.

(3) Egyptian religious customs: His descriptions of Egyptian animal worship, embalming, and priestly practices align with details reflected in the biblical narratives (e.g., Genesis 46:34, where Egyptians detested shepherds; Exodus 8:26, where Moses says the Israelites' sacrifices would be 'detestable to Egyptians').

(4) The Exodus 1:11 store cities: Herodotus mentions massive construction projects in the eastern Delta region, consistent with the store-city system described in Exodus.

(5) Plague-like phenomena: Herodotus records instances of unusual Nile behavior and natural disasters in Egypt, providing a context for the plagues described in Exodus 7-12.
description.zh-Hans:
希罗多德约于公元前450年前往埃及，将其《历史》第二卷全部用于描述埃及文明。他的多项观察与圣经出埃及记/创世记叙事的细节相对应：

（1）强迫劳动和积货城：希罗多德描述法老使用征召劳工进行大规模建筑工程，证实了圣经中以色列人奴役的图景（出埃及记1:11：「他们建造比东和兰塞作为法老的积货城」）。（2）尼罗河三角洲地理：希罗多德准确描述了尼罗河三角洲地区、歌珊地和运河系统——与出埃及记的地理背景吻合。（3）埃及宗教习俗：他对埃及动物崇拜、木乃伊制作和祭司实践的描述与圣经叙事中反映的细节一致（如创世记46:34埃及人厌恶牧羊人；出埃及记8:26摩西说以色列人的祭物「是埃及人所厌恶的」）。（4）出埃及记1:11的积货城：希罗多德提到东部三角洲地区的大规模建设项目，与出埃及记描述的积货城系统一致。（5）类灾疫现象：希罗多德记录了尼罗河的异常行为和埃及的自然灾害，为出埃及记7-12章描述的灾疫提供了背景。

Genesis 46:34's note that shepherds were 'detestable to Egyptians' is confirmed by Herodotus's description of Egyptian religious attitudes. These independent parallels support the historical authenticity of the biblical Egyptian setting.

title.en: Quirinius Inscription — Luke's Census and Roman Administration
title.zh-Hans: 居里扭铭文——路加的人口普查与罗马行政
title.zh-Hant: 居里扭铭文——路加的人口普查与罗马行政

summary.en: Luke 2:1-2 states that a census took place when 'Quirinius was governor of Syria.' The Titulus Tiburtinus inscription and other evidence confirm that Quirinius served in a governing capacity in Syria. While the precise relationship to Luke's dating remains debated, the inscription confirms Quirinius's administrative role in the region during the Augustan period.
summary.zh-Hans: 路加福音2:1-2记载「居里扭作叙利亚巡抚的时候，头一次行报名上册的事」。提布尔提乌斯铭文和其他证据确认居里扭曾在叙利亚担任行政职务。虽然与路加日期的精确关系仍有争议，但铭文确认了居里扭在奥古斯都时期在该地区的行政角色。
summary.zh-Hant: 路加福音2:1-2记载「居里扭作叙利亚巡抚的时候，头一次行报名上册的事」。提布尔提乌斯铭文和其他证据确认居里扭曾在叙利亚担任行政职务。虽然与路加日期的精确关系仍有争议，但铭文确认了居里扭在奥古斯都时期在该地区的行政角色。

description.en:
Luke 2:1-2 records: 'In those days Caesar Augustus issued a decree that a census should be taken of the entire Roman world. (This was the first census that took place while Quirinius was governor of Syria.)'

The Quirinius problem:

(1) Josephus (Antiquities 18.1-2) records that Quirinius conducted a census in Judea in 6 CE when Archelaus was deposed. Critics argue this contradicts Luke, who places Jesus' birth during Herod's reign (died 4 BCE).

(2) The Titulus Tibertinus inscription: A fragmentary inscription from Tivoli (near Rome) honors a Roman official who served as proconsul of Asia and twice as legate of Syria — 'received' the province 'in the shoes of' the previous governor. Most scholars identify this official as Quirinius.

(3) The 'twice' legateship of Syria would mean Quirinius served an earlier term (c. 3-2 BCE) and a later term (6 CE). If so, Luke's reference to the 'first' census may distinguish Quirinius's earlier census from his later, more famous one in 6 CE.

(4) Regular censuses: The Roman Empire conducted regular censuses for taxation. Egypt's census records show 14-year cycles. A census in Herod's kingdom around 3-2 BCE is plausible as a client-state enrollment.

(5) William Ramsay argued that Luke's use of the Greek 'hegemoneuo' (governing) rather than 'legatus' allows for Quirinius holding authority without being the formal legate.

The debate continues, but Luke's reference to Quirinius reflects knowledge of Roman administrative practices that a later forger would be unlikely to fabricate.
description.zh-Hans:
路加福音2:1-2记载：「当那些日子，凯撒奥古斯都有旨意下来，叫天下人民都报名上册。（这是居里扭作叙利亚巡抚的时候，头一次行报名上册的事。）」

居里扭问题：（1）约瑟夫（《犹太古史》18.1-2）记载居里扭于公元6年当亚基劳被废黜时在犹大进行了人口普查。批评者认为这与路加矛盾，因为路加将耶稣降生定在希律统治时期（死于公元前4年）。（2）提布尔提乌斯铭文：来自蒂沃利（罗马附近）的残缺铭文纪念一位曾任亚细亚总督和两次叙利亚总督的罗马官员——「接替」前任总督的职位。大多数学者认为这位官员是居里扭。（3）叙利亚「两次」总督任期意味着居里扭有一个较早的任期（约公元前3-2年）和较晚的任期（公元6年）。如果是这样，路加提到「第一次」人口普查可能是区分居里扭较早的普查与后来公元6年更著名的普查。（4）定期普查：罗马帝国为征税进行定期普查。埃及的普查记录显示14年为一个周期。希律王国约在公元前3-2年进行普查作为属国登记是合理的。（5）威廉·拉姆齐认为路加使用希腊文「hegemoneuo」（治理）而非「legatus」允许居里扭在非正式总督的情况下拥有权力。

争论仍在继续，但路加提到居里扭反映了对罗马行政实践的了解，这是后来的伪造者不太可能编造的。
description.zh-Hant:
路加福音2:1-2记载：「当那些日子，凯撒奥古斯都有旨意下来，叫天下人民都报名上册。（这是居里扭作叙利亚巡抚的时候，头一次行报名上册的事。）」

居里扭问题：（1）约瑟夫（《犹太古史》18.1-2）记载居里扭于公元6年当亚基劳被废黜时在犹大进行了人口普查。批评者认为这与路加矛盾，因为路加将耶稣降生定在希律统治时期（死于公元前4年）。（2）提布尔提乌斯铭文：来自蒂沃利（罗马附近）的残缺铭文纪念一位曾任亚细亚总督和两次叙利亚总督的罗马官员——「接替」前任总督的职位。大多数学者认为这位官员是居里扭。（3）叙利亚「两次」总督任期意味着居里扭有一个较早的任期（约公元前3-2年）和较晚的任期（公元6年）。如果是这样，路加提到「第一次」人口普查可能是区分居里扭较早的普查与后来公元6年更著名的普查。（4）定期普查：罗马帝国为征税进行定期普查。埃及的普查记录显示14年为一个周期。希律王国约在公元前3-2年进行普查作为属国登记是合理的。（5）威廉·拉姆齐认为路加使用希腊文「hegemoneuo」（治理）而非「legatus」允许居里扭在非正式总督的情况下拥有权力。

争论仍在继续，但路加提到居里扭反映了对罗马行政实践的了解，这是后来的伪造者不太可能编造的。

scripturalCorrelation.en: Luke 2:1-2 places Jesus' birth during a census under Quirinius's administration in Syria. The Titulus Tiburtinus inscription confirms Quirinius served in a governing role in Syria. The possibility of an earlier term of office (c. 3-2 BCE) would reconcile Luke's account with Herod's reign. Luke's precise Roman administrative language reflects genuine historical knowledge of the Augustan period.
scripturalCorrelation.zh-Hans: 路加福音2:1-2将耶稣降生定在居里扭在叙利亚行政期间的一次人口普查。提布尔提乌斯铭文确认居里扭曾在叙利亚担任行政职务。较早任期（约公元前3-2年）的可能性可以调和路加的记载与希律的统治。路加精确的罗马行政语言反映了对奥古斯都时期真正的历史知识。

title.en: Weight of Air — Job's Scientific Insight Ahead of Its Time
title.zh-Hans: 空气的重量——约伯超越时代的科学洞见
title.zh-Hant: 空气的重量——约伯超越时代的科学洞见

summary.en: Job 28:25 states that God 'gave weight to the wind' — a statement about air having measurable weight that was not scientifically confirmed until Evangelista Torricelli's experiments in 1643 CE. This biblical reference, written approximately 3,000 years before the science of atmospheric pressure was developed, demonstrates remarkable prescience about the physical properties of air.
summary.zh-Hans: 约伯记28:25记载神「为风定轻重」——这一关于空气具有可测量重量的论述直到公元1643年托里拆利的实验才得到科学证实。这一圣经参考写在大气压力科学发展之前约3000年，展现了对空气物理特性的惊人预见。
summary.zh-Hant: 约伯记28:25记载神「为风定轻重」——这一关于空气具有可测量重量的论述直到公元1643年托里拆利的实验才得到科学证实。这一圣经参考写在大气压力科学发展之前约3000年，展现了对空气物理特性的惊人预见。

description.en:
Job 28:25 (NIV) states: 'When he established the force of the wind and measured out the waters.' The Hebrew word used for 'weight' (mishqal) directly refers to a measurable weight or mass, suggesting that air/wind has weight.

The scientific discovery:

(1) For most of human history, air was considered weightless. The ancient Greeks, including Aristotle, believed air was one of the four fundamental elements but did not attribute weight to it.

(2) Galileo Galilei first suspected air had weight in the early 1600s, noting that a suction pump could not lift water beyond about 10 meters.

(3) Evangelista Torricelli, Galileo's student, conclusively demonstrated air pressure in 1643 CE with his mercury barometer experiment — showing that atmospheric air exerts pressure equivalent to about 760 mm of mercury (approximately 14.7 psi at sea level).

(4) Modern science confirms that a cubic meter of air at sea level weighs approximately 1.225 kg, and the entire Earth's atmosphere weighs about 5.5 quadrillion tons.

The significance:

(5) The book of Job is generally dated to the 2nd millennium BCE, making this statement about air having weight roughly 3,000 years ahead of Torricelli's scientific confirmation.

(6) In context, Job 28 is a meditation on wisdom — noting that God's wisdom is evident in the design of the natural world, including giving weight to the wind and measuring the waters. The specific physical claim about air having weight is embedded in a broader theological argument about the orderliness of creation.

This is one of several scientific insights in the book of Job that appear to anticipate modern discoveries, alongside references to the hydrological cycle (Job 36:27-28), the spherical shape of the earth (Job 26:7), and ocean currents (Job 38:16).
description.zh-Hans:
约伯记28:25记载：「他为风定轻重」。希伯来文中「重量」（mishqal）一词直接指可测量的重量或质量，暗示空气/风具有重量。

科学发现：（1）在人类历史的大部分时间里，空气被认为是无重量的。古希腊人，包括亚里士多德，认为空气是四种基本元素之一，但未赋予其重量。

（2）伽利略在17世纪初首次怀疑空气有重量，注意到抽水泵无法将水提升超过约10米。

（3）伽利略的学生托里拆利在公元1643年通过水银气压计实验确凿地证明了气压——表明大气空气施加约760毫米水银柱的压力（海平面约14.7磅/平方英寸）。

（4）现代科学确认，海平面一立方米空气重约1.225公斤，整个地球大气层重约5.5千万亿吨。

重要意义：（5）约伯记通常被定为公元前2000年左右的著作，使这一关于空气重量的论述比托里拆利的科学证实早了约3000年。

（6）在上下文中，约伯记28章是对智慧的默想——指出上帝的智慧体现在自然世界的设计中，包括为风定轻重和量定众水。关于空气具有重量的具体物理主张嵌入在关于创造秩序的更广泛神学论证之中。

这是约伯记中几个科学洞见之一，似乎预示了现代发现，其他还包括水循环（约伯记36:27-28）、地球的球形（约伯记26:7）和洋流（约伯记38:16）的记载。

Written approximately 3,000 years earlier, this statement demonstrates knowledge of atmospheric weight that was well ahead of ancient scientific understanding.

title.en: Seed Death and Resurrection — Botany Confirms Paul's Analogy
title.zh-Hans: 种子的死亡与复活——植物学证实保罗的类比
title.zh-Hant: 种子的死亡与复活——植物学证实保罗的类比

summary.en: In 1 Corinthians 15:36-38, Paul uses the botanical process of seed germination as an analogy for bodily resurrection: 'What you sow does not come to life unless it dies.' Modern botany confirms that a seed must undergo cellular breakdown (a form of 'death') before new life emerges — the embryo inside must be metabolically activated through imbibition and enzymatic processes that break down stored tissues before growth begins.
summary.zh-Hans: 在哥林多前书15:36-38中，保罗以种子发芽的植物学过程作为身体复活的类比：「你所种的，若不死就不能生。」现代植物学证实，种子必须经历细胞分解（一种「死亡」），然后新生命才能萌发——胚芽必须通过吸水和酶促过程分解储存组织，然后才能开始生长。
summary.zh-Hant: 在哥林多前书15:36-38中，保罗以种子发芽的植物学过程作为身体复活的类比：「你所种的，若不死就不能生。」现代植物学证实，种子必须经历细胞分解（一种「死亡」），然后新生命才能萌发——胚芽必须通过吸水和酶促过程分解储存组织，然后才能开始生长。

description.en:
1 Corinthians 15:36-38 (NIV): 'When you sow, you do not plant the body that will be, but just a seed, perhaps of wheat or of something else. But God gives it a body as he has determined, and to each kind of seed he gives its own body.'

The botanical science:

(1) Seed germination is a remarkable process that parallels Paul's analogy in surprising detail. A seed is essentially a dormant embryo encased in protective layers (seed coat) with stored food (endosperm or cotyledons).

(2) For germination to begin, the seed must absorb water (imbibition), causing it to swell and rupture its seed coat. This initiates a cascade of enzymatic reactions that break down stored starches, proteins, and lipids — effectively dismantling the seed's original structure.

(3) The growing embryo consumes the stored food, meaning the original seed body is progressively destroyed as the new plant grows. This is what Paul means by 'unless it dies' — the seed form must be lost for the plant form to emerge.

(4) Remarkably, the new plant has a completely different form from the seed. A wheat seed looks nothing like a wheat stalk — just as Paul argues that the resurrection body will be different from the earthly body: 'The body that is sown is perishable, it is raised imperishable' (1 Cor 15:42).

(5) Modern plant physiology has identified the complex hormonal signals (gibberellins, auxins) and genetic programs that control this transformation — a level of sophistication that Paul could not have known about, yet his analogy captures the essential biological truth.

(6) Research in seed dormancy and germination (Bewley & Black, 1994) has shown that the 'death' of the seed structure is not merely metaphorical — it involves programmed cell death (apoptosis) in specific tissues to redirect resources to the growing embryo.

Paul's analogy, written around 55 CE, accurately reflects a botanical reality that modern science has only deepened our understanding of — the old form must die for the new form to live.
description.zh-Hans:
哥林多前书15:36-38：「你所种的，不是那将来的形体，不过是子粒，即如麦子，或是别样的谷。但神随自己的意思给他一个形体，并叫各等子粒各有自己的形体。」

植物学科学：（1）种子发芽是一个与保罗类比惊人相似的过程。种子本质上是一个休眠的胚芽，被包裹在保护层（种皮）和储存食物（胚乳或子叶）中。

（2）发芽开始时，种子必须吸收水分（吸胀），导致膨胀并破裂种皮。这启动了一系列酶促反应，分解储存的淀粉、蛋白质和脂质——实际上是拆解种子的原始结构。

（3）生长中的胚芽消耗储存的食物，意味着原始种子体逐渐被破坏。这就是保罗所说的「若不死就不能生」——种子形态必须消逝，植物形态才能出现。

（4）值得注意的是，新植物与种子有完全不同的形态。一粒麦子看起来与麦穗截然不同——正如保罗论证的，复活之体将与地上之体不同：「所种的是必朽坏的，复活的是不朽坏的」（林前15:42）。

（5）现代植物生理学已鉴定出控制这种转化的复杂激素信号（赤霉素、生长素）和遗传程序——这是保罗不可能知道的复杂程度，然而他的类比捕捉了基本的生物学真理。

（6）种子休眠和发芽研究（Bewley & Black, 1994）表明，种子结构的「死亡」不仅仅是比喻性的——它涉及特定组织的程序性细胞死亡（细胞凋亡），以将资源重新分配给生长中的胚芽。

保罗大约在公元55年写下的这一类比，准确反映了现代科学只是加深了我们对之理解的植物学现实——旧形态必须死亡，新形态才能存活。

scripturalCorrelation.en: 1 Corinthians 15:36-38 uses the germination of a seed as an analogy for resurrection: the seed must 'die' (undergo structural breakdown) to produce new life in a different form. Modern botany confirms this as an accurate description of germination — the seed body is consumed through enzymatic processes and programmed cell death as the new plant emerges.

title.en: Ant Behavior — Proverbs 6:6 Confirmed by Myrmecology
title.zh-Hans: 蚂蚁行为——箴言6:6获蚁学证实
title.zh-Hant: 蚂蚁行为——箴言6:6获蚁学证实

summary.en: Proverbs 6:6 exhorts the reader to 'go to the ant' and consider her ways as a model of industry and planning. Modern myrmecology (the scientific study of ants) has confirmed that ant colonies exhibit remarkable organizational behavior including agriculture, animal husbandry, architecture, and division of labor — far exceeding what ancient observers could have known without divine inspiration.
summary.zh-Hans: 箴言6:6劝勉读者「你去察看蚂蚁的动作」。现代蚁学（蚂蚁科学研究）已确认蚁群展现出非凡的组织行为，包括农业、畜牧、建筑和劳动分工——远超古代观察者在无神圣启示下所能知道的程度。
summary.zh-Hant: 箴言6:6劝勉读者「你去察看蚂蚁的动作」。现代蚁学（蚂蚁科学研究）已确认蚁群展现出非凡的组织行为，包括农业、畜牧、建筑和劳动分工——远超古代观察者在无神圣启示下所能知道的程度。

description.en:
Proverbs 6:6-8 states: 'Go to the ant, you sluggard; consider her ways and be wise — which, having no captain, overseer, or ruler, provides her supplies in the summer, and gathers her food in the harvest.' This three-verse observation has been strikingly validated by modern entomology.

Myrmecological research has documented:

(1) Self-organization: Ant colonies operate without centralized leadership — precisely as Proverbs states ('no captain, overseer, or ruler'). Complex colony-wide behaviors emerge from simple individual interactions, a principle now called 'swarm intelligence.'

(2) Food storage and planning: Harvester ants (Pogonomyrmex), common in ancient Israel, collect and store seeds in specially designed granary chambers — exactly as described. Leafcutter ants practice agriculture, cultivating fungus gardens.

(3) Division of labor: Ant colonies exhibit age-based and caste-based task allocation — some forage, some nurse, some defend.

(4) Architectural sophistication: Ant nests can extend 8 meters deep with ventilation systems, temperature regulation, and drainage — engineering achievements rivaling human construction.

The accuracy of these observations is remarkable given that ant behavior was not systematically studied until the 19th-20th centuries. The Hebrew wisdom tradition preserved scientifically valid ethological observations millennia before the scientific method existed.
description.zh-Hans:
箴言6:6-8说：「懒惰人哪，你去察看蚂蚁的动作，就可得智慧。蚂蚁没有元帅，没有官长，没有君王，尚且在夏天预备食物，在收割时聚敛粮食。」这三节经文的观察已被现代昆虫学显著验证。

蚁学研究已记录：

（1）自组织：蚁群在没有中央领导的情况下运作——精确如箴言所述（「没有元帅、官长、君王」）。复杂的群体行为从简单的个体互动中涌现，这一原则现称「群体智能」。

（2）食物储存和规划：收获蚁（Pogonomyrmex）在古以色列常见，收集种子并储存在特别设计的粮仓室中——与描述完全一致。切叶蚁实行农业，培育真菌花园。

（3）劳动分工：蚁群展现基于年龄和等级的任务分配。

（4）建筑精巧性：蚁巢可深达8米，配有通风系统、温度调节和排水设施。

这些观察的准确性令人注目，因为蚂蚁行为直到19-20世纪才被系统研究。希伯来智慧传统在科学方法存在数千年之前就保存了科学有效的动物行为学观察。
description.zh-Hant:
箴言6:6-8说：「懒惰人哪，你去察看蚂蚁的动作，就可得智慧。蚂蚁没有元帅，没有官长，没有君王，尚且在夏天预备食物，在收割时聚敛粮食。」这三节经文的观察已被现代昆虫学显著验证。

蚁学研究已记录：

（1）自组织：蚁群在没有中央领导的情况下运作——精确如箴言所述（「没有元帅、官长、君王」）。复杂的群体行为从简单的个体互动中涌现，这一原则现称「群体智能」。

（2）食物储存和规划：收获蚁（Pogonomyrmex）在古以色列常见，收集种子并储存在特别设计的粮仓室中——与描述完全一致。切叶蚁实行农业，培育真菌花园。

（3）劳动分工：蚁群展现基于年龄和等级的任务分配。

（4）建筑精巧性：蚁巢可深达8米，配有通风系统、温度调节和排水设施。

这些观察的准确性令人注目，因为蚂蚁行为直到19-20世纪才被系统研究。希伯来智慧传统在科学方法存在数千年之前就保存了科学有效的动物行为学观察。

scripturalCorrelation.en: Proverbs 6:6-8's three specific claims about ants — (1) no centralized ruler, (2) self-directed food gathering in summer/harvest, (3) provision storage — have all been confirmed by myrmecology. The passage demonstrates observational accuracy that exceeds what was possible through casual ancient observation, suggesting either remarkably careful study or divine inspiration of the text.

title.en: Dust Cycle — Genesis 3:19 and Modern Soil Science
title.zh-Hans: 尘土循环——创世记3:19与现代土壤科学
title.zh-Hant: 尘土循环——创世记3:19与现代土壤科学

summary.en: Genesis 3:19 declares 'dust you are, and to dust you shall return.' Modern soil science confirms that human bodies decompose into the same mineral compounds found in soil, and NASA/NOAA have documented the global dust cycle — continuous atmospheric movement of soil particles — matching the biblical description.
summary.zh-Hans: 创世记3:19宣告「你本是尘土，仍要归于尘土」。现代土壤科学确认人体分解为与土壤相同的矿物化合物，NASA/NOAA记录的全球尘土循环——大气中土壤颗粒的持续运动——与圣经描述一致。
summary.zh-Hant: 创世记3:19宣告「你本是尘土，仍要归于尘土」。现代土壤科学确认人体分解为与土壤相同的矿物化合物，NASA/NOAA记录的全球尘土循环——大气中土壤颗粒的持续运动——与圣经描述一致。

description.en:
Genesis 3:19 records God's declaration to Adam: 'By the sweat of your brow you will eat your food until you return to the ground, since from it you were taken; for dust you are and to dust you will return.'

Modern science confirms this at multiple levels:

(1) Chemical composition: The human body contains the same elements found in soil — carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen, oxygen, calcium, phosphorus, potassium, and trace minerals.

(2) Decomposition cycle: Upon death, bodies decompose through microbial activity into simple compounds that return to the soil, completing a biological cycle.

(3) The global dust cycle: NASA and NOAA document billions of tons of dust particles circulating annually between continents — Saharan dust fertilizes the Amazon; Asian dust reaches North America.

(4) The Hebrew word 'adamah' (ground/soil) is etymologically linked to 'Adam' — the man made from the ground. The word 'afar' (dust/fine particles) precisely describes microscopic mineral particles.
description.zh-Hans: 创世记3:19记载：「你必汗流满面才得糊口，直到你归了土…你本是尘土，仍要归于尘土。」现代科学在多个层面证实：（1）化学组成：人体含有与土壤相同的元素——碳、氢、氮、氧、钙、磷等。（2）分解循环：死后通过微生物活动分解为简单化合物回归土壤。（3）全球尘土循环：NASA和NOAA记录每年数十亿吨尘土颗粒在大陆间循环——撒哈拉尘土肥沃亚马逊。（4）希伯来文'adamah'（土地）与'Adam'词源相关。'afar'（尘土/微粒）精确描述构成土壤和人体遗骸的微观矿物颗粒。

scripturalCorrelation.en: Genesis 3:19's declaration aligns with established soil science and biochemistry. The human body's chemical composition matches soil; decomposition returns minerals to earth; the global dust cycle continuously recirculates particulate matter. The Hebrew 'afar' (fine particles) precisely describes the microscopic mineral particles constituting both soil and human remains after decomposition.
