title.en: John on Patmos — Cave of the Apocalypse
title.zh-Hans: 约翰在拔摩岛——启示录之洞
title.zh-Hant: 约翰在拔摩岛——启示录之洞

summary.en: Revelation 1:9 locates John's visions on Patmos, a small Aegean island used by Romans as a place of exile. The Cave of the Apocalypse, venerated since at least the 2nd century and enshrined under the Monastery of St. John (founded 1088), preserves the traditional grotto of John's visions on this archaeologically documented Roman-era exile island.
summary.zh-Hans: 启示录1:9将约翰的异象定位于拔摩岛，一个罗马用于流放的爱琴海小岛。启示录之洞自至少公元2世纪起受崇敬，1088年被圣约翰修道院（1088年建成）收纳——保存了这一考古证实的罗马时代流放岛上约翰异象的传统洞窟。
summary.zh-Hant: 启示录1:9将约翰的异象定位于拔摩岛，一个罗马用于流放的爱琴海小岛。启示录之洞自至少公元2世纪起受崇敬，1088年被圣约翰修道院（1088年建成）收纳——保存了这一考古证实的罗马时代流放岛上约翰异象的传统洞窟。

description.en:
Revelation 1:9 begins: 'I, John, your brother and partner in the tribulation and the kingdom and the patient endurance that are in Jesus, was on the island called Patmos on account of the word of God and the testimony of Jesus.' The reference places John's apocalyptic visions on this specific Dodecanese island.

Historical and archaeological context:

(1) Patmos as Roman exile location: Tacitus (Annals 4.30) and Pliny the Elder (Natural History 4.23) confirm the Aegean islands were regularly used by Rome for exile of political and religious opponents — especially under Domitian (AD 81-96), whose persecution of Christians is attested by Suetonius, Dio Cassius, and Eusebius. The Domitianic dating of Revelation (c. AD 95) places John's exile precisely in this documented persecution.

(2) Irenaeus (Against Heresies 5.30.3, c. AD 180): earliest external attestation, states John 'saw the apocalyptic vision… almost in our own time, at the end of Domitian's reign.' This is less than a century after the composition and is the baseline tradition.

(3) Eusebius (Church History 3.18): confirms John's Patmos exile and return under Nerva's amnesty.

(4) The Cave of the Apocalypse (Spilaion tis Apokalypseos): a grotto on the hillside between the harbor (Skala) and the summit of Patmos, venerated from earliest Christian times as the site where John received the visions. Features include: a crack in the rock wall (traditionally where the 'loud voice like a trumpet' of Revelation 1:10 spoke), a rock shelf identified as John's pillow, and a chapel built over the cave in the 11th century.

(5) Monastery of St. John the Theologian: founded 1088 by Saint Christodoulos under a chrysobull from Byzantine emperor Alexios I Komnenos. The monastery houses early biblical manuscripts (including Codex 1424, a significant Byzantine-text Gospels manuscript), confirming the continuous Christian-scholarly use of the site.

(6) Patmos' harbor archaeology confirms a small but continuously inhabited Roman-era settlement, consistent with a place for isolated exile.
description.zh-Hans:
启示录1:9开篇：「我约翰就是你们的弟兄，和你们在耶稣的患难、国度、忍耐里一同有分，为神的道，并为给耶稣作的见证，曾在那名叫拔摩的海岛上。」这一参照将约翰的末世异象定位于十二群岛的这一具体海岛。

历史与考古背景：

（1）拔摩作为罗马流放地：塔西佗（《编年史》4.30）和老普林尼（《自然史》4.23）证实爱琴岛屿经常被罗马用于流放政治和宗教反对者——尤其在多米田（公元81-96年）时期，他对基督徒的逼迫由苏埃托尼乌斯、狄奥·卡西乌斯和优西比乌证实。启示录的多米田定年（公元约95年）将约翰的流放正好置于此有记录的逼迫中。

（2）爱任纽（《驳异端》5.30.3，约公元180年）：最早的外部证据，陈述约翰「几乎在我们自己的时代，在多米田统治末期」见异象。距成书不到一世纪，是基线传统。

（3）优西比乌（《教会史》3.18）：证实约翰的拔摩流放与在涅尔瓦特赦下的返回。

（4）启示录之洞（Spilaion tis Apokalypseos）：拔摩港口（Skala）与山顶之间山坡上的洞窟，自最早的基督徒时代起即被崇敬为约翰领受异象之所。特色包括：岩壁上的裂缝（传统上为启示录1:10「大声音如吹号」所言之处）、被认定为约翰枕头的岩架，以及11世纪建于洞上的礼拜堂。

（5）圣约翰神学家修道院：1088年由圣克里斯托多卢斯在拜占庭皇帝阿列克修斯一世的金玺诏书下创立。修道院藏有早期圣经抄本（包括具重要拜占庭版本的Codex 1424福音书抄本），证实该地连续的基督徒学术使用。

（6）拔摩的港口考古证实罗马时代小而连续居住的聚落，与孤立流放地的定位一致。

scripturalCorrelation.en:
Revelation 1:9's specific location on Patmos is historically confirmed by Roman-era exile practice (Tacitus, Pliny), Domitianic persecution records (Suetonius, Dio Cassius, Eusebius), and the earliest post-apostolic Christian tradition (Irenaeus c. AD 180). The Cave of the Apocalypse's continuous veneration from early centuries, enshrined in 1088 within the Monastery of St. John, preserves the specific topographic memory of John's visions.

The visions themselves are prophetic-theological content beyond archaeological verification, but the setting — a real Aegean exile island with documented Roman-era use for this exact purpose, and a continuously venerated cave-sanctuary traceable to early Christian tradition — provides the authentic historical framework of the biblical book.
scripturalCorrelation.zh-Hans:
启示录1:9在拔摩的具体定位，经罗马流放实践（塔西佗、普林尼）、多米田逼迫记录（苏埃托尼乌斯、狄奥·卡西乌斯、优西比乌）及最早的使徒后基督徒传统（爱任纽，约公元180年）在历史上得到证实。启示录之洞自早期起的连续崇敬，1088年被收入圣约翰修道院，保存了约翰异象的具体地形记忆。

title.en: Crucifixion Darkness and Earthquake — Independent Witnesses
title.zh-Hans: 受难日的黑暗与地震——独立见证
title.zh-Hant: 受难日的黑暗与地震——独立见证

summary.en: The Synoptic Gospels record darkness from the 6th to 9th hour and an earthquake at Jesus's crucifixion. The 1st-century historian Thallus (preserved in Julius Africanus, c. AD 221) independently attests the darkness, and the 2012 Williams-Schwab-Brauer Dead Sea sediment study precisely dated an earthquake to AD 26-36 — the exact window of the crucifixion.
summary.zh-Hans: 对观福音都记载耶稣受难时午正至申初（6时至9时）的黑暗和地震。1世纪历史学家塔鲁斯（由儒略·亚非利加保存，公元约221年）独立证实黑暗，而2012年Williams-Schwab-Brauer死海沉积物研究精确将一次地震定年于公元26-36年——正是受难的窗口。
summary.zh-Hant: 对观福音都记载耶稣受难时午正至申初（6时至9时）的黑暗和地震。1世纪历史学家塔鲁斯（由儒略·亚非利加保存，公元约221年）独立证实黑暗，而2012年Williams-Schwab-Brauer死海沉积物研究精确将一次地震定年于公元26-36年——正是受难的窗口。

description.en:
Matthew 27:45-54, Mark 15:33, and Luke 23:44-45 record unusual phenomena at Jesus's crucifixion: (1) darkness from the 6th to 9th hour (noon to 3 PM); (2) the Temple veil torn in two; (3) an earthquake (Matthew 27:51-54); (4) tombs opening.

Independent evidence:

(1) Thallus fragment (c. AD 52): the historian Thallus, whose works survive only through later citations, wrote a three-volume history of the Eastern Mediterranean covering the period through the mid-1st century. Julius Africanus (c. AD 221, History of the World Book 3) cites Thallus: 'In the third book of his history, Thallus calls this darkness an eclipse of the sun — unreasonably, as it seems to me.' Africanus objects because a solar eclipse is impossible at Passover (full moon). The significance: Thallus, writing within 20 years of the events, knew of and attempted to explain the darkness — confirming the event was public knowledge requiring explanation.

(2) Phlegon of Tralles (c. AD 140): another pagan historian cited by Origen (Contra Celsum 2.33) and Eusebius for recording an 'extraordinary darkness' and 'great earthquake' in the reign of Tiberius, specifically in the 4th year of the 202nd Olympiad (AD 32-33).

(3) The Williams-Schwab-Brauer Dead Sea earthquake study (International Geology Review 2012): sediment cores from the Dead Sea's western shore at Ein Gedi show distinct seismite layers (earthquake-disturbed sediments). Dated seismites occur in 31 BCE (Josephus-attested earthquake) and a second major event dated AD 26-36 — precisely the window of Jesus's crucifixion (AD 30-33 by standard dating). This is independent geological confirmation of a real earthquake in the Jerusalem-Dead Sea region during the exact crucifixion timeframe.

(4) Humphreys and Waddington (Nature 1983): calculated the lunar eclipse of April 3, AD 33, visible from Jerusalem at moonrise — possibly relevant to Acts 2:20's reference to 'the moon turned to blood' and aligning with a crucifixion date of April 3, AD 33 (Friday, 14 Nisan).

(5) The darkness itself: three hours of midday darkness cannot be a solar eclipse (impossible at Passover full moon, and maximum solar-eclipse totality is under 8 minutes). Proposed natural explanations — severe sirocco dust storm, volcanic haze from an unidentified eruption — remain speculative. What is independently confirmed: the event was public, attested by non-Christian historians within a generation, and required explanation.
description.zh-Hans:
马太福音27:45-54、马可福音15:33和路加福音23:44-45都记载耶稣受难时的异常现象：（1）午正至申初（中午至下午3点）的黑暗；（2）圣殿幔子裂为两半；（3）地震（马太福音27:51-54）；（4）坟墓开启。

独立证据：

（1）塔鲁斯残篇（公元约52年）：塔鲁斯的三卷东地中海史仅通过后来引用存留。儒略·亚非利加（公元约221年，《世界史》第3卷）引用塔鲁斯：「在他历史第三卷中，塔鲁斯将这黑暗称作日食——在我看来是不合理的。」亚非利加反对，因为逾越节（满月）不可能日食。意义：塔鲁斯在事件发生20年内便知晓此黑暗并试图解释——证实事件为公众周知、需要解释。

（2）特拉勒斯的斐勒干（公元约140年）：另一位异教历史学家，被俄利根（《驳塞尔苏斯》2.33）和优西比乌引用，记录提比略统治时期「非凡的黑暗」和「大地震」，具体在第202届奥运会第4年（公元32-33年）。

（3）Williams-Schwab-Brauer死海地震研究（《国际地质评论》2012）：从死海西岸恩戈底采集的沉积物岩芯显示明显的地震层（地震扰动的沉积物）。定年地震层发生在公元前31年（约瑟夫记载的地震）和公元26-36年的第二次重大事件——正是耶稣受难的窗口（按标准定年为公元30-33年）。这是对耶路撒冷-死海地区正值受难时段真实地震的独立地质证实。

（4）Humphreys和Waddington（《自然》1983）：计算公元33年4月3日耶路撒冷月升时可见的月食——可能与使徒行传2:20「月要变为血」的参照有关，并与公元33年4月3日（星期五，尼散月14日）的受难定年吻合。

（5）黑暗本身：午正三小时黑暗不可能是日食（逾越节满月不可能，且日食全食最长不到8分钟）。提出的自然解释——严重的西洛克沙尘暴、不明火山喷发的气溶胶——仍属推测。独立证实的是：事件为公开的、一代之内被非基督徒历史学家证实、需要解释。

Matthew 27:45 and parallels specify '6th to 9th hour' darkness and a significant earthquake. Thallus (c. AD 52) and Phlegon (c. AD 140) — both pagan historians — independently acknowledge both phenomena. The Dead Sea sediment study's geological dating of an AD 26-36 earthquake matches the crucifixion window precisely and independently.

The theological interpretation (divine testimony to the crucifixion's significance) is beyond empirical adjudication, but the physical events themselves — three hours of unusual darkness publicly attested within a generation, and a major regional earthquake in the exact AD 26-36 window — are independently verified.

title.en: Water from the Rock — Sinai Hydrogeology
title.zh-Hans: 磐石出水——西奈水文地质
title.zh-Hant: 磐石出水——西奈水文地质

summary.en: Exodus 17 and Numbers 20 record Moses striking a rock to bring forth water at Rephidim and Kadesh. Arie Issar's hydrogeological surveys of Sinai document extensive subsurface aquifers beneath the peninsula's limestone and granite formations — where striking fissured rock in a wadi floor can indeed release water from underground reserves, matching the biblical description.
summary.zh-Hans: 出埃及记17章和民数记20章记载摩西击打磐石在利非订和加低斯出水。阿里耶·伊塞尔的西奈水文地质调查记录了半岛石灰岩与花岗岩层下的广泛地下含水层——在wadi谷底击打破裂岩石确实能释放地下水储，与圣经描述吻合。
summary.zh-Hant: 出埃及记17章和民数记20章记载摩西击打磐石在利非订和加低斯出水。阿里耶·伊塞尔的西奈水文地质调查记录了半岛石灰岩与花岗岩层下的广泛地下含水层——在wadi谷底击打破裂岩石确实能释放地下水储，与圣经描述吻合。

description.en:
Exodus 17:1-7 records Israel at Rephidim without water; Moses is directed to strike 'the rock at Horeb,' and water flows. Numbers 20:1-13 records a parallel event at Kadesh.

Arie Issar (Ben-Gurion University), whose Water Shall Flow from the Rock: Hydrogeology and Climate in the Lands of the Bible (Springer 1990) is the definitive technical study of Sinai-Negev water sources, documents:

(1) Extensive subsurface aquifers beneath Sinai: the Nubian Sandstone aquifer system, the Upper Cretaceous aquifer (containing water from rainfall 10,000-30,000 years ago), and the Quaternary alluvial aquifers of wadi fills. These constitute substantial water reserves under the peninsula's desert surface.

(2) Fracture-fed springs: where the granite basement rock is crossed by fault lines and fissures, water from deep aquifers rises to just beneath the surface. In wadi floors where overlying sediment is thin, breaking the fissured rock can release trapped or pressurized water — a well-documented phenomenon in desert hydrology.

(3) Specifically at Horeb / Jebel Musa / Mount Sinai region: Issar identifies several known fissure-spring sites in the wadis around Jebel Musa and Jebel Katarina, including traditional sites venerated from at least the 4th century (Wadi Leja, near St. Catherine's Monastery).

(4) James Hoffmeier (Ancient Israel in Sinai, 2005) reviews the Exodus-route hydrogeology, noting that the described water events at Rephidim, Marah, and Elim each correspond to real hydrogeological features of the proposed routes. The bitter-water episode at Marah (Exodus 15:22-25) matches brackish-water springs known in the central Sinai.

(5) Menashe Har-El (The Sinai Journeys, 1983) maps the Exodus route against actual Sinai water sources, demonstrating that the biblical itinerary passes through the viable water-availability zones that sustained ancient Bedouin and military traffic.

(6) Traditional Rephidim site: identified with Wadi Refayid / Wadi Feiran region, where Jebel Musa (Mount Sinai) and its attendant water sources are concentrated. Pilgrim traditions from the 4th century onward (Egeria's Travels, c. 381) identify specific rocks as the one Moses struck.
description.zh-Hans:
出埃及记17:1-7记载以色列在利非订缺水，摩西蒙指示击打「何烈的磐石」，水便涌出。民数记20:1-13记载在加低斯的平行事件。

阿里耶·伊塞尔（本-古里安大学）的《水要从磐石涌出：圣经之地的水文地质与气候》（施普林格1990）是西奈-内盖夫水源的权威技术研究，记录：

（1）西奈地下广泛含水层：努比亚砂岩含水层系统、上白垩含水层（含10,000-30,000年前降雨）及wadi冲积的第四纪含水层。这些构成沙漠表层之下的大量水储。

（2）裂隙泉：花岗岩基岩被断层线与裂缝切过之处，深部含水层的水升至地表附近。在覆盖沉积薄的wadi谷底，打破裂隙岩石可释放受压或滞留的水——沙漠水文中已有充分记录的现象。

（3）具体在何烈/杰贝尔穆萨/西奈山地区：伊塞尔识别出Jebel Musa和Jebel Katarina周围wadi中的几个已知裂隙泉地点，包括自至少4世纪起受崇敬的传统地点（Wadi Leja，近圣凯瑟琳修道院）。

（4）詹姆斯·霍夫迈尔（《古以色列在西奈》，2005）审视出埃及路线的水文地质，指出利非订、玛拉和以琳的描述性水事件各对应所提路线的真实水文地质特征。玛拉的苦水事件（出埃及记15:22-25）与中西奈已知的苦咸水泉吻合。

（5）Menashe Har-El（《西奈旅程》，1983）将出埃及路线与西奈实际水源相对照，证明圣经行程穿越了维持古代贝都因和军事交通的可行供水区。

（6）传统利非订地点：与Wadi Refayid/Wadi Feiran地区相认，Jebel Musa（西奈山）及其附属水源集中于此。自4世纪起的朝圣传统（Egeria《旅行记》，约381年）将特定磐石认定为摩西所击之石。

scripturalCorrelation.en:
The biblical narratives specify that water came from struck rock in wilderness locations (Horeb/Rephidim, Kadesh) — a description matching documented Sinai hydrogeology, where breaking fissured rock in wadi floors can release water from subsurface aquifers. The phenomenon is naturalistically well-attested, making the setting of the miracle physically authentic to the region.

The miraculous element in the biblical narrative lies in the timing, precision, and abundance of the flow — providing for a multitude — and in Moses's prophetic direction to the specific rock. Whether a natural subsurface water-release or a direct supernatural provision, the geographical and hydrogeological setting is verified. The wilderness tradition preserves accurate environmental knowledge of Sinai water-availability that no later author inventing the account would have known in such accurate detail.
scripturalCorrelation.zh-Hans:
圣经叙事记载磐石被击在旷野地点（何烈/利非订、加低斯）出水——这一描述与已记录的西奈水文地质吻合，在wadi谷底打破裂隙岩石能释放地下含水层之水。该现象在自然主义上充分证实，使神迹的背景在该区物理上真实。

圣经叙事中的神迹性在于水流的时机、精确性和丰盛——供给众民——以及摩西对具体磐石的先知性指引。无论是自然地下水释放或直接超自然供应，地理与水文地质背景得到证实。旷野传统保留了对西奈水源可得性的准确环境知识，这是后期虚构作者无法如此准确描述的。

title.en: Jacob's Ladder at Bethel — Archaeological Evidence for the Sacred Site
title.zh-Hans: 雅各天梯伯特利——圣地的考古证据
title.zh-Hant: 雅各天梯伯特利——圣地的考古证据

summary.en: Genesis 28:10-22 records Jacob's dream of a ladder to heaven at Bethel. Archaeological excavations at Beitin (ancient Bethel) by Albright (1934) and Kelso (1954-1960) uncovered continuous occupation from the Middle Bronze Age through the Iron Age, including evidence of a sacred cultic site — consistent with Bethel's biblical role as a major Israelite worship center.
summary.zh-Hans: 创世记28:10-22记载雅各在伯特利梦见通天的梯子。奥尔布赖特（1934）和凯尔索（1954-1960）在贝廷（古伯特利）的考古发掘发现了从青铜器中期到铁器时代的连续居住层，包括神圣崇拜遗址的证据——与伯特利在圣经中作为以色列主要崇拜中心的地位一致。
summary.zh-Hant: 创世记28:10-22记载雅各在伯特利梦见通天的梯子。奥尔布赖特（1934）和凯尔索（1954-1960）在贝廷（古伯特利）的考古发掘发现了从青铜器中期到铁器时代的连续居住层，包括神圣崇拜遗址的证据——与伯特利在圣经中作为以色列主要崇拜中心的地位一致。

description.en:
Genesis 28:10-22 describes Jacob fleeing from Beersheba to Haran, stopping at a place where he dreamed of a ladder reaching to heaven with angels ascending and descending. He named it Bethel ('House of God'), set up a stone pillar, and vowed to tithe.

Archaeological evidence:

(1) Site identification: Beitin, 17 km north of Jerusalem, was identified as Bethel by Edward Robinson (1838) based on geographic correspondence. The Arabic name preserves the ancient Hebrew.

(2) Albright's excavation (1934): William F. Albright found continuous occupation from the Early Bronze Age through the Iron Age II. The Middle Bronze Age (c. 2000-1550 BCE) — the patriarchal period — showed substantial occupation with a fortified town.

(3) Kelso's excavation (1954-1960): James Kelso continued work, uncovering evidence of a sacred area including cultic installations, consistent with Bethel's role as a worship center from the patriarchal period through the divided monarchy.

(4) Iron Age occupation: Significant Israelite occupation during the period of the Judges and monarchy, including evidence of destruction consistent with Assyrian campaigns.

(5) Sacred site continuity: The persistence of Bethel as a cultic center through multiple periods aligns with the biblical narrative where Jacob, and later Jeroboam I, established worship there.

Note: Some scholars (Finkelstein, 2009) have questioned the Beitin identification, proposing el-Bireh instead. The debate continues, but the general region matches biblical geography.
description.zh-Hans:
创世记28:10-22描述雅各从别是巴逃往哈兰途中，在一处停歇时梦见通天的梯子，天使上去下来。他称该地为伯特利（「神的殿」），立了一根石柱，并许愿十一奉献。

考古证据：（1）遗址识别：贝廷位于耶路撒冷以北约17公里，由爱德华·罗宾逊（1838年）根据地理对应关系认定为伯特利。阿拉伯语名保留了古希伯来语。（2）奥尔布赖特的发掘（1934年）：威廉·奥尔布赖特发现了从青铜器早期到铁器时代II期的连续居住层。青铜器中期（约公元前2000-1550年）——族长时期——显示有相当规模的设防城镇居住。（3）凯尔索的发掘（1954-1960年）：詹姆斯·凯尔索继续工作，发现包括崇拜设施在内的神圣区域证据，与伯特利从族长时期到分裂王国时期作为崇拜中心的地位一致。（4）铁器时代居住：士师和王國时期有重要的以色列人居住，包括与亚述战役一致的毁灭证据。（5）圣地连续性：伯特利在多个时期持续作为崇拜中心与圣经叙事一致——雅各和后来耶罗波安一世都在此设立敬拜。

注：有学者（芬克尔斯坦，2009年）质疑贝廷的认定，提出el-Bireh为替代。争论仍在继续，但总体区域符合圣经地理。

scripturalCorrelation.en: Genesis 28:10-22 records Jacob's dream at Bethel, where he saw a ladder to heaven and received God's covenant promise. The archaeological evidence at Beitin confirms a significant Bronze Age settlement with cultic installations in the exact region described, consistent with Bethel's long role as a sacred site in Israelite tradition. Jesus later referenced this event in John 1:51: 'You will see heaven open and the angels of God ascending and descending on the Son of Man.'

title.en: Elisha and the Shunammite Woman's Son — Archaeological Context
title.zh-Hans: 以利沙与书念妇人之子——考古背景
title.zh-Hant: 以利沙与书念妇人之子——考古背景

summary.en: 2 Kings 4:8-37 records Elisha raising the Shunammite woman's dead son in her upper room. The village of Shunem (modern Sulam) in the Jezreel Valley has been identified archaeologically, and the Iron Age domestic architecture of the region matches the biblical description of a 'small room on the roof' built for the prophet.
summary.zh-Hans: 列王纪下4:8-37记载以利沙在书念妇人的楼上房间里使她死去的儿子复活。耶斯列谷的书念村（现代Sulam）已被考古确认，该地区铁器时代民居建筑与圣经描述的为先知建造的「楼上的小房」吻合。
summary.zh-Hant: 列王纪下4:8-37记载以利沙在书念妇人的楼上房间里使她死去的儿子复活。耶斯列谷的书念村（现代Sulam）已被考古确认，该地区铁器时代民居建筑与圣经描述的为先知建造的「楼上的小房」吻合。

description.en:
2 Kings 4:8-37 describes a wealthy Shunammite woman who persuaded her husband to build a 'small room on the roof' for Elisha. Later, her young son died, and Elisha lay upon the child mouth-to-mouth, restoring him to life.

Archaeological evidence:

(1) Shunem (Hebrew: Shunem; modern Sulam) is a village on the southwestern edge of the Jezreel Valley, identified through Iron Age pottery and geographic correlation with the biblical site.

(2) Iron Age domestic architecture in the Jezreel Valley features flat roofs with upper rooms (aliyyah) built into the roof structure — precisely matching the 'small room on the roof, with a bed, a table, a chair, and a lampstand' described in 2 Kings 4:10.

(3) The Jezreel Valley was contested territory between Israel and Phoenician/Canaanite powers during the 9th century BCE, consistent with Elisha's ministry context.

(4) The narrative's detail that the woman's husband was old (4:14) and that she had no son reflects the social vulnerability of childless women in ancient Israel, a culturally accurate detail.

(5) The 9th-century BCE prophetic tradition associated with Elisha is confirmed by the Tel Dan Stele and other contemporary evidence for the divided monarchy period.
description.zh-Hans:
列王纪下4:8-37描述一位富有的书念妇人说服丈夫在屋顶上建造「一间小楼」，供以利沙居住。后来她年幼的儿子死去，以利沙俯伏在孩子身上口对口，使他复活。

考古证据：（1）书念（现代Sulam）是耶斯列谷西南缘的村庄，通过铁器时代陶器和地理关联被确认。（2）耶斯列谷铁器时代民居建筑具有平顶结构中的楼上房间（aliyyah）——精确匹配列王纪下4:10描述的「墙上的小楼，里面放床、桌、椅和灯台」。（3）耶斯列谷在公元前9世纪是以色列与腓尼基/迦南势力的争夺地，与以利沙事工背景一致。（4）叙事中丈夫年老（4:14）、妇人无子反映了古代以色列无子女性的社会脆弱性，是文化上准确的细节。

title.en: Josiah's Discovery of the Book of the Law — Archaeological Context
title.zh-Hans: 约西亚发现律法书——考古背景
title.zh-Hant: 约西亚发现律法书——考古背景

summary.en: 2 Kings 22-23 records King Josiah's discovery of the 'Book of the Law' during Temple repairs in 622 BCE, triggering sweeping religious reforms. Archaeological evidence from late 7th century BCE Jerusalem — including Josiah-era bullae, seal impressions, and administrative reforms visible in the material record — provides context consistent with a centralized kingdom implementing religious reforms.
summary.zh-Hans: 列王纪下22-23章记载约西亚王在公元前622年圣殿修缮中发现「律法书」，引发全面宗教改革。公元前7世纪末耶路撒冷的考古证据——包括约西亚时期的封泥、封印和行政改革的物质遗存——提供了与中央集权王国实施宗教改革一致的背景。
summary.zh-Hant: 列王纪下22-23章记载约西亚王在公元前622年圣殿修缮中发现「律法书」，引发全面宗教改革。公元前7世纪末耶路撒冷的考古证据——包括约西亚时期的封泥、封印和行政改革的物质遗存——提供了与中央集权王国实施宗教改革一致的背景。

description.en:
2 Kings 22:8-23:25 describes how Hilkiah the high priest found 'the Book of the Law' during Temple renovations ordered by King Josiah. Upon hearing it read, Josiah tore his robes in distress, consulted the prophetess Huldah, and initiated comprehensive religious reforms: destroying high places, removing idolatrous priests, desecrating Topheth, and reinstating the Passover.

Archaeological context:

(1) The Temple Mount area has yielded numerous bullae (seal impressions) from the late 7th century BCE — precisely Josiah's reign — bearing names of officials consistent with a functioning royal administration.

(2) LMLK jar handles and other administrative materials from this period show a centralized government capable of organizing large-scale reforms.

(3) The City of David excavations have revealed significant construction from the late 7th century, consistent with Josiah's building program mentioned in 2 Chronicles 34:8-13.

(4) The 'silence' of non-biblical sources about Josiah's reforms is expected — ancient Near Eastern records typically commemorate victories, not internal religious reforms.

(5) The discovery fits a pattern: Mesopotamian kings regularly 'found' and restored ancient texts during temple renovations, a well-documented practice that provides cultural context for Hilkiah's discovery.

(6) The Deuteronomic reforms (centralization of worship in Jerusalem) can be traced in the archaeological record through the disappearance of local shrines and figurines in late 7th century Judah.
description.zh-Hans:
列王纪下22:8-23:25描述大祭司希勒家在约西亚王下令的圣殿修缮中「得了律法书」。约西亚听后撕裂衣服，求问女先知户勒大，并启动全面的宗教改革：拆毁高处、除掉偶像祭司、污秽陀斐特、重新守逾越节。

考古背景：（1）圣殿山地区出土了众多公元前7世纪末的封泥——恰为约西亚统治时期——上面有与运作中的王室行政系统一致的官员名字。（2）LMLK罐柄和该时期的其他行政材料显示了一个有能力组织大规模改革的中央政府。（3）大卫城发掘发现了公元前7世纪末的重要建筑，与历代志下34:8-13提到的约西亚建筑工程一致。（4）非圣经来源对约西亚改革的「沉默」是意料之中的——古代近东记录通常纪念军事胜利，而非内部宗教改革。（5）这一发现符合一种模式：美索不达米亚君王在圣殿修缮中经常「发现」并恢复古老文本，这一有充分记录的做法为希勒家的发现提供了文化背景。（6）申命记式改革（集中敬拜于耶路撒冷）可以从考古记录中追溯到公元前7世纪末犹大本地神龛和偶像的消失。

The archaeological record from late 7th century BCE Jerusalem shows evidence of centralized administration, temple activity, and religious changes consistent with the biblical account. The Mesopotamian practice of 'finding' texts during temple restorations provides cultural plausibility for the event.

title.zh-Hans: 所罗巴伯第二圣殿——波斯时期证据
title.zh-Hant: 所罗巴伯第二圣殿——波斯时期证据

summary.en: The Second Temple, rebuilt under Zerubbabel around 516 BCE as described in Ezra 3-6 and Haggai 1-2, is supported by Persian-period Yehud seal impressions found in Jerusalem, the Elephantine Papyri (5th century BCE) referencing 'the temple of YHW' in Jerusalem, and archaeological evidence of Persian-period Jewish settlement in Judea — all confirming a functioning Jewish temple in Jerusalem during the Persian era.
summary.zh-Hans: 由所罗巴伯约在公元前516年重建的第二圣殿（以斯拉记3-6章和哈该书1-2章），得到了在耶路撒冷发现的波斯时期犹大印章印痕、象岛古卷（公元前5世纪）提及耶路撒冷的「雅威之殿」，以及波斯时期犹太人在犹大地定居的考古证据支持——均确认波斯时代耶路撒冷有一座运作中的犹太圣殿。
summary.zh-Hant: 由所罗巴伯约在公元前516年重建的第二圣殿（以斯拉记3-6章和哈该书1-2章），得到了在耶路撒冷发现的波斯时期犹大印章印痕、象岛古卷（公元前5世纪）提及耶路撒冷的「雅威之殿」，以及波斯时期犹太人在犹大地定居的考古证据支持——均确认波斯时代耶路撒冷有一座运作中的犹太圣殿。

description.en:
After the Babylonian exile, the Jewish people returned to Jerusalem and rebuilt the temple under the leadership of Zerubbabel (a descendant of David) and Joshua the high priest, as described in Ezra 3-6, Haggai 1-2, and Zechariah 1-8. The Second Temple was completed around 516 BCE and stood until Herod's renovation/rebuild beginning around 20 BCE.

Biblical account:

(1) Ezra 1:1-4 records Cyrus the Great's decree (538 BCE) allowing the Jews to return and rebuild the temple — confirmed by the Cyrus Cylinder.

(2) Ezra 3:8-13 describes the laying of the temple foundation, with mixed reactions from those who remembered the first temple.

(3) Haggai 1-2 prophesies c. 520 BCE, urging the people to complete the temple construction.

(4) Zechariah 4:6-10 prophesies that Zerubbabel will complete the temple.

Archaeological evidence:

(5) Persian-period Yehud seal impressions (yehud stamps) have been found in excavations throughout Jerusalem and Judea, dating to the 5th-4th centuries BCE. These administrative seals — impressed on jar handles with the Aramaic letters YHD (Yehud, the Persian province of Judea) — confirm a functioning Jewish community under Persian administration.

(6) The Elephantine Papyri, discovered in Egypt (1893-1907), contain letters from a Jewish military colony at Elephantine (Aswan) dating to the late 5th century BCE. A letter from 407 BCE (AP 30) requests permission to rebuild their local temple, referencing 'the temple of YHW [Yahweh] in Jerusalem' — proving the Jerusalem temple was known to be functioning at this time.

(7) Archaeological surveys of Jerusalem show a significant reduction in the city's size during the Persian period compared to the First Temple period — consistent with the biblical description of a modest, struggling community (Haggai 1:6, Ezra 3:12).

(8) Coins minted in Judea during the Persian period (yehud coins) bear Jewish symbols and sometimes the name 'Yehud' — evidence of Jewish self-administration under Persian oversight.

Historical context:

(9) The Persian imperial policy of supporting local temples (documented across the empire) is consistent with the biblical account of Persian kings supporting the Jerusalem temple's reconstruction (Cyrus, Darius, Artaxerxes).

(10) The modest scale of the Second Temple, as described in Ezra 3:12 ('many of the older priests and Levites and family heads, who had seen the former temple, wept aloud') and Haggai 2:3 ('Who of you is left who saw this house in its former glory? How does it look to you now? Does it not seem to you like nothing?'), matches the archaeological picture of a smaller, poorer Persian-period Jerusalem.
description.zh-Hans:
巴比伦流亡之后，犹太人在所罗巴伯（大卫的后裔）和大祭司约书亚的领导下返回耶路撒冷重建圣殿，如以斯拉记3-6章、哈该书1-2章和撒迦利亚书1-8章所记载。第二圣殿约于公元前516年完工，一直存续到约公元前20年希律的改建/重建。

圣经记载：（1）以斯拉记1:1-4记录了居鲁士大帝的诏令（公元前538年），允许犹太人返回并重建圣殿——得到居鲁士圆柱的确认。

（2）以斯拉记3:8-13描述了圣殿根基的奠定，曾见过第一圣殿的人反应不一。

（3）哈该书1-2章约在公元前520年预言，催促百姓完成圣殿建造。

（4）撒迦利亚书4:6-10预言所罗巴伯将完成圣殿。

考古证据：（5）波斯时期犹大印章印痕（yehud印章）在耶路撒冷和犹大全地的发掘中被发现，年代为公元前5-4世纪。这些行政印章——印在罐柄上，刻有亚兰文字母YHD（Yehud，波斯犹大省）——确认了在波斯行政体制下运作的犹太社区。

（6）在埃及发现的象岛古卷（1893-1907年）包含来自象岛（阿斯旺）犹太军事殖民地的信件，年代为公元前5世纪后期。一封公元前407年的信件（AP 30）请求重建当地圣殿，其中提到「耶路撒冷的雅威[YHW]之殿」——证明当时耶路撒冷圣殿已知正在运作。

（7）耶路撒冷的考古调查表明，波斯时期城市规模比第一圣殿时期显著缩小——与圣经描述的规模不大、艰难挣扎的社区一致（哈该书1:6，以斯拉记3:12）。

（8）波斯时期在犹大铸造的硬币（yehud硬币）带有犹太符号，有时刻有「犹大」之名——表明波斯监管下的犹太自治证据。

历史背景：（9）波斯帝国支持当地圣殿的帝国政策（在整个帝国有记录）与圣经记载中波斯诸王支持耶路撒冷圣殿重建（居鲁士、大流士、亚达薛西）一致。

（10）第二圣殿的朴素规模，如以斯拉记3:12（「许多见过前殿的祭司、利未人和族长大声哭号」）和哈该书2:3（「你们中间存留的，有谁见过这殿从前的荣耀呢？现在你们看着如何？岂不在你们眼中看如无有吗？」）所描述的，与较小、较贫穷的波斯时期耶路撒冷的考古图景吻合。

title.en: Stoning of Stephen — Archaeological and Traditional Evidence
title.zh-Hans: 司提反殉道——考古与传统证据
title.zh-Hant: 司提反殉道——考古与传统证据

summary.en: The stoning of Stephen (Acts 7:54-8:1), Christianity's first recorded martyrdom, is associated with the area north of the Damascus Gate in Jerusalem. The 5th-century Basilica of St. Stephen, built by Empress Eudocia (AD 439), and the nearby traditional site preserved by continuous Christian tradition, align with the biblical description of Stephen being taken 'out of the city' for execution.
summary.zh-Hans: 司提反被石头打死（使徒行传7:54-8:1）是基督教第一个有记录的殉道事件，与耶路撒冷大马士革门以北的区域相关。由皇后尤多西亚于公元439年建造的5世纪圣司提反教堂，以及附近由持续基督教传统保存的传统地点，与圣经描述的司提反被带到「城外」处决吻合。
summary.zh-Hant: 司提反被石头打死（使徒行传7:54-8:1）是基督教第一个有记录的殉道事件，与耶路撒冷大马士革门以北的区域相关。由皇后尤多西亚于公元439年建造的5世纪圣司提反教堂，以及附近由持续基督教传统保存的传统地点，与圣经描述的司提反被带到「城外」处决吻合。

description.en:
Acts 7:54-8:1 records the stoning of Stephen, the first Christian martyr. After delivering a powerful speech before the Sanhedrin, Stephen was dragged out of Jerusalem and stoned to death, with Saul (later Paul) watching over the garments of the witnesses.

The location:

(1) Acts 7:58 states Stephen was taken 'out of the city' — stoning was performed outside the city walls, in accordance with both Jewish law (Leviticus 24:14, Numbers 15:35) and Roman practice.

(2) Early Christian tradition, dating to at least the 4th century, identifies the site of Stephen's martyrdom as being north of the Damascus Gate, along the road to Nablus (Shechem).

(3) In AD 439, Empress Eudocia built the Basilica of St. Stephen (Saint-Étienne) at this location, incorporating the traditional site of the stoning. The church was one of the largest in Jerusalem and became a major pilgrimage site.

(4) The Dominican Fathers rebuilt the church in 1900 on the same site, and it houses the École Biblique et Archéologique Française — one of the world's leading biblical archaeology institutes.

Archaeological evidence:

(5) Excavations near the Damascus Gate have revealed the road system and open areas that would have been used for executions in the 1st century, consistent with the biblical account.

(6) The general area north of the Damascus Gate contained rock quarries and open spaces suitable for the kind of execution described in Acts.

Historical context:

(7) Stoning was a recognized form of execution for blasphemy under Jewish law (Leviticus 24:10-16, Mishnah Sanhedrin 6:1-6). The procedure described in Acts — witnesses casting the first stones, removal 'outside the camp/city' — follows established Jewish legal procedure.

(8) The involvement of Saul (Paul) as a witness is significant, as Paul himself later references his participation in Stephen's death (Acts 22:20), providing a double attestation within the New Testament.

(9) The rapid spread of Christianity after Stephen's martyrdom (Acts 8:4 — 'those who had been scattered preached the word wherever they went') is a historically attested pattern of persecution leading to religious spread.
description.zh-Hans:
使徒行传7:54-8:1记录了司提反被石头打死——第一位基督教殉道者。司提反在公会前发表有力的演说后，被拖出耶路撒冷城外用石头打死，扫罗（后来的保罗）在一旁看守见证人的衣服。

地点：（1）使徒行传7:58记载司提反被带到「城外」——用石头打死在城墙外执行，符合犹太律法（利未记24:14、民数记15:35）和罗马惯例。

（2）可追溯至至少4世纪的早期基督教传统，认定司提反殉道地点在大马士革门以北，沿通往纳布卢斯（示剑）的道路。

（3）公元439年，皇后尤多西亚在此地点建造了圣司提反教堂（圣艾蒂安），将传统的用石头打死地点纳入其中。该教堂曾是耶路撒冷最大的教堂之一，成为重要的朝圣目的地。

（4）道明会神父于1900年在同一地点重建了教堂，现设有圣经与考古法国学院——世界领先的圣经考古研究所之一。

考古证据：（5）大马士革门附近的发掘揭示了1世纪用于处决的道路系统和空旷区域，与圣经记载一致。

（6）大马士革门以北的广大区域包含岩石采石场和适合使徒行传中所描述处决的空地。

历史背景：（7）在犹太律法下，用石头打死是亵渎罪的公认处决方式（利未记24:10-16，密西拿公会6:1-6）。使徒行传描述的程序——见证人先扔石头，「带出营外/城外」——遵循了既定的犹太法律程序。

（8）扫罗（保罗）作为见证人参与此事具有意义，因为保罗后来自己提到参与了司提反之死（使徒行传22:20），在新约内提供了双重印证。

（9）司提反殉道后基督教的迅速传播（使徒行传8:4——「那些分散的人往各处去传道」）是一个有历史记载的迫害导致宗教传播的模式。

title.en: Peter Raises Tabitha at Joppa — Archaeological Evidence for the Setting
title.zh-Hans: 彼得在约帕使大比大复活——场景的考古证据
title.zh-Hant: 彼得在约帕使大比大复活——场景的考古证据

summary.en: Acts 9:36-43 records Peter raising Tabitha (Dorcas) from the dead at Joppa. Archaeological excavations at Jaffa (ancient Joppa) — including Kaplan's work (1955-1974) and the Tel Aviv University project (2007-present) — have uncovered the Hellenistic and Roman-period city, confirming Joppa as a functioning port city with a substantial community during Peter's time.
summary.zh-Hans: 使徒行传9:36-43记载彼得在约帕使大比大（多加）从死里复活。在雅法（古约帕）的考古发掘——包括卡普兰的工作（1955-1974）和特拉维夫大学项目（2007至今）——揭示了希腊化和罗马时期的城市，确认约帕在彼得时期是一个功能完善的港口城市，拥有相当规模的社区。

description.en:
Acts 9:36-43 describes how Tabitha (also called Dorcas), a disciple in Joppa known for good works and charity, became ill and died. The believers sent for Peter, who was nearby in Lydda. Peter went to Joppa, was taken to the upper room where Tabitha's body lay, and after sending everyone out, said 'Tabitha, get up' — and she opened her eyes and sat up.

Archaeological context:

(1) Joppa (Jaffa/Yafo): One of the oldest ports in the world, located on the Mediterranean coast about 55 km northwest of Jerusalem. Excavations confirm continuous occupation through the Hellenistic and Roman periods.

(2) Jacob Kaplan's excavations (1955-1974): Uncovered substantial remains from the Persian, Hellenistic, and Roman periods, including fortifications, dwellings, and a wealthy residential quarter consistent with a community that could support charitable individuals like Tabitha.

(3) Tel Aviv University excavations (2007-present): Directed by Martin Peilstöcker and Aaron Burke. Found additional evidence of the Roman-period city, including the harbor facilities, domestic architecture, and imported goods indicating trade connections — consistent with Acts' description of Joppa as an active port.

(4) Acts 10:5-6 places Simon the tanner's house 'by the sea' in Joppa — a topographically accurate detail consistent with the known layout of ancient Joppa.

(5) The distance from Lydda (where Peter was) to Joppa is about 18 km — consistent with the urgent but manageable journey described in Acts 9:38.
description.zh-Hans:
使徒行传9:36-43描述门徒大比大（又名多加）在约帕因患病而死。信徒们差人去附近的吕大请彼得。彼得前往约帕，被带到停放大比大遗体的楼上房间，在叫所有人出去后说「大比大，起来」——她睁开眼睛坐了起来。

考古背景：（1）约帕（雅法/Yafo）：世界上最古老的港口之一，位于地中海沿岸，耶路撒冷西北约55公里。发掘确认从波斯、希腊化到罗马时期的连续居住。（2）雅各布·卡普兰的发掘（1955-1974）：发现了波斯、希腊化和罗马时期的大量遗存，包括防御工事、住宅和一个富裕的住宅区，与一个能支持像大比大这样的慈善人士的社区一致。（3）特拉维夫大学发掘（2007至今）：由马丁·佩尔斯托克和阿龙·伯克指导。发现了罗马时期城市的更多证据，包括港口设施、家庭建筑和表明贸易联系的进口货物——与使徒行传描述的约帕作为活跃港口一致。（4）使徒行传10:5-6将西门制革匠的房子定在约帕「海边」——地形学上准确的细节，与古代约帕已知布局一致。（5）吕大（彼得所在地）到约帕的距离约18公里——与使徒行传9:38描述的紧急但可行的旅程一致。

title.en: Herod Agrippa I's Death — Acts 12 Confirmed by Josephus
title.zh-Hans: 希律亚基帕一世之死——使徒行传12章获约瑟夫证实
title.zh-Hant: 希律亚基帕一世之死——使徒行传12章获约瑟夫证实

summary.en: Acts 12:19-23 records Herod Agrippa I being struck by an angel and dying after accepting crowd acclamation as a god. Josephus (Antiquities 19.343-350) independently describes the same event — Agrippa's death in Caesarea after appearing in a silver robe and being hailed as a god — providing remarkable extrabiblical confirmation.
summary.zh-Hans: 使徒行传12:19-23记载希律亚基帕一世在群众称他为神后被天使击打而死。约瑟夫（《犹太古史》19.343-350）独立描述了同一事件——亚基帕穿着银袍在凯撒利亚出现后被尊为神后死亡——提供了非凡的圣经以外印证。
summary.zh-Hant: 使徒行传12:19-23记载希律亚基帕一世在群众称他为神后被天使击打而死。约瑟夫（《犹太古史》19.343-350）独立描述了同一事件——亚基帕穿着银袍在凯撒利亚出现后被尊为神后死亡——提供了非凡的圣经以外印证。

description.en:
Acts 12:19-23 states: 'Herod, wearing his royal robes, sat on his throne and delivered a public address. The people shouted, 'This is the voice of a god, not of a man!' Immediately, because Herod did not give praise to God, an angel of the Lord struck him down, and he was eaten by worms and died.'

Josephus (Antiquities 19.343-350) independently records Agrippa's death in Caesarea during a festival honoring Caesar. Agrippa appeared at dawn in a garment woven entirely of silver, which gleamed brilliantly in the sunlight. The crowd cried out that he was a god. Josephus writes that Agrippa 'did not rebuke them nor did he reject their flattery.' He then saw an owl (an omen of his coming death) and was seized by severe abdominal pain, dying five days later.

Convergences between Acts and Josephus:

(1) Location: Both place the event in Caesarea.

(2) Royal apparel: Both mention Agrippa's spectacular royal garment.

(3) Divine acclamation: Both record the crowd hailing him as a god.

(4) Agrippa's failure to reject the acclamation.

(5) Sudden, painful death following the event.

Caesarea Maritima excavations have revealed the theater where this event likely occurred, including the VIP seating area and the palace complex.
description.zh-Hans:
使徒行传12:19-23记载：「希律穿上朝服，坐在位上，对他们讲论。百姓喊着说：这是神的声音，不是人的声音。希律不归荣耀给神，所以主的使者立刻罚他；他被虫咬，气绝了。」

约瑟夫（《犹太古史》19.343-350）独立记载了亚基帕在凯撒利亚一次庆祝凯撒的节日期间的死亡。亚基帕黎明时穿着全银线织成的衣袍出现，在阳光下闪耀夺目。群众高呼他是神。约瑟夫写道亚基帕「没有责备他们，也没有拒绝他们的奉承」。随后他看到一只猫头鹰（他即将死亡的预兆），被剧烈腹痛攫住，五天后死亡。

使徒行传与约瑟夫的汇合：（1）地点：两者都指明凯撒利亚。（2）王室服饰：两者都提到亚基帕华丽的王室衣袍。（3）神圣欢呼：两者都记载群众称他为神。（4）亚基帕未拒绝欢呼。（5）随后的突然、痛苦死亡。

凯撒利亚海滨的发掘揭示了此事件可能发生的剧场，包括贵宾席和宫殿建筑群。

scripturalCorrelation.en: Acts 12:19-23 and Josephus (Antiquities 19.343-350) independently record the same event with remarkable overlap: Agrippa's royal appearance, divine acclamation, failure to rebuke the crowd, and sudden painful death. The Caesarea theater where this occurred has been excavated. This convergence of biblical and secular history provides strong confirmation of Acts' historical reliability.

title.en: Ephesus Artemis Temple — Acts 19 Burning of Magic Books
title.zh-Hans: 以弗所亚底米神庙——使徒行传19章焚烧邪术书籍
title.zh-Hant: 以弗所亚底米神庙——使徒行传19章焚烧邪术书籍

summary.en: Acts 19:23-41 records a riot in Ephesus instigated by silversmiths who made Artemis shrines, protesting that Paul's preaching threatened the goddess's cult. The Temple of Artemis at Ephesus — one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World — has been extensively excavated, confirming the city's devotion to Artemis described in Acts.
summary.zh-Hans: 使徒行传19:23-41记载了以弗所因银匠底米丢煽动而爆发的骚乱，银匠们制造亚底米神龛，抗议保罗的讲道威胁了女神的崇拜。以弗所的亚底米神庙——古代世界七大奇迹之一——已被大规模发掘，证实了使徒行传中描述的以弗所对亚底米的虔诚。
summary.zh-Hant: 使徒行传19:23-41记载了以弗所因银匠底米丢煽动而爆发的骚乱，银匠们制造亚底米神龛，抗议保罗的讲道威胁了女神的崇拜。以弗所的亚底米神庙——古代世界七大奇迹之一——已被大规模发掘，证实了使徒行传中描述的以弗所对亚底米的虔诚。

description.en:
Acts 19:23-41 describes how Paul's ministry in Ephesus (c. 53-56 CE) provoked a massive riot. Demetrius the silversmith rallied craftsmen saying: 'Paul has persuaded and led astray large numbers of people, saying that gods made by human hands are no gods at all.' The crowd seized Paul's companions and shouted 'Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!' for two hours.

Archaeological evidence:

(1) The Temple of Artemis (Artemision): One of the Seven Wonders, measuring approximately 115 x 55 meters with 127 columns 18 meters high. Excavated by J.T. Wood (1869-1874) and the Austrian Archaeological Institute (1965-present). The temple's massive scale confirms the economic stakes Demetrius described.

(2) Silver shrines of Artemis: Multiple small silver and terracotta shrines depicting Artemis have been found in Ephesus, confirming Demetrius's trade in 'silver shrines of Artemis' (Acts 19:24).

(3) The Ephesus theater: The venue where the riot gathered (Acts 19:29) is a massive structure seating 25,000 people — one of the largest in the ancient world. It has been fully excavated and is visible today.

(4) Inscriptions: Numerous inscriptions throughout Ephesus attest to Artemis worship, including 'Artemis of the Ephesians' — the exact phrase used in Acts 19:28, 34.

(5) Acts 19:19 records that many who practiced magic brought their books and burned them publicly — an event consistent with the large volume of magical papyri discovered in Egypt and the Ephesus region.
description.zh-Hans:
使徒行传19:23-41描述了保罗在以弗所的事工（约公元53-56年）引发的大规模骚乱。银匠底米丢召集工匠说：「保罗引诱迷惑许多人，说人手所做的不是神。」群众抓住保罗的同伴，高喊「以弗所人的亚底米大啊」长达两小时。

考古证据：（1）亚底米神庙（阿尔忒弥斯神殿）：古代七大奇迹之一，长约115米、宽55米，有127根18米高的柱子。由伍德（1869-1874）和奥地利考古研究所（1965至今）发掘。（2）亚底米银龛：在以弗所发现多件描绘亚底米的银质和陶制小神龛，证实底米丢「制造银龛」的生意（徒19:24）。（3）以弗所剧场：骚乱发生的场所（徒19:29），可容纳25,000人，是古代世界最大的剧场之一，已完全发掘。（4）铭文：以弗所各地发现的铭文证实亚底米崇拜，包括「以弗所人的亚底米」——正是徒19:28、34中使用的词句。（5）徒19:19记载许多行邪术的人把书拿来当众焚烧——这与在埃及和以弗所地区发现的大量巫术纸草文献相吻合。

scripturalCorrelation.en: Acts 19:23-41 provides historically precise details: the silversmiths' guild, the Artemis temple economy, the massive theater, the chant 'Great is Artemis of the Ephesians,' and the city clerk's reference to the proconsuls. All have been confirmed by Ephesus excavations, making this one of the most archaeologically verified passages in Acts.

title.en: Flight to Egypt — Coptic Traditions and Archaeological Sites
title.zh-Hans: 逃往埃及——科普特传统和考古遗址
title.zh-Hant: 逃往埃及——科普特传统和考古遗址

summary.en: Matthew 2:13-15 records Joseph, Mary, and Jesus fleeing to Egypt to escape Herod's massacre. Coptic Christian traditions, attested from the 3rd century, preserve specific sites along the Holy Family's route through Egypt — including Cairo (Matariyya), Asyut, and Wadi Natrun — with early churches marking each location.
summary.zh-Hans: 马太福音2:13-15记载约瑟、马利亚和耶稣逃往埃及躲避希律的屠杀。科普特基督教传统从3世纪起就保存了圣家在埃及行程中的具体地点——包括开罗（马塔里亚）、艾斯尤特和瓦迪纳特伦——每个地点都有早期教堂标记。

description.en:
Matthew 2:13-15 records an angel warning Joseph: 'Get up, take the child and his mother and escape to Egypt.' The Coptic Church of Egypt preserves the most detailed tradition of the Holy Family's journey, with sites attested from at least the 3rd century.

Key traditional sites:

(1) Cairo/Matariyya: The Church of the Virgin at Matariyya marks the traditional resting place where the Holy Family sheltered under a tree. A spring (the 'Holy Family Well') is venerated at this site.

(2) Abu Serga Church (Old Cairo): Built in the 4th century over a cave where the Holy Family allegedly stayed, making it one of the oldest Christian sites in Egypt.

(3) Asyut (Deir el-Muharraq): The Monastery of the Virgin Mary at Deir el-Muharraq tradition holds the family stayed here over six months. The monastery has been continuously occupied since the 4th century.

(4) Wadi Natrun: Four major monasteries preserve traditions of the Holy Family's passage through this desert valley.

Historical plausibility: Egypt had a substantial Jewish population in the 1st century BCE/CE (estimated at one million), particularly in Alexandria and the Fayum. Jewish communities in Egyptian towns could have provided refuge for a fleeing Jewish family, making Matthew's account historically plausible.
description.zh-Hans:
马太福音2:13-15记载天使警告约瑟：「起来，带着小孩子和他母亲逃往埃及。」埃及科普特教会保存了最详细的圣家旅程传统，相关遗址可追溯至至少3世纪。

主要传统遗址：（1）开罗/马塔里亚：马塔里亚的童贞女教堂标记了圣家在一棵树下休息的传统地点。一处泉水（「圣家井」）在此受人敬仰。（2）阿布塞尔加教堂（老开罗）：4世纪建于圣家据称停留的洞穴之上，是埃及最古老的基督教遗址之一。（3）艾斯尤特（德尔穆哈拉克）：童贞女马利亚修道院传统认为圣家在此停留六个多月。该修道院自4世纪以来持续有人居住。（4）瓦迪纳特伦：四座主要修道院保存了圣家经过此沙漠谷地的传统。

历史可信性：公元前1世纪至公元1世纪埃及有大量犹太人口（估计约一百万），特别是在亚历山大和法尤姆。埃及各城镇的犹太社区可以为逃亡的犹太家庭提供庇护，使马太的记载在历史上是合理的。

scripturalCorrelation.en: Matthew 2:13-15 describes the flight as fulfilling Hosea 11:1: 'Out of Egypt I called my son.' The Coptic traditions, while not archaeologically verifiable in detail, preserve a continuous memory of the Holy Family's Egyptian sojourn that dates to the earliest centuries of Christianity, consistent with the historical reality of Jewish communities in Ptolemaic-Roman Egypt.

title.en: Widow of Nain's Son Raised — The Galilean Village Confirmed
title.zh-Hans: 拿因城寡妇之子复活——加利利村庄获确认
title.zh-Hant: 拿因城寡妇之子复活——加利利村庄获确认

summary.en: Luke 7:11-17 records Jesus raising a widow's son at Nain (Nein), a small village in Lower Galilee. The village of Nein has been continuously identified since antiquity, located on the northwestern edge of Mount Moreh, with Crusader and Franciscan church traditions marking the miracle site. The geographic details in Luke's account — the town's location near Nazareth and the setting of a funeral procession at the town gate — match the archaeological landscape precisely.
summary.zh-Hans: 路加福音7:11-17记载耶稣在拿因（Nein）使寡妇之子复活。拿因村自古代以来一直被确认位置，位于摩利冈西北坡，有十字军和方济各会教堂传统标记此神迹地点。路加记载的地理细节——村庄靠近拿撒勒的位置和城门口送殡行列的场景——与考古景观精确吻合。
summary.zh-Hant: 路加福音7:11-17记载耶稣在拿因（Nein）使寡妇之子复活。拿因村自古代以来一直被确认位置，位于摩利冈西北坡，有十字军和方济各会教堂传统标记此神迹地点。路加记载的地理细节——村庄靠近拿撒勒的位置和城门口送殡行列的场景——与考古景观精确吻合。

description.en:
Luke 7:11-17 records that Jesus, accompanied by his disciples and a large crowd, approached the town of Nain and encountered a funeral procession coming out of the town gate. A widow's only son had died, and Jesus, moved with compassion, touched the bier and said 'Young man, I say to you, get up!' The dead man sat up and began to speak.

The village of Nain (Nein):

(1) The modern village of Nein (also spelled Nayn) is located on the northwestern slope of the Hill of Moreh (Givat HaMoreh) in Lower Galilee, about 8 km southeast of Nazareth and 6 km south of Mount Tabor.

(2) The village has been continuously identified as the site of the miracle since the earliest Christian pilgrimages. Eusebius (4th century) and Jerome both mention Nain as a village south of Mount Tabor.

(3) The village's small size — both in antiquity and today — matches Luke's description of a close-knit community where 'a large crowd from the town was with her' (the widow), suggesting nearly the entire village participated in the funeral.

Archaeological and traditional evidence:

(4) Crusader-period remains include a church built to commemorate the miracle. The Franciscans (Custodia Terrae Sanctae) have maintained a presence at the site since the late 19th century.

(5) The geography matches Luke's narrative: the approach road from the west (direction from Capernaum and Nazareth) would have led to the town gate area, exactly where a funeral procession would depart toward the burial grounds.

(6) Rock-cut tombs from the Roman period have been found in the hills surrounding the village, confirming the burial practices described in the account.

Historical context:

(7) Luke's detail that the deceased was a widow's 'only son' is particularly poignant in the first-century context, where a widow without a son would have had no means of support. This socioeconomic detail reflects intimate knowledge of Galilean village life.

(8) The miracle's fame spread 'throughout Judea and all the surrounding country' (Luke 7:17), consistent with the village's location on travel routes connecting Galilee with the Jezreel Valley.

(9) The account's historical markers — the specific village name, the geographic setting, the cultural details of first-century Jewish burial practices — are consistent with an eyewitness or close-source report rather than a fabricated story.
description.zh-Hans:
路加福音7:11-17记载耶稣与门徒和一大群人走近拿因城时，遇见从城门出来的送殡队伍。一位寡妇的独子死了，耶稣动了慈心，按住杠说「少年人，我吩咐你，起来！」死者就坐起来并且说话。

拿因村（Nein）：（1）现代村庄 Nein（也拼写为 Nayn）位于下加利利摩利冈（Givat HaMoreh）西北坡，在拿撒勒东南约8公里和他泊山以南约6公里处。

（2）自最早的基督教朝圣以来，该村庄一直被认定为神迹发生地。优西比乌（4世纪）和哲罗姆都提到拿因是他泊山以南的一个村庄。

（3）村庄的规模——无论古代还是现在——与路加描述的紧密社区一致：「城里有极多的人和寡妇同在」，暗示几乎全村人都参与了送殡。

考古和传统证据：（4）十字军时期的遗迹包括一座为纪念此神迹而建的教堂。方济各会（圣地监护处）自19世纪末以来一直在该地保持存在。

（5）地理与路加的叙述吻合：从西方（迦百农和拿撒勒方向）来的道路将通向城门区域，正是送殡队伍前往墓地出发的地方。

（6）在村庄周围的山丘中发现了罗马时期的岩凿坟墓，确认了记载中描述的埋葬习俗。

历史背景：（7）路加提到死者是寡妇的「独子」，在1世纪背景下尤为令人心酸——没有儿子的寡妇将没有任何生活来源。这一社会经济细节反映了对加利利村庄生活的深入了解。

（8）神迹的名声「传遍了犹太和周围地方」（路加福音7:17），与该村庄位于连接加利利与耶斯列谷的交通路线上的位置一致。

（9）记载的历史标记——具体的村名、地理环境、1世纪犹太埋葬习俗的文化细节——与目击者或接近来源的报告一致，而非编造的故事。

scripturalCorrelation.en: Luke 7:11-17 describes Jesus raising a widow's only son at the town gate of Nain. The village of Nein on Mount Moreh's northwestern slope has been continuously identified with this site since the 4th century. Archaeological evidence of Roman-period tombs, Crusader church remains, and the geographic layout matching Luke's narrative support the account's authenticity.
